sourceDefinition: , aor. ; (S, M, K;) and A^abala , aor. ; (K;) inf. n. A^abaAlapN , (S, M, K,) of the former verb, (S, M, TA,) or, accord. to Sb, A_ibaAlapN , because it denotes an office, and, if so, of the latter verb, (TA,) and A^abalN , (M, K,) which is of the former verb, (M, TA,) and A^abalapN [like galabapN ]; (T;) He (a man, S) was, or became, skilled in the good management of camels (S, M, K) and of sheep or goats. (M, K.) A_ibaAlapN , like kitaAbapN [in measure], signifies The management, or tending, (A, K, TA,) of maAl [meaning camels or other beasts ]. (A, TA.) You say, huwa Hasanu AlA_ibaAlapi He is good in the management, or tending, of his mAl [or camels, &c. ]. (A, TA.) ― -b2- A^abala , aor. : see 2, second signification. ― -b3- A^ubilati AlA_ibilu The camels were gotten, or acquired, as permanent property. (S, TA.) ― -b4- A^abilati AlA_ibilu , aor. ; and A^abalat , aor. ; (K;) inf. n. [of the former] A^abalN and [of the latter] A^ubuwlN ; (TA;) The camels became many, or numerous. (K.) ― -b5- Also A^ubalati AlA_ibilu , (S, M, K,) and the like is said of wild animals, (S, M,) or others, (K,) aor. and , inf. n. A^ubuwlN (S, M, K) and A^abolN ; (M, K;) and A^abilat ; and ↓ tA^bl~t ; (M, K;) The camels were content, or satisfied, with green pasture, so as to be in no need of water: (S, M, K:) the last verb is mentioned by Z, and he says that it is tropical, and hence A^abiylN applied to “a monk.“ (TA.) ― -b6- [Hence,] A^abala Alr~ajulu Eani A@moraA^atihi , and ↓ tA^b~l , (S, M, K,) The man was content to abstain from conjugal intercourse with his wife; syn. AijotazaA^aEanohaA ; (M;) the man abstained from conjugal, or carnal, intercourse with his wife. (S, K, TA.) ― -b7- [Hence also] A^abala , (K,) inf. n. A^abolN , (TA,) (tropical:) He devoted himself to religious exercises; or became a devotee; (K, TA;) as also A^abula , like faquha , inf. n. A^abaAlapN : or this signifies he became a monk. (TA.) ― -b8- And A^abala , aor. , (Kr, M, K,) inf. n. A^ubuwlN , The camels remained, or abode, in the place: (M, K:) or remained, or abode, long in the pasturage, and in the place. (El-Moheet, TA.) ― -b12- A^abala AlEu$obN , inf. n. A^ubuwlN , The herbage became tall, so that the camels were able to feed upon it. (K.) ― -b13- A^abala Al$~ajaru , inf. n. A^ubuwlN , The trees had green [ such, app., as is termed A^ubulN ] growing in its dried parts, mixing therewith, upon which camels, or the like, fatten. (Ibn- 'Abbád.) -A2- A^abalahu , inf. n. A^abolN , He assigned to him, or gave him, ( jaEala lahu ) pasturing camels, or camels pasturing by themselves. (K.)

sourceDefinition: (T, S, M, Msb, K, &c.,) said by Sb to be the only subst. of this form except HibirN , and to have none like it among epithets except bilizN ; for though other instances are mentioned, they are not of established authority; (Msb;) but IJ mentions, with these, HibikN and A_iTilN [which may be of established authority]; (TA;) [and to these may be added A_ibiTN and A_ibidN , and perhaps nikiHN and xiTibN ; respecting which see A_ibidN ;] and for A_ibilN one says also ↓ A_iblN , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) sometimes, by way of contraction; (S, Msb;) or this may be a dial. var. of the former; (Kr, MF;) [ Camels: and a herd of camels: or] at the least, applied to a Siromap ; i. e. a number [ of camels ] more than a *awod [ which is at least nine, ] up to thirty; after which is the hajomap , i. e. forty and upwards; and then, hunayodapu , which is a hundred of A_ibil : (T:) or, accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, a hundred of A_ibil : (TA:) it is a quasi-pl. n.; (Az, S, ISd, Z, O, Msb, &c.;) a word having no proper sing.; (S, M, O, Msb;) and is of the fem. gender, because the quasi-pl. n. that has no proper sing. is necessarily fem. (S, O, Msb) when not applied to human beings, (S, O,) or when applied to irrational beings, (Msb,) and has p added in the dim.; (S, Msb;) the dim. of A_ibilN being ↓ A^ubayolapN : (S, Msb, K:) it is said in the K that it is a sing. applied to a pl. number, and is not a pl., nor a quasi-pl. n.; but in this assertion together with the saying that the dim. is as above is a kind of contradiction; for if it be a sing., and not a quasi-pl. n., what is the reason of its being fem.? (TA:) the pl. is A=baAlN (S, M, Msb, K) and A^abiylN [like EabiydN pl. of EabodN , q. v.]; (Msb, TA;) the pl. meaning herds [ of camels ]; and in like manner A^agonaAmN and A^aboqaArN mean flocks of sheep or goats and herds of bulls or cows: (Msb, TA:) and the dual, A_iblaAni , means two herds [ of camels ], (Sb, T, S, M, Msb,) each with its pastor; (T;) like as ganamaAni means two flocks of sheep or goats: (S:) or, accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, the dual means two hundreds of A_ibil . (TA.) ― -b2- AlA_ibilu AlS~ugoraY [ The smaller camels ] is an appellation applied to sheep; because they eat more than goats. (IAar in TA art. DbT .) ― -b3- It is said in the Kur [lxxxviii. 17], A^afalaA yanoZuruwna A_ilaY A@loA_ibili kayofa xuliqato , meaning, accord. to 'Aboo-Amr Ibn-El- 'Alà, (T, TA,) (tropical:) [ Will they not then consider ] the clouds that bear the water for rain, [how they are created? ] (T, K, TA:) but accord. to him who reads AlA_iboli , the meaning is, the camels. (T, TA.)

(TA:) the pl. is A=baAlN (S, M, Msb, K) and A^abiylN [like EabiydN pl. of EabodN , q. v.]; (Msb, TA;) the pl. meaning herds [ of camels ]; and in like manner A^agonaAmN and A^aboqaArN mean flocks of sheep or goats and herds of bulls or cows: (Msb, TA:) and the dual, A_iblaAni , means two herds [ of camels ], (Sb, T, S, M, Msb,) each with its pastor; (T;) like as ganamaAni means two flocks of sheep or goats: (S:) or, accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, the dual means two hundreds of A_ibil . (TA.) ― -b2- AlA_ibilu AlS~ugoraY [ The smaller camels ] is an appellation applied to sheep; because they eat more than goats. (IAar in TA art. DbT .) ― -b3- It is said in the Kur [lxxxviii. 17], A^afalaA yanoZuruwna A_ilaY A@loA_ibili kayofa xuliqato , meaning, accord. to 'Aboo-Amr Ibn-El- 'Alà, (T, TA,) (tropical:) [ Will they not then consider ] the clouds that bear the water for rain, [how they are created? ] (T, K, TA:) but accord. to him who reads AlA_iboli , the meaning is, the camels. (T, TA.)

definition: Unwholesomeness and heaviness of food;
sourceDefinition: Unwholesomeness and heaviness of food; (S, M, K;) originally wabalapN , like as A^aHadN is originally waHadN ; (S;) as also ↓ A^abalN . (K.) It is said in a trad. that this departs from every property for which the poor-rate has been paid. (S, M.) ― -b2- See also A^ubolapN . ― -b3- An evil quality of herbage or pasture. (AHn, TA in art. n$r .) ― -b4- A cause of harm or injury; evil; mischief. (TA.) ― -b5- A consequence of an action, or a claim which one seeks to obtain for an injury; and a cause of blame or dispraise: having these meanings in the saying, A_ino faEalota *aAka faqado xarajota mino A^abalatihi [ If thou do that, thou wilt escape from its consequence, &c.]. (T.) ― -b6- A fault, vice, or the like. (Aboo-Málik, T.) So in the saying, maA Ealayoka fiY h`*aA AlA^amori A^abalapN [ There is not to be charged against thee, in this affair, any fault, &c.]. (T.) ― -b7- A crime; a sin; an unlawful action. (K.) ― -b8- Rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite. (IB.)

definition: (assumed tropical:) A Christian monk;
sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) A Christian monk; (S M, Msb, K;) so called because of his abstaining ( litaA^abulihi ) from women: (TA:) or the chief monk: (T:) or a derotee: (TA:) or an old man, or elder: (M:) or the chief, or head-man, of the Christians: (M, K:) or the man who calls them to prayer by means of the naAquws ; (A Heyth, M, * K;) the beater of the nAqws : (IDrd:) as also ↓ A^ayobaliY~N , (M and K, but according to the M as meaning “ a monk, ”) which is either a foreign word, or changed by the relative Y , or of the same class as A_inoqaHolN [in which the first letter as well as th second is augmentative], for Sb says that there is not in the language an instance of the measure fayoEalN ; (M;) and ↓ A^ayobuliY~N , and hayobaliY~N , and ↓ A^abuliY~N and ↓ A^ayobalN , (K,) which last is disallowed by Sb for the reason stated above; (TA;) and ↓ A^ayobulN like A^ayonuqN ; and ↓ A^ayobiliY~N ; (K;) the last with fet-h to the hemzeh, and kesr to the b , and with the [first] Y quiescent; or A^ayobaliY~N [app. a mistranscription for A^ayobiliY~N ] is used by poetic licence for ↓ A^abiyliY~N , like A^ayonuqN for A^anowuqN : (TA:) pl. A=baAlN (M, K) and A^ubolN , or A^ubulN , [accord. to different copies of the K,] with damm [which indicates that the former is meant, though it is irregular]. (K.) By A^abiylN AlA^abiyliyna is meant 'Eesà [or Jesus ], (S, K,) the Messiah. (S.) ― -b2- In the Syriac language it signifies Mourning, or sorrowing. (K.) -A2- Also A staff, or stick. (M, K.) ― -b2- See also A_ibaAlapN .

definition: , (T, S, M, Msb, K,) like Eij~awolN , (S, Msb, K, [in the CK, erroneously, Eajuwl ,]) A separate, or distinct, portion of a number of birds, and of horses, and of camels, (M, K,) and of such following one another;
sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, Msb, K,) like Eij~awolN , (S, Msb, K, [in the CK, erroneously, Eajuwl ,]) A separate, or distinct, portion of a number of birds, and of horses, and of camels, (M, K,) and of such following one another; (K;) as also ↓ A_ibiylN and ↓ A_ib~aAlapN , (M, K,) and ↓ A_ibaAlapN , and ↓ A_iyobaAlN : (K:) or it signifies a bird separating itself from the row of other birds; (T, TA;) accord. to IAar. (TA.) It is said to be the sing. of ↓ A^abaAbiylN : (T, S, M, and Jel in cv. 3:) Ks says, I used to hear the grammarians say that this latter has for its sing. A_ib~awolN , like Eij~awolN , of which the pl. is EajaAjiylN : (Msb:) or its sing. is ↓ A_ibaylN ; (S, Msb;) but he who says this adds, I have not found the Arabs to know a sing. to it: (S:) or each of these is its sing.; (M, Jel;) and so is ↓ A_ib~aAlN : (Jel:) or its sing. is ↓ A_ib~aAlapN , (Bd in cv. 3, and Msb,) originally signifying “a great bundle:” (Bd:) it is said that this seems to be its sing.; and so ↓ A^ab~aAlapN : or the sing. may be ↓ A_iybaAlapN , like as diynaArN is sing of danaAniyrN : (T:) or it has no sing., (T, S, M, Bd, Msb, K,) accord. to Fr (T, Msb) and Akh (S) and AO, (T, M,) like $amaATiyTu (Fr, T, Bd) and EabaAdiydN . (AO, M, Bd.) A^abaAbiylN signifies, accord. to some, A company in a state of dispersion: (M:) or dispersed companies, one following another: (Msb:) or distinct, or separate, companies, (Akh, S, Msb, K,) like leaning camels: (Msb:) or companies in a state of dispersion. (AO, Msb.) One says, jaA='ato A_ibiluka A^abaAbiyla Thy camels came in distinct, or separate, companies. (Akh, S.) And TayorN A^abaAbiylu [in the Kur cv. 3 means Birds in distinct, or separate, flocks or bevies ]: (Akh, S:) [or] birds in companies from this and that quarter: or following one another, flock after flock: (Zj, T:) or (assumed tropical:) birds in companies; (Bd, Jel;) likened to great bundles, in respect of their compactness. (Bd.) [Respecting these birds, Fei, in the Msb, quotes many fanciful descriptions, which I omit, as absurd.]

sourceDefinition: [ A blight, blast, taint, canker, disease, bane, pest, plague, or the like; any evil affection; an evil; a cause of mischief or harm or injury; anything that is noxious or destructive; a calamity;] i. q. EaAhapN ; (S, Msb, K;) i. e. (Msb, [in the K “ or, ”]) an accident that mars, or corrupts, that which it affects, or befalls, or smites: (T, M, O, Msb, K:) pl. A=faAtN . (Msb, K.) [See 1.] One says, A=fahu AlZ~arofi AlS~alafu wa A=fapu AlEilomi Aln~isEyaAnu [ The bane of elegance in manners, or the like, is the overpassing the due limits therein, and arrogating to oneself superiority therein, through pride; and the bane of science is forgetfulness ]. (T.) And it is said in a trad., A=fapu AlHadiyvi Alka*ibu wa A=fapu AlEilomi Aln~isoyaAnu [ The bane of discourse is lying; and the bane of science is forgetfulness ]. (TA.) And hence the saying, likul~i $aYo'K A=fapN wa liloEilom A=faAtN [ To everything there is a bane; and to science there are banes ]. (TA.)

definition: (S, M, K, &c.) and A^ay~aA , (M, K,) the latter form used by some, as related on the authority of Ktr; (M;) accord. to some, (M,) a noun of vague signification, (S, M, K,) used metonymically for a...
sourceDefinition: (S, M, K, &c.) and A^ay~aA , (M, K,) the latter form used by some, as related on the authority of Ktr; (M;) accord. to some, (M,) a noun of vague signification, (S, M, K,) used metonymically for a noun in the accus. case, (M,) with which are connected all the affixed pronouns that denote the accus. case: you say A_iy~aAnA [ Thee ] and A_iy~aAhu [ him ] and A_iy~aAYa [ me ] (S, K) and A_iy~aAnaA [ us, &c.]: (S:) and the hemzeh is changed into w , so that you say wiy~aAka (S, M, K *) and way~aAka ; (Ktr, IJ, M, K; *) and sometimes into w , so that you say wiy~aAka [and app. way~aAka also; both of which are used by some of the Arabs in the present day, very commonly in Egypt, for waA_iy~aAka as meaning maEaka ; like as one says wazayodFA , meaning maEa zayodK ]: (K:) the k and h and Y [&c.] are put to show the object meant, in order that the person addressed may be known from the absent [&c.]; and have no place in the analysis of a sentence, like the k in *`lika and A^araA^ayotaka : (S, M: in the former of which is added, and like the A and n in A^anota :) and this is identical with the opinion of Akh: (M, TA:) thus Ay~A is the noun, and what follows it is to denote allocution, [&c.,] and the two become as one thing; for nouns of vague signification are not prefixed to other nouns to govern them in the gen. case, nor are any of the pronouns, being themselves determinate. (S.) Ibn-Keysán says, (S, M,) some of the grammarians say that A_iy~aAka , altogether, is a noun; and he adds, but some say (M) that the k and h &c. are the nouns, and that Ay~A is a support thereto, because they cannot stand by themselves, (S, M,) like the k &c. which occupy the latter place in yaDoribuka &c.; so when the k &c. are put first, [as in A_iy~aAka Darabotu Thee I beat, or struck, ] they are supported by AyA , and the whole becomes as one thing: (S:) and you may also say, Darabotu A_iy~aAYa [ I beat, or struck, me ]; because it is not allowable to say, DarabotuniY : (S as corrected by IB:) but you may not say, Darabotu A_iy~aAka [ I beat, or struck, thee ]; because you only require Ay~Ak when you cannot use the k [alone]; though you may say, Darabotuka A_iy~Aka [ I beat, or struck, thee, thee ]; because the k is made to be syntactically dependent upon the verb, so when you repeat it you require Ay~A . (S.) In the saying of the poet, (S,) Dhu-l-Isba' El-'Adwánee, (TA,) kaA^an~aAyawoma qur~aY A_in~amaA naqotulu A_iy~aAnaA [ As though we, on the day of Kurrà, only killed ourselves ], he has separated it from the verb only because the Arabs do not make the action of the agent to fall upon the agent itself by the adjunction of the pronoun: they do not say, qatalotuniY , but only qatalotu nafosiY : so the poet has used Ay~AnA in the same manner as A^anofusanaA . (S, TA.) Some of the grammarians say that A_iy~aA is prefixed to what follows it, governing it in the gen. case; and adduce as an evidence thereof a saying which see below, commencing with A_i*aA balaga Alr~ajulu . (S.) Zj says that it is an explicit noun, [not a pronoun,] which is prefixed to all the pronouns, governing them in the gen. case; but only to pronouns; so that if one said, A_iy~aA zayodK Had~avotu , it would be bad. (M.) Kh holds that it is a pronoun prefixed to the k [&c.], governing it in the gen. case; (M, K;) and the like is related to have been the opinion of El-Mázinee: and Sb relates of Kh that he said, if any one were to say A_iy~aAka nafosaka [ Thee, thyself ], I would not severely blame him, for this k is [virtually] governed in the gen. case. (M.) sourceDefinition: Numerous, luxuriant or tangled or dense, trees: (S, K:) or a place where water collects and sinks into the ground ( gayoDapN ) producing [ trees of the kinds called ] sidor and A^araAk (Lth, K) and similar soft trees: (Lth:) or a collection of any trees; even, of palm-trees: (K:) or, as some say, a place where [ trees of the kind called ] A^avol grow, and where is a collection of them: or, accord. to AHn, an abundant collection of A^araAk in one place: (TA:) or trees; said to be of the [ kind called ] A^araAk : (Msb:) n. un. with p : (S, Msb, K, &c.:) IAar says, [you say,] A^ayokapN A^avolK and rahoTN , and qaSiymapN . (Sh.) A^aSoHaAbu A@loA^ayokapi occurs in the Kur in four chapters: [xv. 78 and xxvi. 176 and xxxviii. 12 and 1.13:] (Sgh:) he who reads thus means, by the latter word, AlgayoDap [explained above, and also signifying the thicket, or collection of tangled trees, &c.]; (S, K;) or the tangled, or luxuriant, or abundant and dense, trees: (TA:) another reading is layokapa ; accord. to which, this is the name of the town [in which the people here mentioned dwelt]: (S, K:) or, as some say, the two words are [applied to the same place,] like bak~apu and mak~apu : (S:) but Zj says that another reading is allowable, and very good; i. e. A^aSoHaAbu layokapi , as being originally AlA^yokapi ; for the Arabs say, AalaHomaru qado jaA='aniY and laHomaru jaA=A_aniY for AlA^aHomaru ; so that layokap is like laHomar . (TA.)

(M.) -A2- A=na , aor. yay^iynu , inf. n. A^ayonN , (S, M, Msb, K, &c., [but see what follows,]) also signifies Its time came; ( A^ataY waqotuhu ;) as also A^anaY : (Bd lvii. 15:) it was, or became, present: it came, or attained, to its time; to its full, or final, time, or state; to maturity: it was, or became, or drew, near: syn. A^anaY : (M:) and A^adoraka ; like A^anaY : (Ham p. 455:) and HaAna : (S, M, Msb, K:) and qaruba . (Mughnee voce A_in~a .) You say, A=na laka A^ano tafoEala ka*aA , aor. and inf. n. as above, (AZ, S,) i. e. HaAna [ The time has come, or has drawn near, for thee to do, or that thou shouldst do, such a thing ]; like A^anaY : and it is formed from it by transposition: (S:) [i. e.] A^anaY is formed by transposition from A=na : (Msb:) or A=na is a dial. var. of A^anaY ; not formed from it by transposition, [nor is the reverse the case,] because of the existence of the inf. n. [of each]: (M:) or A=na is formed by transposition from A^anaY , because the latter has an inf. n. and the former has not: so says As: for A^ayonN does not belong to this; its meaning being only A_iEoyaA='N and taEabN : or, accord. to AZ, A=na has an inf. n., namely A^ayonN ; and if the case be so, the two [verbs] are equal; neither being the original of the other: (IJ in the Khasáïs:) Suh, in the R, asserts that A=na is formed by transposition from A^anaY : (TA:) the assertion of El-Bekree, that A=na is originally with w [for its medial radical letter], and that it is of the class of waliYa , aor. yaliY , requires consideration, and involves what is contrary to rule. (MF.) You say also, A=na A^ayonuka , (S, M, K,) and A_iynuka , (M, K,) and A=nuka , (S, K,) i. e. HaAna Hiynuka [ Thy time, or season, came, or hath come: or drew near, or hath drawn near ]. (S, M, K.)

sourceDefinition: : see A^ayonN . ― -b2- A@loA=na is a noun denoting the present time; (S, M, Msb, K;) [signifying At the present time; now; for] it is an adverbial noun; (S, Msb, K;) one which, in a place where it is fitting to be used as such, may not be used otherwise; occurring in a determinate sense; (S, K;) the Al being inseparable from it; (IJ, M, Msb;) not prefixed to it for the purpose of rendering it determinate, because it has not that which participates in its meaning: (S, Msb, K:) as Ibn-Es-Sarráj says, there is not one A=n and another A=n : (Msb:) [accord. to ISd, who quotes a long disquisition by IJ on this word,] the Al which is expressed in this case is redundant, because the noun is determinate without it, but it is rendered so by another Al , which is understood, as in the case of A^amosi : so says IJ, following Aboo-'Alee; and his is the correct opinion: (M:) Fr says that it is a particle, compounded with Al , which is inseparable from it; and that it is originally A^awaAna [or A@loA^awaAna ]: or that it may have originated from the phrase A=na laka A^ano tafoEala [explained above], and is therefore mansoob, like qiyla and qaAla when used as nouns: but Zj disallows its originating from A=na ; and says that the right opinion is that of Kh, that A@loA=na is indecl. with fet-h for its termination, and that the Al is prefixed because the meaning is h`*aA Alwaqot ; and this is the opinion of Sb. (T.) You say, A^anaA A@loA=na A^afoEalu ka*aA [ I, at the present time, or now, do, or will do, thus, or such a thing ]. (M.) And kunotu A@loA=na Einodahu , meaning I was, in this time, of which part is present and some portions have passed, with him, or in his presence. (IJ, M.) And when you mean the kind of expression which is used in this saying, you say, AaloA=nu Had~u Alz~amaAnayoni [ The term “ now ” is the limit of the two times; namely the past and the future]; thus pronounced, marfooa: so says IJ: but in the Book of Sb we read, AlA=na Had~u Alz~amaAnayoni , with nasb: and in like manner, in the same, AlA=na A=nuka [ Now is thy time ]; the former with nasb and the latter with refa. (M.) You say also, h`*aA A^awaAnu A@loA=na [ This is the present time ]: and maA jiy^otu A_il~aA A^awaAna A@loA=na , meaning I came not save at the present time, or now: with the last word mansoob in both instances. (ISh, T.) [And A_ilaY A@loA=na and Hat~aY A@loA=na To the present time and until the present time; i. e. hitherto. And mina A@loA=na From the present time; henceforward. ] Sometimes the hemzeh [after the l ] is suppressed, and its vowel is transferred to the l ; so that you say AlaAna . (Bd ii. 66.) And sometimes also the l is pronounced with fet-h and both the hemzehs are suppressed; so that you say laAna . (S, K.) And sometimes ta is prefixed to it, like as it is to Hiyna ; so that you say talaAna , like as you say taHiyna . (El-Umawee, A 'Obeyd. [See art. tln .])

sourceDefinition: is an adverbial noun, (Msb,) an interrogative respecting a place: (S, M, Msb, K:) [signifying Where? in what place? ]: Zj says that it is an interrogative particle, like kayofa : (T:) [ISd says,] it is a noun, because you say, mino A^ayona [meaning From what place? whence? ]: (M:) [and you say also, A_ilaY A^ayona To what place? whither? ]: it is always mansoob, unless you prefix the article to it, saying AlA^ayonu [which means The place where ]: (Lth, T:) it is fem.; but may be made masc. (Lh, M.) You say, A^ayona zayodN Where, or in what place, is Zeyd? (S, Msb.) And A^ayona bayotuka [ Where is thy house, or tent? ]. (M.) And A^ayona yu*ohabu bika , which may mean Where, or whither, wilt thou be taken away, and what will be done with thee and made to come to pass with thee, if this be thine intellect? or, accord. to Mtr, it is a saying of the people of Baghdád, addressed to him whom they charge with foolish judgment or opinion, as meaning A^ayona yu*ohabu biEaqolika [ Where, or whither, is thine intellect taken away? ]. (Har p. 574.) [And A^ayona h`*aA mino *aAka and Eano *aAka and wa *aAka What place does this hold in relation to that, or in comparison with that? what is this in relation to that, or in comparison with that? what has this to do with that? what has this in common with that? ] ― -b2- It also denotes a condition: when you say, A^ayona tajoliso A^ajoliso [ Where thou sittest, I will sit ], the sitting must be in one place: and maA is added to it; so that you say, A^ayonamaA taqumo A^aqumo [ Wherever thou standest, I will stand ]. (Msb.) ― -b3- It also occurs used as a proper name of a particular place: thus the poet Homeyd Ibn-Thowr speaks of his companions as being biA^ayona wa A^ayonamaA [app. meaning In certain places: where and wherever those places were, there were my companions]: in which case it is divested of the meaning of an interrogative, and is imperfectly decl. because determinate and of the fem. gender. (M, L. [In one copy of the former, biA^an~aY wa A^ayonamaA , which may mean the same; and voce A^aY~N , q. v., biA^aY~a wa A^ayonamaA .])

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, &c.,) of the measure faE~aAl , or it may be of the measure faEolaAn , (Msb,) also pronounced ↓ A_iy~aAna , (T, S, M, K,) the latter of the dial. of Suleym, mentioned by Fr, (T, S,) and by Zj, (M,) is an interrogative respecting a time, (T, S, Msb,) but only respecting a time not come: (T:) signifying When? (S, M, Msb;) at what time? (Msb, K:) it is fem.; but may be made masc.: (Lh, M:) and it may be pronounced with imáleh, though not belonging to a class of words regularly subject to imáleh. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [xvi. 22 and xxvii. 67], accord. to different readings, A^ay~aAna yuboEavuwna or ↓ A_iy~aAni [ When they shall be raised to life ]; (T, S, M;) i. e. when shall be the resurrection. (Aboo-Is-hák, T.) But you may not say, A^ay~aAna faEalota *aAka as meaning When didst thou that? (T.) ― -b2- IJ says that, were it syn. with mataY , it would be conditional; whereas it was not mentioned by his colleagues among the adverbs used conditionally, as mataY and A^ayona &c.: but sometimes it has a conditional meaning, though that meaning be not explicit. (M.) A poet says, A^ay~aAna nuw^ominoka taA^omano gayoranaA wa A_i*aA lamo tudoriki AlA^amona min~aA lamo tazalo Ha*iraA [ When we grant thee security, thou wilt be secure from others than us; and when thou obtainest not security from us, thou wilt not cease to be in a state of fear ]. (I 'Ak p. 300.)

(of the former, S, M, Msb, or of the latter, B) is A^aboraAN ; and (of the latter, S, M, Msb, or of the former, B) bararapN : (S, M, Msb, K:) the former pl. is often specially applied to saints, those who abstain from worldly pleasures, and devotees; and the latter, to the recording angels. (B.) Albar~u is also a name of God; (M, K;) meaning (assumed tropical:) The Merciful, or Compassionate: (M:) or the Very Benign to his servants; (IAth;) the Ample in goodness or beneficence: (B:) AlbaAr~u is not so used. sourceDefinition: inf. n. of 1: (T, S, M, &c.:) it is said by some to signify primarily Ampleness, largeness, or extensiveness; whence bar~N as opposed to baHorN : then, ― -b2- Benevolent and solicitous regard or treatment or conduct [ to parents and others; i. e. piety to parents; and (tropical:) towards God ]: and goodness, or beneficence: and kindness, or good and affectionate and gentle behaviour, and regard for the circumstances of another: (Esh-Shiháb [El-Khafájee], MF:) or bar~N , as opposed to baHorN , [or as signifying “ a wide tract of land, ” (Bd in ii. 41,)] is the original of bir~N , (Bd in ii. 41, B, TA,) which signifies ample, large, or extensive, goodness or beneficence, (Z, in the Ksh, ii. 41, [but he regards it as the original of bar~N ,] and Bd on the same passage, and B, K, TA,) to men; (TA;) or comprehending every kind of goodness: (Ksh and Bd ubi suprà:) and hence it is said to be in three things: in the service of God: in paying regard to relations; acting well to them: and in dealing with strangers: (Bd ubi suprà:) or every deed that is approved: (Ksh and Bd in ii. 172:) and [particularly] obedience to God: (T, S, M, &c.: [see also bar~apu :]) [and every incumbent duty: and hence,] the pilgrimage to Mekkeh: (K:) and fidelity to an engagement: (TA:) also a gratuitous gift, or favour; and a bounty, or benefit; syn. faDolN ; (Msb;) and A_iHosaAnN ; as also ↓ mabar~apN [an inf. n., but when used as a simple subst. its pl. is mabaArN and mabar~aAtN ]. (Har p. 94.) In the Kur [ii. 172], where it is said, lukin~a Albir~a mano A=mana biAA@ll~`hi , by Albr~ is meant *aA Albir~i [i. e. But the pious, or obedient to God, is he who believeth in God ]; (T, M, Ksh, Bd, Jel;) and some read AlbaAr~a : (Ksh, Bd, Jel:) or the meaning is, lkn~ Albir~a bir~u mn A=mn bA ll~`h i. e. but the obedience of which it behooveth one to be mindful is the obedience of him who believeth in God: (Sb, T, IJ, M, Ksh, Bd:) and this explanation is preferable to the former. (Bd.) It is said in a prov., (T, S,) laA yaEorifu hir~FA mino birK , (S, A, K, but in the T and M maA is put in the place of lA ,) meaning He knows not him who dislikes him, or hates him, from him who behaves towards him with kindness, or goodness and affection and gentleness, and regard for his circumstances: (S, M, A, K, * TA:) or undutiful conduct to a parent from gentleness, or courtesy: (ElFezáree, T, K:) or altercation, (T,) or dislike, or hatred, (K,) from honourable treatment: (T, K:) or the calling of sheep, or goats, from the driving of them: (IAar, S, K:) or the driving of sheep, or goats, from the calling of them: (Yoo, T:) or the calling of them to water from the calling of them to fodder; (K;) which last rendering is agreeable with an explanation of bir~N by IAar [mentioned in the T]; (TA;) and ↓ birobirN , also, has the signification here assigned to bir~N : (K, * TA:) or Alharoharap from Albarobarap ; (A'Obeyd, T, K;) i. e. the crying of sheep from the crying of goats: (A'Obeyd, T:) or the cat from the rat, or mouse: (IAar, T, M, K:) and bir~N also signifies the [ species of rat called ] jura* : (Aboo-Tálib, T, K:) or a small animal resembling the rat or mouse: (M:) and the young of the fox. (K.) ― -b3- Also Good, as a subst., not an adj.; syn. xayorN ; (Sh, T, Mgh, Msb, K;) which comprises all that has been said in explanation of bir~N (Sh, T, Mgh) as used in the saying of Mohammad, Ealyokumo biAlS~idoqi faA_in~ahu yahodiY A_ilaY Albir~i [ Keep ye to truth; for it guides to good, or to a good, or right, state ]: some render it in this instance by Alxayor ; and some, by AlS~alaAH . (Sh, T.) It signifies also The good of the present life, consisting in spiritual and worldly blessings, and of that which is to come, consisting in everlasting enjoyment in Paradise: so in the Kur iii. 86: (T:) or [simply] Paradise. (K.) ― -b4- Also The heart; or the mind. (K.) So in the saying, huwa muTomay^in~u Albir~i [ He is quiet, or at rest, in heart, or mind ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) sometimes pronounced baEiyrN , (K,) which latter is of the dial. of BenooTemeem, but the former is the more chaste, (TA,) A camel, male or female; (S, Msb, K;) as applied to a camel, like A_inosaAnN applied to a human being; (S, Msb;) whereas jamalN is applied only to a male camel, and naAqapN to a she-camel; bakorN and bakorapN are respectively terms like fatnFY and fataApN ; and qaluwSN is like the term jaAriyapN ; so say, among others, ISk and Az and IJ; and it is added in the Mutahffidh, that the terms jml and nAqp are applied only when the animal has entered the seventh year: (Msb:) but bEyr is more commonly applied to the male camel; (Msb, K;) and only to one that has entered its fifth year; (S, K;) or that has entered its ninth year: (K:) the pl. is A^aboEirapN [a pl. of pauc.] and buEoraAnN (S, Msb, K) and biEoraAnN (K) and buEurN (TA) and (pl. of A^aboEirapN TA) A^abaAEiru (S, Msb, K) and A^abaAEiyru (K.) If one say, A^aEoTuwniY baEiyrFA [ Give ye to me a bEyr ], the persons so addressed, accord. to EshSháfi'ee, are not to give a she-camel: (Msb:) but the following phrases are transmitted from the Arabs: SaraEatoniY baEiyriY My she-camel threw me down prostrate: (S, A:) and Halabotu baEiyriY I milked my camel: (A, Msb:) and $aribotu mino labani baEiyriY I drank of the milk of my camel: (S:) and kilaA h`*iyoni AlbiEorayoni naAqapN Each of these two camels is a she-camel. (A.) layolapu AlbaEiyri [ The night of the camel ], mentioned in a trad. of Jábir, means the night in which the Prophet purchased of him his camel. (TA.) ― -b2- Also An ass: (IKh, K:) so in the Kur xii. 72; but this signification is of rare occurrence: (IKh:) and anything that carries: (IKh, K:) so in the Hebrew language [ 165 (see Gen. xlv. 17)]. (TA.)

definition: , aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. bukaA='N and bukFA (S, Msb, K) and mabokFY , (Har p. 11,) He wept; i. e. he lamented, or grieved, shedding tears at the same time; and he lamented, or grieved, alone; and...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. bukaA='N and bukFA (S, Msb, K) and mabokFY , (Har p. 11,) He wept; i. e. he lamented, or grieved, shedding tears at the same time; and he lamented, or grieved, alone; and he shed tears alone: (Er-Rághib, TA:) accord. to some, the preferable opinion is, that there is no difference between bukaA='u and bukFA : (TA:) or the former means the crying, or uttering of the voice [ of lamentation ], (S, IKtt, Msb, TA, &c.,) that accompanies AlbukaA=' [so in copies of the S and in the TA, but correctly AlbukaA ]; (S, IKtt, TA;) and the latter ( bukFA ), the shedding of tears: (S, IKtt, Msb, TA, &c.:) or the former, i. e. with medd, means the shedding of tears by reason of lamentation, or grief, and raising of the voice, or crying, [ at the same time, ] when the voice is predominant, being like rugaA='N , and vugaA='N and other words of the same form applied to denote the uttering of a cry or of the voice; and the latter, [the shedding of tears &c. ] when lamentation, or grief, is predominant: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or by the former is meant the crying, or uttering of the voice [ of lamentation ]; and by the latter, the lamenting, or grieving. (Kh, TA.) tabokaA='N and tibokaA='N [may be inf. ns. of bakaY or of ↓ bak~aY , and] signify the same as bukaA='N : or much bukaA' [or weeping, &c.]: (K:) MF asserts that tibokaA='N (with kesr) and the former of these explanations are unknown; but both the word and the explanation are mentioned by Lh, as used in a form of words uttered by Arab women of the desert to fascinate men: ISd, however, says that it should be tabokaA=' , because it is an inf. n. of a class formed to denote muchness [of the attribute signified by the verb], like taho*aArN and taloEaAbN &c.; and IAar says that tabokaA'N , with fet-h, has the latter of the two significations assigned to it above. (TA.) [See what is said of the measure tifoEaAlN voce bay~ana .] You say, bakaY lahu (MF, TA) and bakaY Ealayohi , (S, Msb, K, MF,) meaning [ He wept ] for, or over, him, or it: and only bakaY bihi [or thus and also bakaYminohu as appears from what follows] when meaning [ He wept ] because, or in consequence, of it: ('Ináyeh, MF, TA:) and bakaAhu and ↓ bak~aAhu , (As, AZ, S, Msb, K,) inf. n. of the former bukaA='N (K) [and bukFA ], and of the latter tabokiyapN , (TA,) signify the same as bakaY Ealayohi ; (As, AZ, S, Msb, * K;) the object being a man: (As, S:) and (or as some say, TA) he wept for, or over, him, i. e., one dead; or did so, and enumerated his good qualities or actions; syn. ravaAhu : (K:) or, as some say, bakaAhu means [ he wept because, or in consequence, of it, i. e.,] on account of being pained: and bakaY Ealayohi , [ he wept for, or over, him, ] by reason of tenderness of heart, or compassion: and [hence] it is said that bakayotuhu is originally bakayotu minohu : (TA:) [and ↓ bak~aAhu may have an intensive, or a frequentative, meaning; for it is said that] bak~iY , addressed to the eye, signifies weep thou much, and repeatedly. (Ham p. 461.) ― -b2- [Hence,] bakat Als~aHaAbapu (assumed tropical:) The cloud rained. (Msb.) ― -b3- bakaY also means He sang: [in the CK, wbakaY Ean~iY is erroneously put for wbakaY gan~aY :] thus it has two contr. significations: (K, TA:) accord. to MF, it has this meaning only in relation to the pigeon and the like; but it is also used in this sense when said of a man, as in a verse cited voce janaAzapN , q. v. : and he observes that the assertion of its having two contr significations requires consideration, seeing that it is also said to signify ravaY ; [for in the performance of rivaA=' , it is a common practice to sing;] but rivaA=' is generally accompanied by lamentation, and ginaA=' by rejoicing. (TA.) ― -b4- baAkayotuhu fabakayotuhu : see 3.

definition: [ Hyoscyamus, or henbane;
sourceDefinition: [ Hyoscyamus, or henbane; ] an arabicized word, [said to be] from [the Persian] banoko ; [but see a quotation from Hammer-Purgstall, near the close of this paragraph;] a certain plant, (Mgh, and Har p. 365,) having an intoxicating kind of grain, or, as some say, (Mgh,) of which the leaves and peel and seeds torpify: (Mgh, Har:) it is said, in the Kánoon, (Mgh,) by Aboo-'Alee [Ibn-Seenà, or Avicenna], (Har,) that it is a poison which confuses the intellect, and annuls the memory, and occasions insanity and [ the disorder termed ] xunaAq [or quinsy ]; (Mgh, Har;) and it is red, and white: (Har:) a certain plant having a kind of grain that confuses the intellect, and occasions alienation of the mind, or insanity; and sometimes it intoxicates, when a man drinks it after it has been dissolved; and it is said to occasion forgetfulness: (Msb:) a certain torpifying plant, well known; different from Ha$iy$u AlHaraAfiy$i ; disordering the intellect ( muxab~iTN liloEaqoli ), rendering insane, allaying the pains of humours and pustules, and the earache, (K, TA,) applied as a liniment or as a poultice; (TA;) the worst kind (K, TA) for use (TA) is the black; then, the red; and the safest kind is the white. (K, TA.) [Kzw says that the leaves of the garden-hemp ( qin~ab busotaAniY~ , or $ahodaAnaji , the latter of which properly signifies hemp-seed,) are the banoj which, when eaten, disorders the intellect. And ElIdreesee applies the appellation Ha$iy$iy~ap to the “ Assassins. ” This establishes the correctness of De Sacy's opinion, that the appellation “ Assassins ” is derived from the vulgar pl. Ha$~aA$iyn , (hemp-eaters, or persons who intoxicate themselves with hemp,) for Ha$~aA$iyn is syn. with Ha$iy$~ap , and the sect called by us the “ Assassins ” are expressly said by the Arabs to have made frequent use of banoj . Baron Hammer-Purgstall, correctly regarding banoj as hyoscyamus (or henbane), makes the following important observations, “ ‘ Bendj, ’ the pl. of which in Coptic is ‘ nibendj, ’ is without doubt the same plant as the ‘ nepenthe, ’ which has hitherto so much perplexed the commentators of Homer. Helen evidently brought the nepenthe from Egypt, and bendj is there still reputed to possess all the wonderful qualities which Homer attributes to it. ” (Trébutien, “ Contes Inédits des Mille et une Nuits, ” tome i. p. 12, note.)] The phrase $ariba Albanoja is used by ElKarkhee [as meaning He drank the bnj ] because it is mixed with water; or [as meaning he took, or swallowed, the bnj ,] according to the conventional language of the physicians. (Mgh.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) the most chaste form of the verb in the sense here following, (S, TA,) and that which most commonly obtains, and the only form allowed by Th and IKt; (TA;) and bahita , (S, L, Msb, K,) aor. ; (Msb, K;) and bahuta , (S, L, Msb, K,) in which the dammeh is said to give intensiveness to the signification, as in qaDuwa Alr~ajulu , (TA,) aor. ; (Msb, K;) and bahata , aor. (K) and ; (TA;) inf. n. bahotN ; (JK, K;) He was, or became, confounded, perplexed, or amazed, and unable to see his right course; (JK, S, Msb, K;) not knowing what to prefer nor what to postpone: (TA in art. A$r :) he looked at a thing that he saw with a look of wonder: (A, TA:) he was, or became, affected with wonder: (JK:) he was, or became, cut short, ( AnoqaTaEa , K, TA,) and was silent, being confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course: (TA:) he (an adversary in a dispute or litigation) was overcome by an argument, an allegation, or a plea. (L.) All these forms occur in different readings of the saying in the Kur [ii. 260], fabuhita A@l~a*iY kafara and fabahita &c., (IJ, TA,) explained in the Wá'ee as meaning, And he who disbelieved remained in confusion, or perplexity, not seeing his right course, looking as one in wonder: (Lb, TA:) but accord. to him who reads fabahata , the word Al*Y may hold the place of a noun in the accus. case [as will be seen from what follows]. (IJ, TA.) -A2- bahatahu , aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. bahotN , (S, K,) He, or it, caused him to become confounded, perplexed, or amazed, not seeing his right course: (Zj, Msb: [Golius, on the authority of Ibn-Maaroof, assigns this meaning to ↓ bh~thu :]) or took him unawares, or by surprise, or unexpectedly, or suddenly. (S, K.) Zj cites as an ex. of the former meaning the saying in the Kur [xxi. 41], taA^otiyhimo bagotapF fatabohatuhumo , i. e., It shall come upon them suddenly, or unawares, and cause them to become confounded, &c.: (TA: and so Bd and Jel explain it:) or, and shall overcome them: (Bd:) J cites the same as an ex. of the latter of the two meanings in the preceding sentence; but his doing so requires consideration; for the meaning which he gives is taken from the word bgtp ; not from Albahotu . (MF, TA.) [But it is said also that] mubaAhatapN [inf. n. of ↓ bAhthu ] signifies The taking, or coming upon, [one] unawares, by surprise, or unexpectedly. (JK.) ― -b2- bahatahu , aor. , (S, A, K, &c.,) inf. n. bahotN and bahatN and buhotaAnN , (S, K,) or the last is a simple subst., (Msb,) He calumniated him; slandered him; accused him falsely; said against him that which he had not done: (S, A, K:) [or he did so in such a manner as to make one to be confounded, or perplexed, or amazed, at the falsity of the charge, and not to see his right course: (see buhotaAnN , below:)] he lied against him; forged a lie, or lies, against him; and i. q. qaAbalahu biAlka*ibi [ he accused him to his face falsely, or with falsehood ]; (TA;) Albahotu signifies AisotiqobaAluka A^axaAka bimaA layosa fiyhi [ thy accusing thy brother, or fellow, to his face, of that which is not in him ]: (JK:) and bahatahaA , aor. , inf. n. bahotN , he accused her falsely of adultery; and forged a lie against her. (Msb.) [See also AigotaAbahu .] In the saying of Abu-n-Nejm, sub~iY AlHamaApa waA@bohatiY EalayohaA [ Revile thou the mother-in-law, and calumniate her, or forge lies against her ], ElY is [said by J to be] redundant, or pleonastic; for one does not say, baEata Ealayohi , but only bahatahu . (S.) Upon this, F says, in the K, that faA@bohatiY ElyhA [thus in the K] is a mistake; that J is in error, and that the right reading is faA@nohatiY ElyhA , with n : but this assertion made by F depends upon the authority of relaters of the verse in which the word in question occurs. (MF.) IB says that AbhtY may be here rendered trans. by means of ElY because it is syn. with AifotariY , which is so rendered trans., in like manner as is done in other instances, of which he gives an ex. from the Kur [xxiv. 63], yuxaAlifuwna Eano A^amorihi , meaning yaxorujuwna En Amrh : he adds that, accord. to J, En in this ex. should be considered redundant; but that En and ElY are not used redundantly like b . A$r :) he looked at a thing that he saw with a look of wonder: (A, TA:) he was, or became, affected with wonder: (JK:) he was, or became, cut short, ( AnoqaTaEa , K, TA,) and was silent, being confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course: (TA:) he (an adversary in a dispute or litigation) was overcome by an argument, an allegation, or a plea. (L.) All these forms occur in different readings of the saying in the Kur [ii. 260], fabuhita A@l~a*iY kafara and fabahita &c., (IJ, TA,) explained in the Wá'ee as meaning, And he who disbelieved remained in confusion, or perplexity, not seeing his right course, looking as one in wonder: (Lb, TA:) but accord. to him who reads fabahata , the word Al*Y may hold the place of a noun in the accus. case [as will be seen from what follows]. (IJ, TA.) -A2- bahatahu , aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. bahotN , (S, K,) He, or it, caused him to become confounded, perplexed, or amazed, not seeing his right course: (Zj, Msb: [Golius, on the authority of Ibn-Maaroof, assigns this meaning to ↓ bh~thu :]) or took him unawares, or by surprise, or unexpectedly, or suddenly. (S, K.) Zj cites as an ex. of the former meaning the saying in the Kur [xxi. 41], taA^otiyhimo bagotapF fatabohatuhumo , i. e., It shall come upon them suddenly, or unawares, and cause them to become confounded, &c.: (TA: and so Bd and Jel explain it:) or, and shall overcome them: (Bd:) J cites the same as an ex. of the latter of the two meanings in the preceding sentence; but his doing so requires consideration; for the meaning which he gives is taken from the word bgtp ; not from Albahotu . (MF, TA.) [But it is said also that] mubaAhatapN [inf. n. of ↓ bAhthu ] signifies The taking, or coming upon, [one] unawares, by surprise, or unexpectedly. (JK.) ― -b2- bahatahu , aor. , (S, A, K, &c.,) inf. n. bahotN and bahatN and buhotaAnN , (S, K,) or the last is a simple subst., (Msb,) He calumniated him; slandered him; accused him falsely; said against him that which he had not done: (S, A, K:) [or he did so in such a manner as to make one to be confounded, or perplexed, or amazed, at the falsity of the charge, and not to see his right course: (see buhotaAnN , below:)] he lied against him; forged a lie, or lies, against him; and i. q. qaAbalahu biAlka*ibi [ he accused him to his face falsely, or with falsehood ]; (TA;) Albahotu signifies AisotiqobaAluka A^axaAka bimaA layosa fiyhi [ thy accusing thy brother, or fellow, to his face, of that which is not in him ]: (JK:) and bahatahaA , aor. , inf. n. bahotN , he accused her falsely of adultery; and forged a lie against her. (Msb.) [See also AigotaAbahu .] In the saying of Abu-n-Nejm, sub~iY AlHamaApa waA@bohatiY EalayohaA [ Revile thou the mother-in-law, and calumniate her, or forge lies against her ], ElY is [said by J to be] redundant, or pleonastic; for one does not say, baEata Ealayohi , but only bahatahu . (S.) Upon this, F says, in the K, that faA@bohatiY ElyhA [thus in the K] is a mistake; that J is in error, and that the right reading is faA@nohatiY ElyhA , with n : but this assertion made by F depends upon the authority of relaters of the verse in which the word in question occurs. (MF.) IB says that AbhtY may be here rendered trans. by means of ElY because it is syn. with AifotariY , which is so rendered trans., in like manner as is done in other instances, of which he gives an ex. from the Kur [xxiv. 63], yuxaAlifuwna Eano A^amorihi , meaning yaxorujuwna En Amrh : he adds that, accord. to J, En in this ex. should be considered redundant; but that En and ElY are not used redundantly like b . (TA.) ― -b3- bahata AlfaHola Eani Aln~aAqapi He removed the stallion from the she-camel in order that a stallion of more generous race might cover her. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ bahiytapN signify the same [when the former is used as a subst.; i. e. definition: [ A great, or frequent, calumniator, slanderer, or false-accuser;
sourceDefinition: [ A great, or frequent, calumniator, slanderer, or false-accuser; as also ↓ bah~aAtN , mentioned in the S only as an epithet applied to him who calumniates, slanders, or accusely falsely; ] an intensive epithet from Albahotu ; (IAth;) [i. e.] an intensive form of the act. part. n. from AlbuhotaAn [inf. n. of bahatahu ]: (Mgh:) or i. q. ↓ mubaAhitN ; (K;) i. e., one who confounds, or perplexes, or amazes, the hearer, by what he forges against him: (TA:) and one who falsely accuses a woman of adultery, and forges a lie against her: (Msb:) pl. buhutN (IAth, Mgh, Msb, K) and buhotN , and, accord. to the K, also buhuwtN ; but ISd and MF hold it to be pl. of baAhitN , not of bahuwtN ; the former observing, that a word of the measure faAEilN is one of those which have a pl. of the measure fuEuwlN , but not so one of the measure faEuwlN ; and that, as to the saying of A'Obeyd, that Eu*uwbN is pl. of Ea*uwbN , it is a mistake; for it is only pl. of EaA*ibN , and the pl. of Ea*uwbN is Eu*ubN . (TA. [But see art. E*b .])

sourceDefinition: fem. of *aA ; (M;) i. q. *iho [ This and that ]; (T;) a noun of indication, denoting that which is female or feminine; like *aA (S, K) applied to that which is male or masculine; (S;) and you say also tiho , like *iho : (S, K:) the dual is taAni : and the pl., A^uwlaA='i . (S, K.) En-Nábighah [Edh-Dhubyánee] says, (T, S,) excusing himself to En-Noamán [Aboo-Káboos], whom he had satirized, (TA,) haA A_in~a taA Ei*orapN A_ino lamo takuno nafaEato faA_in~a SaAHibahaA qado taAha fiY Albaladi [ Now verily this is an excuse: if it profit not, then verily its author has lost his way in the desert, or in the waterless desert ]: (T, S: but in the latter, lA is put in the place of lm :) tA here points to the qaSiydap [or ode]; and E*rp is a subst from AiEoti*aArN ; and tAh means taHay~ara ; and Albld means AlmafaAzap . (TA.) The dim. of taA is tay~aA , (T, S, M, K,) which is anomalous, like *ay~aA the dim. of *aA , &c. (I'Ak p. 343. [Much has been written respecting the formation of this dim. to reduce it to something like rule, but I pass it over as, in my opinion, unprofitable and unsatisfactory; and only refer to what is said respecting the duals A^ulay~aA and A^ulay~aA='i in art. AlY . See an ex. voce mir~apN .] ― -b2- haA is prefixed to it (T, S, K) [as an inceptive particle] to give notice of what is about to be said, (S,) so that one says haAtaA [meaning This ], (T, S, K,) as in haAtaA fulaAnapu [ This is such a woman ]; (T;) and [in the dual] haAtaAni ; and [in the pl.] h`w^ulaA='i : and the dim. is haAtay~aA . (S.) ― -b3- When you use it in addressing another person, you add to it k [as a particle of allocution], and say taAka (S, K) and tiyka and tiloka (T, S, K) and taloka , which is a bad dial. var., (S, K,) and taAlika , (T, S,) which is the worst of these: (T:) [all meaning That: ] the dual is taAnika and taAn~ika , the latter with tesh-deed, (S, K, [but in some copies of the S, only the latter is mentioned,]) and taAlika [which, like taAn~ika , is dual of tiloka or taloka , which are contractions of taAlika ; these two duals being for taAnilika , the original, but unused, form]: (K:) the pl. is A^uwl`y^ika [or A^uwlaA=y^ika ] and A^uwlaAka and A^uwlaAlika [respecting all of which see A^ulaY , in art. AlY ]: (S, K:) and the dim. is tay~aAka and tay~aAlika : (K: [in the TA, the latter is erroneously written tay~Anika :]) the k relates to the person or persons whom you address, masc. and fem. and dual and pl.: [but in addressing a female, you may say taAki &c.; in addressing two persons, taAkumaA &c.; in addressing more than two males, taAkumo &c.; and in addressing more than two females, taAkun~a &c.:] what precedes the k relates to the person [or thing] indicated, masc. and fem. and dual and pl. (S.) ― -b4- haA is also prefixed to tiyka and taAka , so that one says, haAtiyka hinodu and haAtaAka hinodu [ This, or that, is Hind ]. (S, K. *) Abu-n-Nejm says, jiy^onaA nuHay~iyka wanasotajodiykaA faA@foEalo binaA haAtaAka A^awo haAtiykaA meaning [ We have come saluting thee and seeking of thee a gift: then do thou to us ] this or that: [give us] a salutation or a gift. (S.) The haA that is used to give notice of what is about to be said is not prefixed to tlk because the l is made a substitute for that hA : (S, TA:) or, as IB says, they do not prefix that hA to *`lika and tiloka because the l denotes the remoteness of that which is indicated and the hA denotes its nearness, so that the two are incompatible. (TA.) -A2- taA and tA='N Names of the letter t : see that letter, and see arts. twA^ and tY . -A3- taA and taA^aA or taA= for ta$aA=' : see (near its end) art. A .

sourceDefinition: [a coll. gen. n., of which the n. un. is with p : Native gold, in the form of dust or of nuggets: this is the sense in which the word is generally used in the present day:] broken gold: (M:) it is not so called unless in the dust of its mine, or broken: (IJ, M:) or gold, and silver, before it is wrought: (Lth, T, IF, Msb:) or broken, or crumbled, particles of gold, and of silver, before they are wrought: when they are wrought, they are called *ahabN and fiD~apN : (IAar, T, K:) or uncoined gold (S, Mgh, Msb) and silver: (Mgh:) when coined, it is called EayonN : (S, Msb:) [properly,] the term tbr should not be employed save as applied to gold; but some apply it to silver also: (S:) the tbr of silver, as well as of gold, is mentioned in a trad.: (TA:) or gold (M, K) universally: (M:) and silver: (K:) or what is extracted from the mine, (M, K,) of gold and silver and all jawaAhir [here meaning native ores ] of the earth, (M,) before it is wrought (M, K) and used: (M:) or any jawohar [or native ore ] before it is used, of copper (Zj, T, Mgh, Msb) and brass (Zj, T, Mgh) or iron (Msb) &c.: (Zj, Mgh, Msb:) and any jwhr [or native ore ] that is used, of copper and brass: (K:) the word is sometimes applied to other minerals than gold and silver, as copper and iron and lead, but generally to gold; and some say that its primary application is to gold, and that the other applications are later, or tropical: (TA:) also broken pieces of glass. (Zj, T, M, K.)

definition: and turojumaAnN and tarojamaAnN , (S in art.
sourceDefinition: and turojumaAnN and tarojamaAnN , (S in art. rjm , and Msb and K in the present art.,) of which three dial. vars. the first is the best, (Msb,) and is that which commonly obtains, (TA,) An interpreter; (S, Msb, K;) an explainer of speech in another language: (S, Msb:) [ a translator: (see the verb, above:)] pl. taraAjimu and taraAjimapN ; which latter favours the opinion of those who hold the word to be of foreign origin. (S, Msb.) The t and m are [said to be] radicals; but J makes the t to be augmentative, and trjmAn is mentioned in the T [as well as in the S] in art. rjm , though the author of the T has mentioned the verb among quadriliteral-radical words; and there is a reason [for deriving it from rajama ], for one says lisaAnN yarojumu meaning “ a tongue that is chaste, or perspicuous, and copious, in speech: ” most, however, hold the t to be a radical. (Msb.) definition: , applied to denote a number, [namely Nine, ] is masc.
sourceDefinition: , applied to denote a number, [namely Nine, ] is masc. ; and ↓ tisoEN , so applied, is fem.: (S:) the latter is also written ↓ tasoEN , with fet-h to the t ; and is thus pronounced in the Kur xxxviii. 22, (Bd, MF,) accord. to one reading. (Bd.) You say tisoEapu rijaAlK [ Nine men ], and tisoEN nisowapK [ Nine women ]. (K.) When it means the things numbered, not the amount of the number, tsEp is imperf. decl., being regarded as a proper name: thus you say, tisoEapu A^akovaru mino vamaAniyapa [ Nine things are more than eight things ]. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [xvii. 103], wa laqado A=tayonaA muwsaY tisoEa A=yaAtK bay~inaAtK [ And we formerly gave unto Moses nine evident signs; generally understood to mean the principal miracles which he was empowered to perform, and which are differently enumerated in the K and other works; but by some supposed to mean statutes]. (K, * TA.) ― -b2- In tisoEapa Ea$ara , which is masc., and tisoEa Ea$orapa , which is fem., [each signifying Nineteen, ] each of the two words ends with fet-h in every case, because they are two nouns which are regarded as one noun. (TA.) The former is pronounced by some of the Arabs tisoEapa Eo$ara : and the latter, thus in the dial. of El-Hijáz [and of most of the Arabs], is pronounced tisoEa Ea$irapa in the dial. of Nejd. (S in art. E$r .) In the Kur lxxiv. 30, some read, tisoEapa Eo$ara , making the E in E$r quiescent, instead of tisoEaha Ea$ara , from a dislike of this consecution of vowels in what is like one word. (Bd, TA. *)

definition: The sheath of the penis of a camel (Lth, * AZ, T, S, M, K) &c.
sourceDefinition: The sheath of the penis of a camel (Lth, * AZ, T, S, M, K) &c.; (K;) [i. e.,] of a he-goat also, and of a bull: (M:) or the penis itself: (Lth, T, M, K:) sometimes also used in relation to a man: (M:) and ↓ vayolN signifies the same; (K;) mentioned by Ibn-'Abbád; and IAth adds vuwlN . (TA.) Hence the prov., A^axolafu mino viyli Aljamali [ More contrary to what is usual than the sheath of the penis, or than the penis, of the camel ]: for the camel, like the lion, is a retromingent. (TA.) -A2- A kind of plant; (S, K;) as also ↓ vay~ilN : (K:) a certain plant having a root and stem; when short, called najomN : and a certain herb, or, as some say, a plant, that is found on the banks, or sides, of rivers, in meadows: and, some say, a species of the [ plants, or trees, called ] janobap , which grows in the territory of [ the tribe of ] Temeem, and becomes large, so that the sheep, or goats, lie in its shelter: (M:) AHn says, (M,) in the “ Book of Plants, ” (Mgh,) the viyl , (M,) or ↓ vay~il , (Mgh,) [both appellations now applied to triticum repens, or dog's grass, ] is the najomap ; called in Persian ryzwPAdlh [?]; (Mgh;) its leaves are like those of wheat, but shorter, and it spreads upon the face of the ground, extending far, and becoming com- plicated, or tangled, so as to be like felt (M, Mgh) upon the ground; (M;) it has many joints, or knots, and short internodal portions; and scarcely, or never, grows anywhere but over water, or in a place beneath which is water; (M, Mgh;) and it is one of the plants that are regarded as indicative of the existence of water: n. un. with p : (M:) Lth says that the viyl is a certain plant that tangles upon the ground: Th, on the authority of IAar, says that it is a kind of plant said to be that called liHoyapu Alt~ayosi : and Sh says that the viylap is a green small tree [or plant ] resembling the first shoots that come forth from grain. (T.)

sourceDefinition: , an arabicized word, (S, K,) from the Persian, (S,) originally Girodaho baAno “guardian of the cake of bread,” (S, K,) and jurodubaAnN and ↓ jarodabiY~N and ↓ mujarodibN , (K,) One who puts his hand, (K,) or who puts his left hand, (S,) upon food, (K,) or upon a thing that is before him on the table, (S,) in order that no other person may take it: (S, K:) or who eats with his right hand, and prevents [ others from eating ] with his left hand: and one who eats greedily, gluttonously, or voraciously: or the first and ↓ third signify, (K, TA,) or signify also, (tropical:) a spunger; (K, TA;) because of his greediness, gluttony, or voraciousness, and his boldness. (TA.) A poet says, (namely, ElGhanawee, TA voce jarodabiylN ,) A_i*aA maA kunota fiY qawomK $ahaAwaY falaA tajoEalo $imaAlaka jarodabaAnaA [ When thou art among a greedy company of men, put not thy left hand upon the food as a jrdbAn ]: (Fr, S:) or the last word is jarodabiylaA , meaning, (accord. to Sh, as also jarodabaAn , TA voce jrdbyl ,) one that takes a fragment [ of food ] with his left hand, and eats with his right hand, and, when what the party have is consumed, eats what is in his left hand. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. jarofN (S, Msb, K) and jarofapN , (Lh, K,) He took away, carried away, or removed, the whole of it, (S, Msb, K,) or the greater part of it, (S,) or much of it: (S, K:) and [in like manner ↓ jr~fhu ; for its inf. n.] tajoriyfN signifies the act of carrying away wholly: (KL:) and ↓ Ajtrfhu he took the whole of it. (TA in art. jft .) ― -b2- Also, (inf. n. jarofN , TA,) He swept it away, namely, mud, (S, K,) from the surface of the earth; (TA;) and so ↓ jr~fhu , (K,) inf. n. tajoriyfN ; (TA;) and ↓ tjr~fhu : (K:) or ↓ tajoriyfN signifies the act of clearing away mud or the like well; in Persian, nyk rndydn : (KL: [Golius, app. misled by a mistranscription, has explained the verb, jr~f , as on the authority of the KL, by “ bene effudit: ”]) and Al$~aYo'a ↓ Ajtrf he swept away the thing ( jarafahu ) from the surface of the earth. (TA.) You say also, jarafatohu Als~uyuwlu , (Msb,) or ↓ jr~fthu , inf. n. tajoriyfN ; (S;) and ↓ tjr~fthu ; (S, K;) The torrents swept it away; (TA;) [or swept it partially away; or wore it away; ] namely, a portion of land. (S, Msb, K. See jurufN .) And, of a death commonly prevailing, jarafa Aln~aAsa kajarofi Als~ayoli (tropical:) [ It swept away, or destroyed, men, like the sweeping away of the torrent ]: (TA:) and ↓ yajotarifu maAla Alqawomi [ It sweeps away, or destroys, the cattle of the people ]. (S, TA.) ― -b3- [ He shovelled it, or scooped it, away, or up, or out. ] You say, jarafahu bikilotaA yadayohi [ He scooped it up, or out, with both his hands ]; i. e. something dry, as flour, and sand, and the like. (S in art. Hfn .) ― -b4- jurifa It (herbage) was eaten up utterly. (TA.)

definition: and ↓ jurofN , (S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ jurofN , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) the latter a contraction of the former, (Msb,) [ An abrupt, water-worn, bank or ridge; ] a bank ( jaAnibN Ksh and Jel in ix. 110) of a valley, the lower part of which is excavated by the water, and hollowed out by the torrents, so that it remains uncompact, unsound, or weak; (Ksh ib.;) a bank, or an acclivity, of a water-course of a valley and the like, when the water has carried away from its lower part, and undermined it, so that it has become like what is termed a daHol , with its upper part overhanging; (L;) a portion of land (or sand, S in art. thr ) which the torrents have partially swept away, or worn away, (↓ tajar~afatohu , S, K, or ↓ jarafatohu , Msb,) and eaten; (S, Msb, K;) a portion of the lower part of the side of a valley, and of a river, eaten by the torrent; (M, TA;) the side of the bank of a river, that has been eaten by the water, so that some part of it every little while falls: (Har p. 47:) and the latter, [or each,] a place which the torrent does not take away; as also ↓ jirofN ; (K;) [i. e. a bank, or ridge, that remains rising abruptly by the bed of a torrent or stream: ] pl. [of pauc.] (of jurufN , TA) A^ajoraAfN , (K,) like A^aTonaAbN pl. of TunubN , (TA,) and [of mult.] (of jurofN , though it is implied in the K that it is of jurufN , TA) jirafapN , like jiHarapN (S, K) pl. of juHorN , (S,) and juruwfN . (ISd, TA.)

definition: A torrent that carries away everything;
sourceDefinition: A torrent that carries away everything; (S, Msb;) i. q. juHaAfN applied to a torrent; as also ↓ jaworafN ; (K;) and ↓ jaAruwfN a torrent that sweeps away that by which it passes, by reason of its copiousness, carrying away everything, and so ↓ jaArifN applied to rain. definition: The flower of the pomegranate: an arabicized word, from GulonaAro , (K,) which is Persian, composed of Gulo “ a flower, ” and naAro “ a pomegranate.
sourceDefinition: The flower of the pomegranate: an arabicized word, from GulonaAro , (K,) which is Persian, composed of Gulo “ a flower, ” and naAro “ a pomegranate. ” (MF.) It is said that whoever swallows three grains of it, of the smallest that may be, (K,) on the condition of his taking them with his mouth from the tree, before their opening, at sunrise, on a Wednesday, (Tedhkiret Dáwood, TA,) will not have ophthalmia in that year. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. jimaAHN (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.) and jumuwHN (S, A, Msb, K) and jamoHN , (K,) or this last has not been heard, (Mgh,) He (a horse) overcame his rider, or gained the mastery over him, (S, L, K,) running away with him: (L:) or broke loose, or ran away, (Msb,) and went at random, without any certain aim, so as not to be turned by anything: (Mgh, Msb:) or ran so as to have the mastery over his rider: (Ham p. 568:) and jamaHa biraAkibihi (A, Mgh, Msb) he overcame his rider, (A, Mgh,) and ran away so that he could not govern him: (A:) or became refractory, so that he overcame his rider: (Msb:) and sometimes, (Msb,) this verb also signifies he was quick, or swift, (A, Msb,) and brisk, lively, or sprightly; denoting in this case a quality that is approved; whereas in the senses before explained it denotes a quality that is disapproved: but in the last sense it is obsolete [unless tropically applied to a man]. (Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) He (said of anything [i. e. of a man or any animal]) went at random, or heedlessly, without consideration or certain aim, not obeying a guide to the right course. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) He (said of a man, S, L) hastened, or went quickly, (S, L, K,) A_ilayohi to him, or it, so that his course was not turned for anything. (L, TA.) wahumo yajomaHuwna , in the Kur [ix. 57], means (assumed tropical:) They hastening, or going quickly: (AO, S, L:) or hastening so that nothing turns them back, like the horse that is termed jamuwH : (Bd, Jel:) or running like horses that overcome their riders and run away so as to be ungovernable by them. (A.) And jamaHa fiY A_ivorihi , occurring in a trad., (assumed tropical:) He hastened after him, or it, so that nothing turned him back. (L.) ― -b3- jamaHati AlmaroA^apu (tropical:) The woman went forth from the place where she used to pass the night, in anger, without the permission of her husband. (Msb.) And jamaHato mino zawojihaA , so in the S and L &c., but in the K jamaHato zawojahaA , [which is evidently a mistake,] (TA,) (tropical:) She went forth from the house, or tent, of her husband, to her own family, before he divorced her; (S, L, K;) inf. n. jimaAHN . (L, TA.) And jamaHato A_ilaY A^aholihaA (tropical:) She went to her family without the permission of her husband. (A.) ― -b4- jamaHati Als~afiynapu (tropical:) The ship quitted her course, (A, TA,) and became ungovernable by the sailors; inf. n. jumuwHN . (TA.) ― -b5- jamaHati AlmafaAzapu biAlqawomi (tropical:) The desert led the people, or party, far away, by reason of its great extent. (A, TA.) ― -b6- jamaHa bihi muraAduhu (tropical:) The object of his desire baffled his efforts to attain it. (A, TA.)

definition: (T, S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, K) and ↓ jaAmiHN (Mgh, Msb) A horse that overcomes his rider, or gains the mastery over him, (S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, K,) being refractory, (Msb,) and runs away with him, (L,) or...
sourceDefinition: (T, S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, K) and ↓ jaAmiHN (Mgh, Msb) A horse that overcomes his rider, or gains the mastery over him, (S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, K,) being refractory, (Msb,) and runs away with him, (L,) or runs away so that his rider cannot govern him, (A,) or goes away at random, without any certain aim, so as not to be turned by anything: (Mgh:) or that will not bend his head: (TA:) the former epithet, (T, Mgh, TA,) and the latter, (Mgh, Msb,) applied alike to the horse and the mare: (T, Mgh, Msb, TA:) and the former has two meanings; one denoting what is a fault, for which the horse may be returned; (T, Mgh, TA;) i. e., that habitually takes his own way, so that his rider cannot turn him from it; (T, TA;) or as explained before; (Mgh;) the other meaning being quick, or swift, and brisk, lively, and sprightly; and this does not imply a fault (T, Mgh, TA) for which he may be returned. (T, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) Anything [i. e. a man or any animal] that goes at random, or heedlessly, without consideration or certain aim, not obeying a guide to the right course: (TA:) and the former epithet, (Msb, K,) or each of the two, (S, * A,) (tropical:) a man who follows his own natural desire, without consideration, not obeying a guide to the right course of conduct, (S, A, Msb, K,) so that he cannot be turned back. (S, K.) And ↓ jum~aAHN [is pl. of ↓ jaAmiHN , accord. to analogy, and] signifies (assumed tropical:) Men routed, defeated, or put to flight, in war. (IAar, K.) ― -b3- mafaAzapN jamuwHN (assumed tropical:) [ A desert that leads one far away, by reason of its great extent: see 1, last sentence but one: likened to a horse that is termed jamuwH ]: occurring in a poem of Dhu-r-Rummeh. (TA in art. nHb .)

definition: An arrow, (S, K,) or a small arrow, (L,) without an iron point, having a round head, with which the art of shooting is learned (S, L, K) by a boy: (S, L:) or one with which boys play, putting upon...
sourceDefinition: An arrow, (S, K,) or a small arrow, (L,) without an iron point, having a round head, with which the art of shooting is learned (S, L, K) by a boy: (S, L:) or one with which boys play, putting upon its head a date or some clay, in order that it may not wound: (L:) or it signifies also a date put upon the head of a piece of wood, with which boys play: (K:) birds are shot at with it, and knocked down, without being killed, so that the shooter takes them: and it is also called jub~aAHN : (T, TA:) or a boy's arrow, upon the end of which he puts a lump of chewed dates of the size of the EifaAD [here meaning stopper ] of a bottle, in order that it ( the end ) may go more directly, and be smooth; without feathers, and sometimes without a notch. (AHn, L.) -A2- Also That [ kind of plant ] at the extremities of which come forth what resemble ears of wheat, soft, (L, K,) like foxes' tails, or (L) resembling the heads of the HaliY~ and the Sil~iyaAn and the like: (L, K:) a coll. gen. n.: n. un. with p : (L:) pl. jamaAmiyHu ; and in poetry jamaAmiHu ; (L, K;) the latter allowable only in cases of necessity. (L.) -A3- See also jamuwHN .

definition: , (Fr, Msb,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (Fr, Msb,) inf. n. tajomiyEN , (K,) He collected; brought, or gathered, together; gathered up; assembled; congregated; mustered; drew together; or contracted; [thus I render jamaEa , as explained above;] much; with much, or extraordinary, energy, or effectiveness, or the like; vigorously; or well. (Bd in civ. 2; Msb, K.) Thus in the Kur [civ. 2], Al~a*iY jam~aEa maAlFA waEad~adahu (S, * Bd) Who hath collected much wealth, and hath made it a provision for the casualties of fortune, or reckoned it time after time: (Bd:) [or who hath amassed, or accumulated, wealth, &c.:] or who hath gained, acquired, or earned, wealth, &c.; thus differing from jamaEa , explained above: but it is allowable to say maAlFA ↓ jamaEa , without teshdeed; (Fr;) and thus it is [generally] read in this passage of the Kur. (Bd.) See also 1. ― -b2- Ham~aEato , (TA,) inf. n. as above, (K,) She (a hen) collected her eggs in her belly. (K, TA.) ― -b3- jam~aEuwA , (inf. n. as above, S,) They were present on the Friday, (S, Mgh, Msb,) or with the congregation [ then collected ], (Mgh,) and performed the prayers [ with the congregation ] on that day. (S, Mgh.) ― -b4- Hence the saying, A^aw~alu jumoEapK jum~iEato fiY AlA_isolaAmu baEoda Almadiynapi bijuw^aAviY [ The first Friday that was observed by the performance of congregational prayer in the time of El-Islám, after the observance thereof in El-Medeeneh, was in Ju-áthà ]. (TA.)

Thus in the Kur [civ. 2], Al~a*iY jam~aEa maAlFA waEad~adahu (S, * Bd) Who hath collected much wealth, and hath made it a provision for the casualties of fortune, or reckoned it time after time: (Bd:) [or who hath amassed, or accumulated, wealth, &c.:] or who hath gained, acquired, or earned, wealth, &c.; thus differing from jamaEa , explained above: but it is allowable to say maAlFA ↓ jamaEa , without teshdeed; (Fr;) and thus it is [generally] read in this passage of the Kur. (Bd.) See also 1. ― -b2- Ham~aEato , (TA,) inf. n. as above, (K,) She (a hen) collected her eggs in her belly. (K, TA.) ― -b3- jam~aEuwA , (inf. n. as above, S,) They were present on the Friday, (S, Mgh, Msb,) or with the congregation [ then collected ], (Mgh,) and performed the prayers [ with the congregation ] on that day. (S, Mgh.) ― -b4- Hence the saying, A^aw~alu jumoEapK jum~iEato fiY AlA_isolaAmu baEoda Almadiynapi bijuw^aAviY [ The first Friday that was observed by the performance of congregational prayer in the time of El-Islám, after the observance thereof in El-Medeeneh, was in Ju-áthà ]. (TA.)

definition: A^ajomaEotu Al$~aYo'a signifies I put the thing together;
sourceDefinition: : see 1. A^ajomaEotu Al$~aYo'a signifies I put the thing together; such, for instance, as spoil, or plunder. (S.) You say, A^ajomaEotu Aln~ahobi , meaning I collected together from every quarter the camels taken as spoil from the people to whom they belonged, and drove them away: (AHeyth:) or A_ijomaAEN signifies [simply] the driving of camels together, or collectively. (K.) ― -b2- AlA_ijomaAEu also signifies The composing and settling a thing which has been discomposed [ and unsettled ]; as an opinion upon which one determines, resolves, or decides: (TA:) or jaEolu AlA^amori jamiyEFA baEoda tafar~uqihi , (AHeyth, K,) i. e. the determining, resolving, or deciding, upon an affair, so as to make it firmly settled, [ after it had been unsettled in the mind, or] after considering what might be its issues, or results, and saying at one time, I will do thus, and at another time, I will do thus. (AHeyth.) You say, A^ajomaEotu AlA^amora , (Ks, S, Mgh, * Msb, K,) and EalaY AlA^amori , (Mgh, * Msb, K,) I determined, resolved, or decided, upon the affair; (Ks, S, Mgh, * Msb, K;) as though I collected myself, or my mind, for it; (TA;) as, for instance, a journeying, and a fasting, (Mgh, Msb,) and a going forth, and a tarrying or an abiding; (TA;) and in like manner, A^amorahu ↓ jamaEa He determined, resolved, or decided, upon his affair; as, for instance, a fasting: (TA:) and A^ajomaEotu Alr~aA^oYi I determined, or settled, the opinion. (TA.) You say also, A^ajomiEo A^amoraka walaA tadaEohu munota$irFA [ Determine thou, or decide, upon thine affair, and do not leave it unsettled ]. (S.) The saying, in the Kur [x. 72], faA^ajomaEuwA A^amorakumo wa$urakaA='a kumo means Then determine ye, or resolve, or decide, upon your affair, (Fr, Ibn-'Arafeh, Bd,) and prepare for it, (Fr,) or AijoEaluwhu jamiyEFA , [which has the former of these meanings, as shown above,] (AHeyth,) and call ye your companions, (Fr, S, Bd, K,) $rkA'km being governed in the accus. case by the verb understood, (Bd, TA,) becanse the verb in the text is not used with $rkA' for its object, (S, K,) but only the unaugmented verb: (S:) or the meaning is then determine ye, with your companions, upon your affair; (Bd, K;) so says Aboo-Is-hák, adding that what Fr says is erroneous: (TA:) or then determine ye upon your affair and the affair of your companions, for waA^amora $urakaAy^ikumo . (Bd.) It is also said that the phrase, in the Kur [xx. 67], faA^ajomiEuwA kayodakumo means Therefore determine ye, or resolve, or decide, upon your artifice, or stratagem: (TA:) but some read kayodakumo ↓ faA@jomaEuwA , (Bd, TA,) meaning therefore combine ye all your artifice; leave nothing thereof unexerted; (TA;) and this latter reading is favoured by the phrase kayodahu ↓ fajamaE [in verse 62 of the same ch.]. (Bd.) ― -b3- Also The agreeing, or uniting, in opinion. (K, * TA.) You say, A^ajomaEuwA EalaY AlA^amori meaning They agreed, or were of one mind or opinion, upon, or respecting, the affair; (Mgh, Msb;) [and so Ealayohi ↓ AjtmEwA ; and Elyh ↓ tjm~EwA .] ― -b4- Also The preparing [a thing], or making [it] ready; syn. AlA_iEodaAdu . (K, TA. [In the CK, erroneously, AlAaEodaAdu .]) You say, A^ajomaEotu ka*aA I prepared, or made ready, such a thing. (TA.) And A^ajomiEuwA A^amorakumo Prepare ye for your affair. (Fr.) ― -b5- Also The binding the teats of a she-camel all together with the SiraAr , q. v. (K.) You say, AjmE biAln~aAqapi , (S, TA,) and AjmE Aln~aAqapi , (TA,) He so bound the teats of the she-camel; (S, TA;) and so A^akoma$a bihaA . (TA.) ― -b6- Also The drying [a thing]; drying [it] up; making [it] dry; syn. Alt~ajofiyfu waAlA_iybaAsu . (K TA. [In the CK, erroneously, Altaxofuyfu wAlAiyonAsu .]) Hence the saying of Aboo-Wejzeh Es-Saadee, waA^ajomaEati AlhawaAjiru kul~a rajoEK mina AlA^ajomaAdi waAld~amivi AlbavaA='i i.e. [ And the vehement mid-day-heats ] dried up every pool left by a torrent [ of the hard and elevated grounds and of the soft and even ground ]. (TA.) ― -b7- AjmE AlmaTaru AlA^aroDi The rain made the whole of the land, both its soft tracts and its hard tracts, to flow: (K:) and in like manner you say, A^ajomaEati AlA^aroDu saAy^ilapF The land flowed in its soft tracts [ as well as in its hard tracts; i. e., in every part ]. (TA.) [See also 10.]

definition: It (a thing in a scattered or dispersed state, S, and a number of men, Msb, [and a number of things,]) became collected, brought together, gathered together, gathered up, assembled, congregated, mustered, drawn together, or contracted;
sourceDefinition: It (a thing in a scattered or dispersed state, S, and a number of men, Msb, [and a number of things,]) became collected, brought together, gathered together, gathered up, assembled, congregated, mustered, drawn together, or contracted; or it collected, collected itself together, gathered itself together, came together, assembled, congregated, drew itself together, contracted itself; coalesced; combined; (K, TA;) so that the several parts or portions became near [or close ] together; (TA;) as also AijodamaEa , (K,) with d [substituted for the t ]; (TA;) and ↓ tjm~E and ↓ AstjmE signify the same: (Msb, K:) and ↓ tjm~EwA signifies they became collected, &c., [ from several places, or] hence and thence. (S, K:) [See also 10.] You say also, AjtmE maEahu (Mgh) and bihi (Msb) [meaning He was, or became, in company with him; came together with him; met with him; met him; had a meeting, or an interview, with him ]. And AjtmE maEahu EalaY A^amori ka*aA : (S, K:) see 3, first sentence: and see the sentence there next following. And in like manner, EalaY ↓ tjm~EwA fulaAnK They combined, conspired, or leagued, together against such a one. (Ibn-Buzurj, TA in art. Dfr .) [See also AjtmEwA EalaY AlA^amori in 4, latter half.] You also say, AijotamaEati A=raAw^uhumo EalaY AlA^amori [ Their opinions agreed together, or were in unison, upon, or respecting, the affair ]. (Er-Rághib.) And AijotamaEato $araAy^iTu AlA_imaAmapi The conditions of the office of Imám occurred together [or were combined, or they coexisted, in such a case]; as also ↓ AisotajomaEato . (Msb: [but it is implied in the Mgh that the latter verb in this sense is not of established authority.]) [See a similar ex. voce ArtfE .] ― -b2- [ He , or it, was, or became, compact in make or frame, compressed, contracted, or the like. ― -b3- And hence,] He (a man) attained to his full state of manly vigour, and his beard became fullgrown. (K, TA.) The verb is not thus used in speaking of a woman. (S, TA.) ― -b4- [Hence also,] AjtmE fiY AlHaAjapi [ He was quick and vigorous in executing the needful affair, or in accomplishing that which was wanted; as though he compacted his frame, and collected all his energy: see ma$aY mujotamiEFA , below: and see also 10]. (TA in art. km$ .) ― -b5- [Hence also,] AijotamaEati Alqidoru The cooking-pot boiled. (Z, TA.) ― -b6- [Hence also, AjtmE said of a thing, or an affair, It was, or became, composed, arranged, or settled. ]
