definition: ↓ AstjmE kul~a majomaEK [ He desired, or demanded, the collecting together of every body of soldiers;
sourceDefinition: ↓ AstjmE kul~a majomaEK [ He desired, or demanded, the collecting together of every body of soldiers; or he summoned together every body of soldiers ]: said of him who demands, or summons, armies, or military forces. (S, TA.) [But this usage of the verb is perhaps post-classical: for Mtr says,] With respect to the saying of ElAbeewardee, $aA=miy~apN tasotajomiEu Al$~awola Harojafu [ A north wind, cold and vehement, inviting to collect themselves together the she-camels whose milk has dried up, they having passed seven or eight months since bringing forth, or since pregnancy ], it seems that he has compared this verb with the generality of others of the same class, [and so derived the meaning in which he has here used it,] or that he heard it [in that sense] from the people of the cities, or towns, or villages, and cultivated lands. (Mgh.) -A2- AstjmE used intransitively is syn. with AjtmE , which see in two places, and tjm~E . (Msb, K.) ― -b2- AstjmE Als~ayolu The torrent collected itself together from every place. (S, Mgh, K.) ― -b3- AstjmE AlwaAdiY The valley flowed in every place thereof. (TA.) [See also 4, last signification.] ― -b4- AisotajomaEato lahu A^umuwruhu His affairs, or circumstances, all combined in a manner pleasing to him. (Mgh, K.) ― -b5- AstjmE Alfarasu jaroyFA (S, Mgh, K) The horse exerted all his force, or energy, in running: (K, TA:) the last word is here in the accus. case as a specificative. (Mgh.) You say also, AisotajomaEuwA lahumo , meaning They exerted [ all ] their strength, force, or energy, for fighting them: and hence, lakumo ↓ A_in~a Aln~aAsi qado jamaEuwA [app. meaning Verily the men, or people, have exerted all their strength for fighting you ]. (A, TA.) ― -b6- AstjmE Alqawomu The people, or company of men, all went away, not one of them remaining; like as one says of a valley flowing in every place thereof. (TA.) ― -b7- AstjmE Albaqolu The herbs, or leguminous plants, all dried up. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: inf. n. of 1. (S, &c.) [Hence,] yawomu AljamoEi The day of resurrection [when all mankind will be collected together]. (IDrd, K.) ― -b2- Also, without the article Al , A name of El-Muzdelifeh [between 'Arafát and Minè]; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) determinate, like EarafaAtu : (TA:) so called because people collect themselves there; (S, Msb;) or because Adam there met with Eve (Mgh, Msb) after they had fallen [from Paradise]: (TA:) [or, app., a name of the tract from 'Arafát to Minè inclusive of these two places: and hence,] yawomu jamoEK the day of 'Arafeh [when the pilgrims halt at Mount 'Arafát]: and A^ay~aAmu jamoEK the days of Minè. (IDrd, K.) ― -b3- As an inf. n. used as a subst., properly so termed, (S, * Mgh, Msb,) it also signifies A collection; a number together; an assembly; a company, troop, congregated or collective body, party, or group; a mass; syn. ↓ jamaAEapN , (S, Mgh, L, Msb, K,) of men; (S, L, K;) as also ↓ majomaEN (L, Msb, TA) and ↓ majomiEN (Msb) and ↓ majomaEapN (L, TA) and ↓ jamiyEN : (O, K:) but ↓ jamaAEapN is also used as signifying a collection, a number together, or an assemblage, of other things than men; [of beasts, as camels, horses and the like, bulls and cows, and antelopes, gazelles, &c., i. e. a herd, troop, or drove; of dogs, i. e. a pack; of sheep and goats, i. e. a flock; of birds, i. e. a flock or bevy; of bees, and locusts, &c., i. e. a swarm; ] and even of trees, and of plants; (L, TA;) it signifies a collection, or an assemblage, or aggregate, of any things, consisting of many and of few; (Msb;) [as also ↓ majomuwEN and ↓ majomaEN ;] a number, a plurality, and a multitude, of any things: (TA:) the pl. of jamoEN is jumuwEN . (S, Mgh, Msb, K.) ― -b4- And particularly, An army; a military force; (TA;) as also ↓ jamiyEN . (S, K.) Whence the phrase, in a trad., lahu sahomN jamoEN , [or, more probably, sahomu jamoEK ,] meaning For him or shall be, the like of an army's share of the spoil. (TA.) ― -b5- Also The plural of a thing [or word; i. e. a proper plural, according to the grammarians; and also applied by the lexicologists to a quasi-plural noun, which the grammarians distinguish by the terms Aisomu jamoEK and jamoEN lugawiY~N ]; and so ↓ jimaAEN , (S, K,) and ↓ jamiyEN , except that this last is what is termed AisomN laAzimN [app. meaning a subst. which does not govern another as its complement in the gen. case like as jamoEN and jimaAEN do, being thus likened to what is termed fiEolN laAzimN , i. e. an intransitive verb; so that you say of AlxibaA='u , for instance, AljamiyEu AlA^axobiyapu the plural is AlAxbyp ; for in this manner I always find it used when it has this signification, which is frequently the case in several of the older lexicons, and in some others; not jamiyEu AlxibaA='i AlA^axobiyapu ]; (TA;) [whereas] you say, [ jamoEu AlxibaA='i AlA^axobiyapu and] ↓ jimaAEu AlxibaA='i AlA^axobiyapu , (S, K,) i. e. the jamoE [or plural ] of AlxbA' is AlxibaA='i ; (K) for ↓ AljimaAEu is what comprises a number [of things]. (S, K.) See also this last word below. ― -b6- And see also the next paragraph, in three places. ― -b7- The worst sort of dates; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) because they are collected together and mixed, (Mgh, Msb,) from among the dates of fifty palm-trees: (Mgh:) and afterwards, by predominant usage, [ any ] bad dates: (Mgh, * Msb:) or a certain kind of dates (K, TA) mixed together, of several sorts, not in request, and not mixed but for their badness: (TA:) or it signifies, (Mgh, K,) or signifies also, (S, Msb,) palm-trees (As, S, Mgh, Msb, K) of any kind, (As, Mgh, Msb,) growing from the date-stones, (S, K,) of which the name is unknown. (As, S, Mgh, Msb, K.) ― -b8- Red gum; (Ibn-'Abbád, K;) [app. because collected and mixed with gum of lighter colour. ] ― -b9- The milk of any camel having her udder bound with the SiraAr [q. v.]; ([i. e. the milk that collects in the udder so bound; ] that of any camel not having her udder bound therewith is called fuwaAqN ;) as also ↓ jamiyEN . (K.)

A^ajomaAEN . (K.) You say, Darabotuhu bijumoEi kaf~iY I beat him, or struck him, with my fist. (S, Msb. *) And Darabuwhu biA^ajomaAEihimo They beat him, or struck him, with their [ clinched ] hands. sourceDefinition: is [a subst.] from AlAijotimaAEu , like as [its contr.] furoqapN is [ a subst.] from AlAAifotiraAqu : (Mgh:) and signifies A state of union, agreement, congruity, or congregation: or sociableness, socialness, familiarity, companionableness, companionship, fellowship, friendship, and amity: syn. A^ulofapN : as in the saying, A^adaAma A@ll~`hu jumoEapa maA bayonakumaA [ May God make permanent the state of union, &c., subsisting between you two ]. (Aboo-Sa'eed, K.) ― -b2- Hence, (Mgh,) yawomu AljumoEapi , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) the original form, (TA,) of the dial. of 'Okeyl; (Msb, TA;) and yawomu AljumuEapi , (S, Msb, K,) the most chaste form, (TA,) of the dial. of El-Hijáz; (Msb, TA;) and yawomu AljumaEapi , (Msb, K,) of the dial. of Benoo-Temeem; (Msb, TA;) and, in consequence of frequency of usage, AljumaEapu alone; (Mgh;) A well-known day; (K;) [ the day of the congregation; i. e. Friday; ] formerly called (TA) the day of AlEaruwbap : (S, TA:) called ywm AljmEp because of the congregating of the people thereon: (Msb:) Th asserts that the first who named it thus was Kaab Ibn-Lu-eí; and he is related to have said that it was thus called because Kureysh used to gather themselves together to Kuseí, [on that day,] in [the building called] daAru Aln~adowapi : (TA:) accord. to the R, Kaab Ibn-Lu-eí was the first who collected a congregation on the day of AlErwbp , which was not called AljmEp save since the coming of El-Islám; [or it was not generally thus called before El-Islám; for it is added,] and he was the first who named it AljmEp ; for Kureysh used to congregate to him on this day, and he used to preach to them, and to put them in mind of the mission of the apostle of God, informing them that he should be of his descendants, and bidding them to follow him and to believe in him: (TA:) or, as some say, it was thus called in the time of El-Islám because of their congregating [thereon] in the mosque: accord. to a trad., the Ansár named it thus, because of their congregating thereon: (TA:) or it was thus named because God collected thereon the materials of which Adam was created: (I 'Ab:) those who say AljumaEapu regard it as an epithet, meaning that this day collects men much; comparing it to humazapN and lumazapN and DuHakapN : (TA:) the pl. is jumaEN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and jumoEaAtN (Msb, K) and jumuEaAtN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and jumaEaAtN ; (Msb, K;) of which the last is pl. of jumaEapN , [as well as of jumoEapN , accord. to analogy,] but not so jumaEN (AHát) [nor either of the other pls. mentioned above]. ― -b3- In like manner you say SalaApN AljumoEapi [ The prayer of Friday ], and, in consequence of the frequency of usage, AljumoEapu alone. (Mgh.) ― -b4- AljumoEapu , with the m quiescent, is also a name for [ The week; i. e.] the days of the week [ collectively ]; of which the Arabs are said, by IAar, to have reckoned the Sabbath ( Als~abot [i. e. Saturday]) as the first, though they called Sunday the first of the days. (Msb.) ― -b5- jumoEapN is also syn. with majomuwEapN [meaning Things collected together; or a collection of things]; (K;) as in the phrase jumoEapN mino HaSFY [ a collection of pebbles ]. (TA.) ― -b6- You say also jumoEapN mino tamorK , meaning A handful of dates. (S, K.)

Wine is what comprises a number of sins: or] that in which sin is comprised, and known to be: the saying is a trad.: (TA:) or jimaAEu AlA_ivomi signifies the plurality ( jamoE ) of sins. (Msb.) Hence also the saying of El-Hasan El-Basree, Ait~aquwA h`*ihi AlA^ahowaA='a faA_in~a jimaAEahaA AlD~alaAlapu wamaEaAdahaA Aln~aAru [ Beware ye of these natural desires; for what they involve is error, and the place to which they lead is the fire of Hell]. (TA: in the L, wmyEAdhA .) And it is said in a trad., Had~ivoniY bikalimapK takuwnu jimaAEFA i. e. Tell me a saying comprising [virtually] a plurality of sayings. (TA.) [See a similar phrase below, voce jaAmiEN .] ― -b2- [Hence also,] buromapN jimaAEN A stonecooking-pot of the largest size: (Ks, L:) or qidorN jimaAEN , and ↓ jaAmiEapN , (S, K, TA,) a cooking-pot that comprises a slaughtered camel; or, accord. to the A, that comprises a sheep or goat: (TA:) or a great cooking-pot; (S, K;) as also ↓ jaAmiEN : (Sgh, K:) pl. [most probably of this last] jumoEN [like as buzolN is pl. of baAzilN , &c.]. (K.) ― -b3- You say also, fulaAnN jimaAEN libaniY fulaAnK Such a one is an object of resort for his counsel and authority to the sons of such a one. (TA.) -A2- [See also 3.]

definition: In a state of collection, congregation, or union;
sourceDefinition: In a state of collection, congregation, or union; being together; met together; [as also ↓ mujotamiEN ;] contr. of mutafar~iqN . (S, K.) You say qawomN jamiyEN A people, or number of men, in a state of collection, &c.; being together; met together; syn. ↓ mujotamiEuwna : (TA:) and in like manner, ↓ A_ibilN jam~aAEapN Camels in a state of collection; &c. (TA.) ― -b2- [ All, or the whole, of any things or thing.] See A^ajomaEu , last sentence. ― -b3- [As an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant,] A tribe [or any number of men ] in a state of collection, congregation, or union; being together; met together; syn. ↓ HaY~N mujotamiEN . (S, K.) See also jamoEN , in four places. ― -b4- A man compact, or compressed, or contracted, in make, or frame: ( Alxaloqi ↓ mujotamiEu ;) strong; who has not become decrepit nor infirm. (TA.) ― -b5- rajulN jamiyEN All~aA^omapi A man having his arms, or weapons, collected together. (TA.) ― -b6- rajulN jamiyEu Alr~aA^oYi , and ↓ mujotamiEuhu , A man of right, not disordered or unsettled, opinion, or judgment, or counsel. (AHeyth.)

definition: Anything of which the several component parts are collected, brought, gathered, or drawn, together.
sourceDefinition: Anything of which the several component parts are collected, brought, gathered, or drawn, together. (IDrd, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] as an epithet, applied to a woman, it means Short. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] jum~aAEN Alv~uray~aA The cluster of the Pleiades: (IDrd:) or persons who collect together for the rain of the Pleiades, which is the rain called AlwasomiY~ , looking for the fruitfulness and herbage resulting from it. (IAar.) ― -b4- And jum~aAEu Aln~aAsi A medley, or mixed or promiscuous multitude or collection, of men, or people, (S, Msb, K,) of various tribes; (S, K;) as also jum~aAEN alone: (TA:) or the latter, people scattered, or in a state of dispersion. (Ham p. 302.) ― -b5- jum~aAEN also signifies The place [either properly or tropically] which comprises the origin of anything; (K, TA;) the source of descent or extraction of people; and hence applied by I 'Ab to main tribes from which other tribes are derived; or, as some say, used by him as meaning various classes of men, such as are termed A^awozaAE and A^awo$aAb . (TA.) ― -b6- [And The main, or most essential, part of a thing. Thus,] jum~aAEu jasadi AlA_inosaAni means The head of the man. (TA.) ― -b7- jum~aAEu Alt~amori The contraction ( tajam~uE ) of the envelopes of the flowers of dates, in one place, upon [ the germs of ] the fruit, or produce, thereof. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of 1; Collecting; &c.] ― -b2- AljaAmiEu one of the names of God; meaning The Collector of the created beings for the day of reckoning: or, as some say, the Combiner of things of similar natures and of things of contrary natures, in existence. (IAth.) ― -b3- The belly; [because it collects what passes from the stomach;] of the dial. of El-Yemen. (TA.) ― -b4- Also, (Msb,) or Almasojidu AljaAmiEu , (S, K,) [ The congregational mosque; ] the mosque in which the [ congregational ] prayers of Friday are performed; because it collects the people for a certain time; (Msb;) and you may also say, masojidu AljaAmiEi , meaning masojidu Alyawomi AljaAmiEi , (S, K,) like as you say AlHaq~u Alyaqiynu and Haq~u Alyaqiyni , [the latter] as meaning Haq~u Al$~aYo'i Alyaqiyni ; for it is not allowable to prefix a noun to another of the same meaning except with this kind of subaudition; or, accord. to Fr, the Arabs used to do so because of the difference of the two words themselves: (S:) or msjd AljAmE is a mistake: (K:) so says Lth; but all others allow it; for the Arabs prefix a subst. to another signifying the same thing, and also to its epithet, as in the phrases in the Kur diynu Alqay~imapi [ch. xcviii. v. 4] and waEoda AlS~idoqi [ch. xlvi. v. 15]: (Az, TA:) [pl. jawaAmiEu .] ― -b5- miSorN jaAmiEN [ A great town comprising a large population; a comprehensive great town ]. (Msb in art. mdn [where it is given as the explanation of madiynapN ]; and K in art. qrY [where it is less properly given as the explanation of qaroyapN ].) ― -b6- qidorN jaAmiEN and jaAmiEapN : see jimaAEN ― -b7- AimoraA^apN jAmiEN : see the paragraph commencing with AljumoEu ; last signification. ― -b8- A^ataAnN jaAmiEN A she-ass pregnant when beginning to be so. (S, O, K.) ― -b9- ↓ jaAmiEapN A [ collar of the kind called ] gul~ ; (S, K;) because it collects together the two hands to the neck: (S:) pl. jawaAmiEu . (TA.) ― -b10- A^amorN jaAmiEN An affair that collects people together: or, as Er-Rághib says, a momentous affair, on account of which people collect themselves together; as though the affair itself collected them. (TA.) [Similar to this is the saying,] AlS~alaApu jaAmiEapN likul~i Aln~aAsi Prayer is a collector of all people. (Msb.) ― -b11- It is said of Mohammad, (Msb,) kaAna yatakal~amu bijawaAmiEi Alkalimi He used to speak comprehensive but concise language; language conveying many meanings in few words. (Msb, K. [In the CK, Alklm is omitted.]) And hence the saying of 'Omar Ibn-'Abd-el-'Azeez, Eajibotu limano laAHana Aln~aAsa kayofa laA yaEorifu jawaAmiEa Alkalimi , meaning [ I wonder at him who vies with men in endeavouring to show his superiority of intelligence, ] how it is that he does not [ know the way to ] confine himself to conciseness, and abstain from superfluity, of speech. (TA.) In like manner, (TA,) it is said in a trad., A^uwtiytu jawaAmiEa Alkalimi , meaning I have had communicated to me the Kur-án, (K, TA,) in which many meanings are comprised in a few words. (TA.) AljawaAmiEu mina Ald~uEaA='i , also, signifies Prayers, or supplications, combining petitions for good and right objects of desire with praise of God and with the general prescribed observances proper to the case. (TA.) You say also, AlmaHaAmidi ↓ Hamidotu A@ll~`ha bimajaAmiEi I praised God with words comprising various forms of praise. (Msb.) [See also jimaAEN .] ― -b12- rajulN jaAmiEN A man who combines such qualities that he is suited to hardship and to easiness of circumstances. (As. T in art. Adm .) And rajulN jaAmiEN liloxayori (T and M and K in art. Am ) A man combining all kinds of good qualities. (TK in that art.) ― -b13- daAb~apN jaAmiEN A beast fit for the A_ikaAf and the saroj [i. e. for the saddle of either of the kinds thus called ]. (Sgh, K.) ― -b14- jamalN jaAmiEN , and naAqapN jaAmiEapN , (K,) accord. to ISh, (TA,) A hecamel, and a she-camel, that fails of putting forth the tooth called nAb at the time expected; expl. by A^axolafaA buzuwlFA : but this is not said except after four years: (K:) so in the copies of the K; but correctly, accord. to the O and TS, this is not said after four years, [app. reckoned from the usual time of bzwl , for this is in the ninth year, or, sometimes, in the eighth,] without the exceptive particle. (TA.)

(TA.) ― -b4- Also, (Msb,) or Almasojidu AljaAmiEu , (S, K,) [ The congregational mosque; ] the mosque in which the [ congregational ] prayers of Friday are performed; because it collects the people for a certain time; (Msb;) and you may also say, masojidu AljaAmiEi , meaning masojidu Alyawomi AljaAmiEi , (S, K,) like as you say AlHaq~u Alyaqiynu and Haq~u Alyaqiyni , [the latter] as meaning Haq~u Al$~aYo'i Alyaqiyni ; for it is not allowable to prefix a noun to another of the same meaning except with this kind of subaudition; or, accord. to Fr, the Arabs used to do so because of the difference of the two words themselves: (S:) or msjd AljAmE is a mistake: (K:) so says Lth; but all others allow it; for the Arabs prefix a subst. to another signifying the same thing, and also to its epithet, as in the phrases in the Kur diynu Alqay~imapi [ch. xcviii. v. 4] and waEoda AlS~idoqi [ch. xlvi. v. 15]: (Az, TA:) [pl. jawaAmiEu .] ― -b5- miSorN jaAmiEN [ A great town comprising a large population; a comprehensive great town ]. (Msb in art. mdn [where it is given as the explanation of madiynapN ]; and K in art. qrY [where it is less properly given as the explanation of qaroyapN ].) ― -b6- qidorN jaAmiEN and jaAmiEapN : see jimaAEN ― -b7- AimoraA^apN jAmiEN : see the paragraph commencing with AljumoEu ; last signification. ― -b8- A^ataAnN jaAmiEN A she-ass pregnant when beginning to be so. (S, O, K.) ― -b9- ↓ jaAmiEapN A [ collar of the kind called ] gul~ ; (S, K;) because it collects together the two hands to the neck: (S:) pl. jawaAmiEu . (TA.) ― -b10- A^amorN jaAmiEN An affair that collects people together: or, as Er-Rághib says, a momentous affair, on account of which people collect themselves together; as though the affair itself collected them. (TA.) [Similar to this is the saying,] AlS~alaApu jaAmiEapN likul~i Aln~aAsi Prayer is a collector of all people. (Msb.) ― -b11- It is said of Mohammad, (Msb,) kaAna yatakal~amu bijawaAmiEi Alkalimi He used to speak comprehensive but concise language; language conveying many meanings in few words. (Msb, K. [In the CK, Alklm is omitted.]) And hence the saying of 'Omar Ibn-'Abd-el-'Azeez, Eajibotu limano laAHana Aln~aAsa kayofa laA yaEorifu jawaAmiEa Alkalimi , meaning [ I wonder at him who vies with men in endeavouring to show his superiority of intelligence, ] how it is that he does not [ know the way to ] confine himself to conciseness, and abstain from superfluity, of speech. (TA.) In like manner, (TA,) it is said in a trad., A^uwtiytu jawaAmiEa Alkalimi , meaning I have had communicated to me the Kur-án, (K, TA,) in which many meanings are comprised in a few words. (TA.) AljawaAmiEu mina Ald~uEaA='i , also, signifies Prayers, or supplications, combining petitions for good and right objects of desire with praise of God and with the general prescribed observances proper to the case. (TA.) You say also, AlmaHaAmidi ↓ Hamidotu A@ll~`ha bimajaAmiEi I praised God with words comprising various forms of praise. (Msb.) [See also jimaAEN .] ― -b12- rajulN jaAmiEN A man who combines such qualities that he is suited to hardship and to easiness of circumstances. (As. T in art. Adm .) And rajulN jaAmiEN liloxayori (T and M and K in art. Am ) A man combining all kinds of good qualities. (TK in that art.) ― -b13- daAb~apN jaAmiEN A beast fit for the A_ikaAf and the saroj [i. e. for the saddle of either of the kinds thus called ]. (Sgh, K.) ― -b14- jamalN jaAmiEN , and naAqapN jaAmiEapN , (K,) accord. to ISh, (TA,) A hecamel, and a she-camel, that fails of putting forth the tooth called nAb at the time expected; expl. by A^axolafaA buzuwlFA : but this is not said except after four years: (K:) so in the copies of the K; but correctly, accord. to the O and TS, this is not said after four years, [app. reckoned from the usual time of bzwl , for this is in the ninth year, or, sometimes, in the eighth,] without the exceptive particle. (TA.)

definition: [ Collecting, comprising, or containing, a greater, or the greatest, number or quantity;
sourceDefinition: [ Collecting, comprising, or containing, a greater, or the greatest, number or quantity; more, or most, comprehensive. Of its usage in a superlative sense, the following are exs.]. A_i*aA A^axa*a $aAhida zuwrK baEava bihi A_ilaY Als~uwqi A^ajomaEa maA kaAna [ When he took a false witness, he sent him to the market when it comprised, or contained, the greatest number of people]: AjmE being here in the accus. case as a denotative of state with respect to the swq : and the reason why kAnt is not here said [instead of kAn ] is that swq is sometimes masc. (Mgh.) And AifoEalo maA huwa A^ajomaEu liA^uSuwli AlA^aHokaAmi [ Do thou that which is most comprehensive in relation to the principles of the ordinances applying to the case]. (Msb in art. HwT .) -A2- [As a simple epithet, Entire, complete, or whole: fem. jamoEaA='u . You say,] bahiymapN jamoEaA='u A beast free from defects, entire in all its limbs or members, without mutilation, and without cauterization; (TA;) a beast from the body of which nothing has gone. (S, K.) ― -b2- naAqapN jamoEaA='u [may sometimes have the like meaning: or,] accord. to IAar, (TA,) A she-camel extremely aged, (K, TA,) so that her teeth have become short, and almost gone. (TA.) -A3- It is also a sing. having the meaning of a pl., (S, K,) without any proper sing. of its own: (S:) its pl. is A^ajomaEuwna : and its fem. is jamoEaA='u : (S, K:) and the pl. of this last is jumaEu , though by rule it should be formed by the addition of A and t to the sing., like as the pl. of A^ajomaEu is formed by the addition of w and n ; (S;) the original form from which jumaEu is changed being jamoEaAwaAtN ; or it is jamaAEaY ; it is not jumoEN , because A^ajomaEu is not an epithet, like as A^aHomaru is, of which the pl. is HumorN ; (L;) for it is determinate, though of the measure of an epithet, which is indeterminate; (AAF;) and though it is in concordance with the noun which precedes it, like an epithet, it is shown to be not an epithet by its not having a broken pl.: (L:) it is a simple corroborative; (S, K;) and so are A^ajomaEuwna and jamoEaA='u and jumaEu ; not used as an inchoative nor as an enunciative nor as the agent of a verb nor as the objective complement of a verb, like as are some other corroboratives, such as nafosuhu and Eayonuhu and kul~uhu . (S.) You say, A^axa*otu Haq~iY A^ajomaEa [ I took my right, or due, all of it, or altogether ]: and rA^ayotu Aln~isowapa jumaEa [ I saw the women, all of them, or all together ]: the last word in this and similar cases being imperfectly declinable, and determinate word: (Sudot;, TA:) and jaAw^uwA A^ajomaEuwna [ They came, all of them, or all together ]: and raA^ayotuhumo A^ajomaEiyna [ I saw them, all of them, or all together ]: and mararotu bihimo A^ajomaEiyna [ I passed by them, all of them, or all together ]. (Msb.) Fr mentions the phrases, A^aEojabaniY AlqaSoru A^ajomaEa [ The palace pleased me, all of it, or altogether ], and Ald~aAru jamoEaA='a [ The house, all of it, or altogether ], with the accus. case, as denotative of state; but does not allow A^ajomaEuwna nor jumaEu to be used otherwise than as corroboratives: IDrst, however, allows A^ajomaEiyna to be used as a denotative of state; and this is correct; and accord. to both these ways is related the trad., faSal~uwA juluwsFA A^ajomaEiyna and A^ajomaEuwna [ And pray ye sitting, all of you, or all together ]; though some make AjmEyn [here] to be a corroborative of a pronoun understood in the accus. case, as though the speaker said, A^aEoniykumo A^ajomaEiyna [ I mean you, all of you, or all together ]: (K in art. btE :) or AjmEyn in this case is a corruption committed by the relaters in the first age; and he is in error who says that it is in the accus. case as a denotative of state, for corroboratives are determinate, and the denotative of state is literally or virtually indeterminate. (Msb.) [Respecting the usage of this corroborative together with others similar to it, see A^abotaEu .] You say also, jaAw^uwA biA^ajomaEihimo , and biA^ajomuEihimo , with damm to the m , [ They came, all of them, or all together, ] (S, Msb, K,) the latter mentioned by ISk. (Msb.) And you say, qabaDotu AlmaAla A^ajomaEahu [ I took, or received, the property, all of it, or altogether ]. (Msb.) And ↓ jamiyEN , also, is used as a corroborative: (S, Msb:) as in the saying jaAw^uwA jamiyEFA , meaning They came, all of them: (S:) and qabaDotu AlmaAla jamiyEahu , like A^ajomaEahu [explained above]: (Msb:) and jamiyEapF occurs as its fem.; but this is extr. (TA.)

definition: and majomiEN , (S, Msb, K,) the latter anomalous, like ma$oriqN and magoribN &c.
sourceDefinition: and majomiEN , (S, Msb, K,) the latter anomalous, like ma$oriqN and magoribN &c., (TA,) A place of collecting, and the like: (S, Msb, * K:) [pl. majaAmiEu ] [Hence,] majomaEu AlbaHorayoni , in the Kur [xviii. 59], means The place where the two seas meet. (Bd.) And in like manner, where it is said in a trad., fDaraba biyadihi majomaEa bayona EunuqiY wakatifiY , [in which maA seems to have been dropped by the copyist between mjmE and byn ,] the meaning is, [ And he struck with his hand ] the place where my neck and my shoulder-blade meet. (TA.) [Hence also the phrase majaAmiEu AlmaHaAmidi , explained above: see jaAmiEN , near the end of the paragraph. And majaAmiEu AlA^umuwri , meaning The concurrences of affairs, or of circumstances, or of events. ] ― -b2- A place in which people collect, assemble, or congregate: (Msb, * TA:) and [in like manner,] ↓ majomaEapN signifies an assembly-room; a sitting room in which people assemble: (TA:) [pl. of both majaAmiEu .] You say, h`*aA AlkalaAmu A^awolaju fiY AlmasaAmiEi waA^ajowalu fiY AlmajaAmiEi [ This language, or discourse, is more, or most, penetrating into the ears, and more, or most, circulating in the places of assembly ]. (TA.) ― -b3- See also jamoEN , as syn. with jamaAEapN , in two places; and see 10, first sentence. ― -b4- [The whole of anything, considered as the place in which the several parts thereof are collected: see an instance voce xuf~N : and see also mujotamaEN .]

definition: A year of dearth, drought, sterility, or unfruitfulness: (Ks, K:) because it is an occasion of people's collecting together in the place where herbage, or plenty, is found.

definition: [signifying He, or it, was, or became, loved, beloved, an object of love, affected, liked, or approved, is originally Habuba or Habiba ].
sourceDefinition: [signifying He, or it, was, or became, loved, beloved, an object of love, affected, liked, or approved, is originally Habuba or Habiba ]. You say, Hab~a A_ilaY~a h`*aA Al$~aYo'u , [aor. or ,] inf. n. Hub~N , This thing was, or became, an object of love to me. (K. [The meaning is there indicated, but not expressed. In the CK, Al$~aY'a is erroneously put for Al$~aYo'u .]) And Habubotu A_ilayohi I became loved, beloved, or an object of love, to him: [said to be] the only instance of its kind except $arurotu and labubotu . (K.) And maA kunota HabiybFA walaqado Habibota , with kesr, Thou wast not loved, and thou hast become loved. (S.) See also 5. ― -b2- Hab~a , formed from Habuba , by making the former b quiescent and incorporating it into the latter, is also a verb of praise [signifying Beloved, lovely, pleasing, charming, or excellent, is he, or it]; (TA;) and so Hub~a , [which is more common,] formed from the same, by incorporating the former b into the latter after transferring the dammeh of the former to the H . (ISk, S, TA.) A poet says, wazaAdahu kalafFA fiY AlHub~i A^ano manaEato waHab~a $ayoy^FA AlaY AlAnosaAni maA muniEaA [ And her denying increased his devotion in love: for lovely, as a thing, to man, is that which is denied ]. (TA.) And Sá'ideh says, hajarato gaDuwbu waHab~a mano yatajan~abu waEadato EawaAdK duwna waloyika ta$oEibu [ Ghadoob hath forsaken thee, ( and lovely is the person who withdraweth far away, ) and obstacles in the way of thy drawing near have occurred to separate thee and her]. (S, TA.) [See also Hab~a*aA , below.] ― -b3- [Both are also verbs of wonder.] You say, Hab~a bifulaAnK , (As, S, and so in copies of the K,) and Hub~a , (I 'Ak p. 236, [where both forms are mentioned as correct,] and so in the CK,) How beloved, or lovely, &c., is such a one (As, S, K) to me! (As, S.) [See also 4.] A'Obeyd and Fr read this Hab~a , saying that it means Habuba bflAn , and that the former b is rendered quiescent by the suppression of its dammeh, and incorporated into the latter. (S, * TA.) -A2- See also 4, in two places. -A3- Also Hab~a , [aor., accord. to analogy, ,] He stood still, stopped, or paused. (K.) -A4- And Hub~a , with damm, He was fatigued, or tired. (K.)

definition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_iHobaAbN ; (KL;) and ↓ Hab~ahu , (S,) first pers. Hababotuhu , (Msb, K,) aor. , which is anomalous, (S, Msb, K,) the regular aor. being , which is unused, (Msb,) [said to be] the only instance of a trans. verb whose second and third radical letters are the same having the measure yafoEilu as that of its aor. without having also the measure yafoEulu , (S,) and therefore by some disapproved, as not chaste, and disallowed by Az, though he allows the pass. form Hub~a , (TA,) inf. n. Hub~N , (K,) or this is a simple subst., (Msb,) and Hib~N ; (K;) and [↓ Hab~ahu ,] first pers. Habibotuhu , aor. ; and ↓ HaAb~hu , inf. n. HibaAbN , of the dial. of Hudheyl; (Msb;) and ↓ AstHb~hu ; (Msb, K;) signify the same; (S, Msb, K;) He loved, affected, liked, approved, or took pleasure in, him, or it: (A, K, and KL in explanation of the first and last:) he held him, or esteemed him, as a friend: (KL in explanation of the first and last:) or AisotiHobaAbN signifies the esteeming [a person or thing] good: (S:) and the preferring, or choosing, [a person or thing,] as also A_iHobaAbN : (KL:) and AstHb~hu EalaY gayorihi means he loved, or esteemed, him, or it, above another, or others; preferred him, or it, to another, or others. (K, A, * TA.) maA A^aHabotu *`lika , in the dial. of the tribe of Suleym, is for mA A^aHobabotuhu [ I loved not, or liked not, that ]; like Zanotu for Zananotu , and Zalotu and Zilotu for Zalilotu . (Lh, TA.) [ A^uHib~u A^ano yakwuna ka*aA may be rendered I would that it were thus, or that such a thing were. ] It is said of Ohod, in a trad., huwa jabalN yuHib~unaA wanuHib~uhu , meaning It is a mountain whose inhabitants love us, and whose inhabitants we love: or it may mean we love the mountain itself, because it is in the land of people whom we love. (IAth, TA.) And one says fiY saAEapK yuHib~uhaA AlT~aEaAmu for yuHab~u fiyhaA [ In an hour, or a time, in which food is loved, or liked ]. (TA.) ― -b2- maA A^aHab~ahu A_ilaY~a i. q. Hab~a bihi [ How beloved, lovely, pleasing, charming, or excellent, is he, or it, to me! ]; (As, S, K, * TA;) and so A^aHobibo A_ilaY~a bihi . (A, TA.) [De Sacy, in his Gram. Ar., sec. ed., ii. 221, mentions the saying, maA A^aHab~a Almuw^omina ll~`hi wamaA A^aHab~ahu A_ilaY A@ll~`hi , as meaning How greatly does the believer love God! and how great an object of love is he to God! ] -A2- AHb~ , (S, K,) inf. n. as above, (S,) also signifies He (a camel) kneeled and lay down, and would not spring up: (K:) or was restive: or kneeled and lay down: (S:) or was afflicted by a fracture, or disease, and would not move from his place until cured, or remained there until he died: (AZ, S, K:) or became jaded: (TA: [agreeably with this last explanation the act. part. n. is rendered in the S and K on the authority of Th:]) or was at the point of death, by reason of violent disease, and therefore kneeled and lay down, and could not be roused. (AHeyth, TA.) Accord. to AO, A^aHobabotu Hub~a Alxayori Eano *ikori rab~iY [in the Kur xxxviii. 31] means I have stuck to the ground, on account of my love of the horses, [lit., of good things, ] and so been diverted from prayer, until the time of prayer has passed: (TA:) by Alxyr is meant Alxayol . (Jel.) -A3- Also He became in a state of recovery from his disease. (K.) -A4- And It (seed-produce) had, bore, or produced, grain. (S, K.)

sourceDefinition: Love; affection; syn. wud~N , (A,) or widaAdN ; (K;) inclination of the nature, or natural disposition, towards a thing that pleases, or delights; (Kull p. 165;) contr. of bugoDN : (Mgh, TA:) Hub~N and ↓ Hib~N and ↓ Hub~apN [this being said in the S to be syn. with Hub~N and in the K to be syn. with maHab~apN , and it is used as an inf. n. in an ex. cited voce daAHN in art. dwH ,] and ↓ HubaAbN (S, K) and ↓ HibaAbN (K) and ↓ maHab~apN (S) signify the same; (S, K;) i. e., as above. (K.) The degrees of Hub~ are as follow: first, hawFY , the “ inclining of the soul, or mind; ” also applied to the “ object of love itself: ” then, EalaAqapN , “ love cleaving to the heart; ” so termed because of the heart's cleaving to the object of love: then, kalafN , “ violent, or intense, love; ” from kulofapN signifying “ difficulty, or distress, or affliction: ” then, Ei$oqN , [“ amorous desire; ” or “ passionate love; ”] in the S, “ excess of love; ” and in the language of the physicians, “ a kind of melancholy: ” then, $agafN , “ ardour of love, accompanied by a sensation of pleasure; ” like lawoEapN and laAEijN ; the former of which is “ ardour of love; ” and the latter, “ ardent love: ” then, jawFY , “ inward love; ” and “ violence of amorous desire, ” or “ of grief, or sorrow: ” then, tatay~umN , “ a state of enslavement by love: ” then tabolN , “ lovesickness: ” then, walahN , “ distraction, or loss of reason, in love: ” and then, huyaAmN “ a state of wandering about at random in consequence of overpowering love. ” (Kull ubi suprà.) [Accord. to the Msb, it is a simple subst.: but accord. to the K, an inf. n.; and hence,] Hub~FA limaA A^aHobabotumo , meaning A^uHib~u Hub~FA [ I love with loving, i. e. much, what ye have loved ]. (Har p. 186.) Hence the phrase, wakaraAmapF ↓ naEamo waHub~apF [ Yea; and with love and honour will I do what thou requirest: or for the sake of the love and honour that I bear thee: or Hb~p may be here used for Hub~FA to assimilate it in termination to krAmp : see what follows]. (S, TA.) Hence also the saying of Abu-l-' Atà EsSindee, fawaA@ll~`hi maA A^adoriY waA_in~iY laSaAdiqN A^adaA='N EaraAniY mino HubaAbiki A^amo siHoru [ And by God, I know not ( and indeed I am speaking truth ) whether disease have befallen me in consequence of love of thee, or enchantment ]: (S, TA:) but IB says that the reading best known is ↓ mino HibaAbiki ; and that HibAb , here, may be an inf. n. of HaAbabotuhu ; or it may be pl. of Hub~N , like as Ei$A$N is of Eu$~N ; (TA;) or it may be an inf. n. of Hababotuhu : some also read ↓ mino HabaAbiki , with fet-h to the H , said to mean on account of the love of thee, and of the main amount thereof: (Ham p. 26:) and some read mino janaAbiki “ from thy part ” [or “ from thee ”]. (TA.) ― -b2- See also HabiybN . -A2- Also a Persian word, arabicized, (AHát, S, Msb,) from xunob , (AHát, TA,) [or xubo or xuPo ,] i. q. xaAbiyapN , (S, Msb,) A jar, (K, MF,) whether large or small, used for preparing wine: (MF:) or a large jar: (K:) or one for water: (IDrd, TA:) or the four pieces of wood upon which is placed a two-handled, or two-eared, jar: (K, TA: [in the CK, by a misplacement of words, this last signification is assigned to HabaAb :]) pl. [of pauc.] A^aHobaAbN (K) and [of mult.] HibaAbN and HibabapN . (S, Msb, K.) From this last signification is [said to be] derived the phrase Hub~FA wakaraAmapF [pronounced Hub~FA wakaraAmaho , lit. A jarstand and a cover will I give thee, or the like], krAmp signifying the “ cover ” of a jar, (K, TA,) whether of wood or of baked clay. (TA.) [If this be the true derivation, the phrase may have originated from a person's asking of another the loan or gift of a jar, and the latter's replying “ Yea; and I will give thee a jar-stand and a cover; ” meaning “ I will do what thou requirest, and more: ” but this phrase is now, and perhaps was in early times, generally used, agreeably with the more common significations of the two words, in the sense assigned above to the phrase Hub~apF wakaraAmapF .]

sourceDefinition: : see Hub~N . ― -b2- HabaAbuka Thine utmost: (Msb:) or the utmost of thy power: (S:) or the utmost of thy love: or, of thine endeavour ( jahodika [like juhaAdaAka and HumaAdaAka and quSaAraAka and gunaAmaAka and nuEaAmaAka ]). (K. [In the CK juhodika .]) You say, HabaAbuka ka*aA , (K,) and HbAbk A^ano tafoEala *`lika , (S, Msb, * TA,) and HbAbk A^ano yakuwna *`lika , (TA,) Thine utmost, (Msb,) or the utmost of thy power, (S,) or of thy love, or of thine endeavour, (K,) will be such a thing, (K,) and thy doing that, (S, Msb, * TA,) and that event's taking place. (TA.) -A2- Also, and ↓ HababN and ↓, The main body, the mass, or bulk, or greater part or portion, of water, (S, K,) and of sand, (K,) and of [the beverage called] nabiy* : but it is said that the third word applies particularly to water: (TA:) or the first signifies the streaks, or lines, of water, (As, K, TA,) resembling variegated work: (As, TA:) or the waves of water that follow one another: (TA:) or the bubbles (S, A, K) of water, (S, K,) or of wine, (A, TA,) that float upon the surface; (S, A, K;) as also the second (AHn, A) and the third: (AHn, TA:) [it is a coll. gen. n., in this sense, of which the n. un. is with p :] accord. to IDrd, Hbbu AlmaA='i and HbAbu AlmaA='i signify takas~aruhu [app. meaning the ripple, or broken surface, of water, such as is seen when it is slightly fretted by wind, and when it flows over uneven ground]. (TA.) Tirota biEubaAbihaA wafuzota biHabaAbihaA , in a trad. of 'Alee, relating to Aboo-Bekr, is explained as meaning Thou hast outrun others, and attained to the place where the flood of El-Islám collects, and reached the first [ springs ] thereof, and drunk the purest of it, and become possessor of its excellencies: [this is the only explanation of it that I have found:] but it is also otherwise explained. (Hr and others, TA in art. Eb .) ― -b2- HabaAbN also signifies (tropical:) Dew-drops; (A;) the dew (IAth, K) that is on trees &c. in the evening. (IAth, TA.) It is said in a trad., of the inhabitants of Paradise, that their food shall turn into a sweat like HbAb Almsok , by which is meant Musky dew: or, perhaps, musky bubbles. (IAth, TA.)

HubabN : (K:) the fem. of HabiybN is with p ; (Msb, K;) and so is that of ↓ maHobuwbN , (K, TA,) [and that of ↓ muHab~N ,] and that of ↓ Hib~N : (TA:) the pl. of HabiybN is A^aHib~aA='u , instead of HubabaA='u , which would be the reg. pl. but for the repetition of the b ; and the pl. of HabiybapN is HabaAy^ibu : (Msb:) the pl. of ↓ Hib~N is A^aHobaAbN [a pl. of pauc.] and Hib~aAnN (K) and Hub~aAnN (MF) and HubuwbN and HibabapN and ↓ Hub~N , which last is rare ( EaziyzN ) [as a pl.], or is a quasi-pl. n. definition: , (K,) or A^abuw HubaAHibK , (S,) [ A kind of fire-fly;
sourceDefinition: , (K,) or A^abuw HubaAHibK , (S,) [ A kind of fire-fly; ] a fly that flies in the night, (K,) resembling fire, (S,) emitting rays like a lamp: (K:) AHn says that HbAHb and AbwHbAHb were both unknown to him, and that nothing respecting them had been heard by him from the Arabs; but that some people asserted the insect thus called to be the yaraAE , a moth that, when it flies by night, no person not knowing it would doubt to be a spark of fire: Aboo-Tálib says, as on the authority of Arabs of the desert, that HbAHb is the name of a flying thing longer than the common fly, and slender, that flies between sunset and nightfall, resembling a spark of fire: (TA:) or, accord. to As, it is a flying thing, like the common fly, with a wing that becomes red; when it flies appearing at a distance like a lighted piece of fire-wood. (Har p. 500.) naAru AlHubaAHibi (S, K) and naAruA^abiY HubaAHibK and simply AlHubaAHibu (S) mean The fire of the fly above mentioned: or of El-Hobáhib or Aboo-Hobáhib: (TA:) [for] El-Hobáhib, (S,) or Aboo-Hobáhib, (K,) is said to have been a niggardly man, who never lighted any but a faint fire, fearing to attract guests, so that his fire became proverbial. (S, K.) El-Kumeyt says, describing swords, yaraY Alr~aAw^uwna biAl$~afaraAti minohaA kanaAri A^abiY HubaAHiba waAlZ~ubiynaA [ The beholders see, in the sides of the blades thereof, and the extremities, the semblance of the fire of the fire-fly ]: (S:) here the poet has made HbAHb imperfectly decl., regarding it as a fem. [proper] name [of the fly above mentioned]. (TA.) Or nArAlHbAHb (S, K) and simply AlHbAHb (S) signify The fire that is struck by a horse's hoofs: (Fr, S:) or the sparks of fire that are made to fly forth in the air by the collision of stones: or the sparks that fall from the pieces of wood that are used for producing fire [ by means of friction ]: (K:) or they are derived from HaboHabapN , (IAar, K,) signifying “ weakness, ” (IAar, TA,) [and their meaning is faint fire. ] ― -b2- A^um~u HubaAHibK A flying insect resembling the [ species of locust called ] junodab , (K, * TA,) spotted with yellow and green: when people see it, they say, bar~idiY yaA HubaAHibu [ Spread forth thy wings ( burodayoki ), hobáhib ]; whereupon it spreads its two wings, which are adorned with red and yellow. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , meaning HabiybN , as in the phrase Hab~a*aA AlA^amoru [ Loved, beloved, affected, loved, or approved, is the thing, or affair; or lovely, charming, or excellent, is it ]; (K;) and in Hab~a*aA zayodN [ Loved, beloved, &c., is Zeyd ]; (S;) is composed of Hab~a , (Sb, Fr, S, K,) a verb of praise, in the pret. form, invariable, originally Habuba , (Fr, S,) and *aA , (Sb, Fr, S, K,) its agent, (S,) which together constitute it a single word, (Sb, S, K,) a noun, (Sb, K,) or occupying the place of a noun, (S,) governing the noun [particularized by praise] that follows it in the nom. case; (Sb, S, K;) the place that it occupies in construction making it virtually in the nom. case as an inchoative, and the noun that follows it being its enunciative: (S:) [but see what follows.] It is used in the same manner as a prov.; (Sb, K;) [i. e., it is not altered to agree in number or gender with the noun particularized by praise, which follows it;] remaining the same when used in the dual and pl. and fem. sense; so that one says, Hb~*A zayodN and Alz~ayodaAni and Alz~ayoduwna and hinodN and A^anota and A^anotumaA and A^anotumo [&c.]; (Ibn-Keysán, TA;) and Hb~*A A@moraA^apN , not Hab~a*ihi AlmaroA^apu ; (Sb, S, K; *) which shows that the noun that follows it may not be regarded as a substitute for *A : (S:) [but see what follows.] It is allowable, but bad, to say, zayodN Hab~a*aA . (TA.) [There are, however, various opinions respecting Hb~*A and the noun that follows it.] Some hold that Hb~*A is a noun, composed of Hab~a and *A , and is an inchoative, and that the noun particularized by praise is its enunciative; or that the former is an enunciative, and the latter an inchoative, reversing the usual order: others hold that Hab~a is a verb in the pret. form; and *A , its agent; and that the noun particularized by praise may be an inchoative, of which Hb~*A is the enunciative; or it may be an enunciative of which the inchoative is suppressed, so that Hb~*A zayodN is for Hb~*A huwa zayodN [ Loved, or beloved, &c., is this person: he is Zeyd ], or Hb~*A AlmamoduwHu zayodN [ loved, &c., is this person: the person praised is Zeyd ]: others hold that Hb~*A is a pret. verb, composed of Hab~a and *A , and that the noun following it is its agent; but this is the weakest of opinions: one also says, in dispraise, laAHab~a*aA zayodN . (I 'Ak p. 235.)

definition: The better, or best, of cattle or other property;
sourceDefinition: The better, or best, of cattle or other property; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ Haziyrapu AlmAli : or the latter signifies property to which the heart clings: (TA:) the term Hzrp is applied alike to what is masc. and what is fem.: (AO, Msb:) the pl. is HazaraAtN (S, Msb, K) and HazoraAtN , as though the sing. were an epithet: (Msb:) it is applied to the better or best of property because the owner of such property always, when he sees it, computes its quantity or number in his mind: accord. to Aboo-Sa'eed, HazaraAtu AlA^amowaAli signifies those kinds of property which their owners love: accord. to AO, choice kinds of property. (TA.) You say also, h`*aA Hazorapu nafosiY , meaning This is the best of what I have: and of such property the collector of the poor-rate is forbidden to take. (S, Mgh, * TA.) Also, hiYa Hazorapu qalobihi It is the choice thing of his heart. (AO.)

sourceDefinition: A collector of firewood: (Msb, TA:) and so ↓ HaT~aAbN , (A, Msb,) but in an intensive sense: (Msb:) or the latter, one who collects and sells firewood: (TA:) and HaT~aAbapN a company of collectors of firewood: (S, Mgh:) and A_imaA='N HawaATibu [pl. of HaATibapN ] female slaves who collect firewood. (TA.) It is said in a prov., AlmikovaAru HaATibu layolK (tropical:) The loquacious is [like] a collector of firewood by night. (A 'Obeyd, TA.)

sourceDefinition: and Him~KSN ; (S, Msb, K;) the former preferred by Th, (S, TA,) and by the Koofees, (Msb, TA,) and the only word of that form except qin~afN and ql~afN and qin~ibN and xin~abN ; (Fr, TA;) the latter alone allowed by Mbr, (S,) and this alone mentioned by Sb, (TA,) and preferred by the Basrees, (Msb, TA,) and said by Mbr to be the only word of this form except Hil~izN , meaning “ short, ” and jil~iqN , the name of a place in Syria, (S, TA,) but IAar did not know this latter form of the word; (Az, TA;) [The cicer arietinum; or chick-peas; ] a certain grain, (S, Msb, K,) well known, (Msb, K,) of the description termed AlqaTaAni : (AHn:) n. un. Him~aSapN and Him~iSapN : (TA:) it is white, and red, and black, and of a sort called kirosiniY~N [or karosaniY~N ?]; and is also wild, and cultivated in gardens: the wild sort is the hotter, and the more contracted; the nutriment of the garden-sort is the better; and the black is the most powerful in its operations: (the Minháj, TA:) it is flatulent, lenitive, diuretic, having the property of increasing the seminal fluid and the carnal appetite and the blood: (K:) Hippocrates says that it has in it two substances, which quit it by cooking; one of them salt, or saline, which is lenitive; and the other sweet, which is diuretic; and it clears away spots in the skin, and beautifies the complexion, and is beneficial for hot tumours, and its oil is serviceable for the ringworm, or tetter; and its meal, for the fluid of foul ulcers; and the infusion thereof, for toothache, and for swelling of the lip; and it clears the voice: (TA:) it also strengthens the body and the penis; (K;) wherefore it is given as fodder to the stallions of horses and the like, and of camels; (TA;) on the condition of its being eaten not before [other] food nor after it, but in the midst thereof; (K;) or, correctly, as in the Minháj, it should be eaten between two meals. (TA.)

definition: Foolishness, or stupidity;
sourceDefinition: Foolishness, or stupidity; i. e. unsoundness in the intellect or understanding; (T, Mgh, Msb;) and stagnancy, or dulness, therein; (T, Mgh;) or deficiency, or defectiveness, therein; (IF, Mgh;) or paucity, or want, thereof; and ↓ HumuqN and ↓ HamaAqapN signify the same: (S, K:) [all are said to be inf. ns.; but the last, accord. to the Msb, is a simple subst.: (see 1:)] the proper and primary signification of HumoqN is [said to be] the putting a thing in a wrong place, with knowledge of its being bad [ to do so ]. (TA.) [Hence,] nawomapu AlHumoqi The sleep after [ the period of the afternoon called ] the EaSor ; when no one sleeps except one who is intoxicated, or one who is insane, or unsound in mind. (Har p. 223. [See also xuroqN and xuluqN .]) ― -b2- And Deceit; or a deception. (TA.) ― -b3- [It is said that] AlHumoqu also signifies Wine: (Z, K:) as being a cause of Humoq ; like as wine is called A_ivomN as being a cause of A_ivom : (Z, TA:) but Ez-Zejjájee disallows this: and [it is also said that] ↓ AlHumayoqaA='u signifies the same, because wine occasions Humoq to its drinker. (TA.)

definition: a contracted dim.
sourceDefinition: a contracted dim. of A^aHomaqu ; or dim. of HamiqN : [the dim. form being app. used in this case to denote enhancement of the signification: (see also Hum~ayoqapN :)] so in the prov., (TA,) Earafa HumayoqN jamalahu [ A very foolish, or stupid, man knew his camel ]; i. e. he knew thus much, although A^aHomaq : or, as some relate it, Earafa HumayoqFA jamaluho , i. e. his camel knew him, [namely, a very foolish, or stupid, man, ] and emboldened himself against him; or it means that he knew his quality: (K, TA:) it is applied to the case of excessive familiarity with men: (TA:) or to him who deems a man weak, and is therefore fond of annoying, or molesting, him, (K, TA,) and ceases not to act wrongfully towards him: or, as some say, [ Hmyq is here a proper name; and] this person had a camel with which he was familiar, and he made and attack upon him. (TA.) [See Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 85.]

definition: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ HamiqN (S, Msb) and ↓ HamoqaAn [whether with or without tenween is not shown] (Sb, TA) Foolish, or stupid; i. e. unsound in intellect or understanding; (T, Mgh, Msb;) and stagnant, or dull, therein; (T, Mgh;) or deficient, or defective, therein; IF, Mgh;) or haring little, or no, intellect or understanding: (S, K:) fem. of the first HamoqaA='u ; (S, Msb;) and of the second HamiqapN : (TA:) pl. of the first, applied to men and to women, (S, K,) HumoqN , (so in two copies of the S,) or HumuqN , with two dammehs, (K,) and HamoqaY and HamaAqaY (S, K) and HumaAqaY (Sgh, K) and HimaAqN . (Ibn- 'Abbád, K.) Accord. to some, A^aHomaqu is from the phrase AinoHamaqati Als~uwqu : and accord. to some, from the phrase layaAlK muHomiqaAtN , because the AHmq deceives one at first by what he says. (TA.) The sounds of wailing for the dead, and trilling, or quavering, in playing, are termed A^aHomaqaAni because of the Humoq of the person from whom they proceed. (Mgh.) ― -b2- Albaqolapu AlHamoqaA='u (S, K) and baqolapu AlHamoqaA='i , (K,) the latter for baqolapu AlHab~api AlHamoqaA='i , i. q. Alr~ijolapu [ Garden purslane ]; (S, ISd, K;) which is the name applied to it by the vulgar; (ISd, TA;) the chief of herbs, or leguminous plants: called by those names because exuding mucilage ( mulaE~ibapN ), so that it is likened to the A^aHomaq whose slaver is flowing: IDrd says, they assert that it is so called because it grows in the tracks of men, so that it is trodden upon; and in water-courses, so that the water uproots it: IF says that it is so called because of its weakness: and it is said that some persons, hating 'Áïsheh, called it baqolapu EaAy^i$apa ; but this is one of their fanciful assertions; for such was its name in the time of utter paganism: so says Sgh. (TA.) ― -b3- [ A^aHomaqu also signifies More, and most, foolish, or stupid, &c. Hence,] it is said in a prov., A^aHomaqu mino rijolapK [ More foolish, or stupid, than a plant of gardenpurslane: explained by what precedes]. (TA.) [See also another prov. voce vamaAnuwna .] And in a trad., A^aHomaqu AlHumoqi Alfujuwru [ The most foolish of foolishness, or the most stupid of stupidness, is vice, or immorality, or unrighteousness ]. (A in art. kys .)

definition: and muHomiqapN (S, K) A woman who brings forth a child that is A^aHomaq [i.
sourceDefinition: and muHomiqapN (S, K) A woman who brings forth a child that is A^aHomaq [i. e. foolish, &c.]; (S;) or who brings forth HamoqaY [i. e. foolish children ]: (K:) or, accord. to IDrd, the latter has this signification; but the former signifies a man who begets HamoqaY ; and he does not allow its application to a woman. (TA.) ― -b2- AlmuHomiqaAtu (tropical:) The nights [ that make a fool of one; i. e.] during the whole of which the moon is above the horizon but intercepted by clouds; so that one imagines that he has arrived at the time of morning; (A, O, K, TA;) because he sees light, but sees not the moon: derived from AlHumoqu . (TA.) One says, gar~aniY guruwra AlmuHomiqaAti (tropical:) [ He, or it, deceived me with the deceiving of the nights thus called ]. (TA.) And you say, sironaA fiY layaAli muHomiqaAtK (tropical:) [ We journeyed during such nights ]; because the rider therein thinks that he has arrived at the time of morning until he becomes weary. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaHuwTu : see 4, in three places. ― -b2- HaATahu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (S, Msb,) inf. n. HawoTN (S, Msb, K) and HiyTapN and HiyaATapN , (S, K, TA, [the second and third, in the CK, erroneously, with fet-h to the H , the former of them being expressly said in the S and TA, and the latter also in the TA, to be with kesr, and both being shown in the S to be originally with w , i. e. HiwoTapN and HiwaATapN ,]) and HiyaATN is used in poetry for the last of these; (TA;) and ↓ Hw~Thu , (K,) inf. n. taHowiyTN ; (TA;) and ↓ tHw~Thu ; (K, TA; [omitted in the CK;]) He guarded, kept, kept safely, protected, or took care of, him, or it; (S, Msb, K, TA;) he defended him, or it; (TA;) he paid frequent attention to him, or it; (K, TA;) he minded, or was regardful of, the things that were for his, or its, good. (TA.) You say, laA zilota fiY HiyaATapi A@ll~`hi Mayest thou not cease to be in the protection of God. (TA.) And maEa fulaAnK HiyTapN laka There is with such a one compassion and affection for thee: you should not say Ealayoka . (S.) And A^aHuwTu EiroDiY [ I guard, or defend, or take care of, my honour, or reputation ]. (TA.) And A^axaAhu ↓ huwa yataHaw~aTu He takes care of, or pays frequent attention to, his brother; and undertakes, or superintends, or manages, his affairs. (TA.) And HaATahumo qaSaA='ahumo and biqaSaAy^ihimo He fought in their defence. (TA.) [But this is generally meant ironically.] When an affliction befalls thee, and thy brother does not guard thee, or defend thee, and does not aid thee, one says [to thee], HaATaka AlfaDaA='a [so in the TA, app. a mistranscription for AlqaSaA='a or AlqaSaA , with which, however, it is nearly syn.,] which is used ironically; i. e. He guarded thee, or defended thee, in a distant quarter; meaning, (tropical:) he did not guard thee, or defend thee; for he who guards, or defends, his brother, draws near to him, and supports him, or aids him. (A, TA.) [See also 1 in art. Hbw .] You say also, HaATuwnaA AlqaSaA='a , (K,) or AlqaSaA , (TK,) [both are said to be correct in the TA in art. qSw , on the authority of Ibn-Wellád,] in some of the copies of the K with f and D , and in some with f and D , the latter unpointed, and so in [a copy of] the A, (TA,) (tropical:) They retired to a distance from us, they being around us, and we not being distant from them, had they desired to come to us. (K, TA.) And HuToniY AlqaSaA (tropical:) Retire thou to a distance from me; (Ibn-Wellád, and K in art. qSw ;) as also AlqaSaA='a . (Ibn-Wellád, and TA in that art.) And laA^aHuwTan~aka AlqaSaA walaA^agozuwan~aka biAlEaSaA , in each case with the short & A , meaning I will assuredly leave thee, and not go near thee; [ and I will assuredly go against thee to fight thee with the staff. ] (Ks, TA in art. qSw .) HuTo HuTo means Take thou care of the tie of kindred, and preserve it. (IAar, K. *) It also signifies Deck thou the boys ( AlS~iboyap [in the CK AlS~abiy~ap the girl ]) with the HawoT [ for preservation from the evil eye ]. (IAar, K.) And HuwTuwA gulaAmakumo Deck ye your boy with the HawoT . (AA.) ― -b3- HaATa AlHimaAru EaAnatahu , (S, * Msb, K,) nor, as above, (S, Msb,) inf. n. HawoTN , (Msb,) The [wild] he-ass collected, or drew together, (S, * Msb, K, *) and guarded, or took care of, (TA,) his EaAnap [app. meaning his herd of wild asses: or the phrase may mean the he-ass drew towards himself, or compressed, and guarded, his she-ass: Freytag here renders EAnp by “ pubem; ” and Golius, by “ veretrum ”]. (S, Msb, K.)

sourceDefinition: ↓ HaATa signify the same [i. e. It, or he, surrounded, encompassed, environed, enclosed, or hemmed in, it, or him ]. (TA.) You say, AHAT Alqawomu biAlbaladi , inf. n. A_iHaATapN ; and ↓ HaATuwA bihi ; The people surrounded, encompassed, environed, encircled, or beset, the sides of the town. (Msb.) And AHATt Alxayolu bifulaAnK , (S, TA,) and bh ↓ HaATato , (TA,) and bh ↓ AHtATt , (S,) The horses, or horsemen, surrounded, encompassed, environed, encircled, or beset, such a one. (S, TA.) [And AHATwA bihi mino jaAnibayohi , meaning They surrounded him on all his sides; lit. on his two sides: see janobN .] ― -b2- It is said in the Kur [xvii. 62], A_in~a rab~aka A^aHaATa biAln~aAsi (assumed tropical:) Verily thy Lord hath men in his grasp, or power: (Bd, TA:) or (assumed tropical:) hath destroyed them; meaning Kureysh. (Bd.) You say also, A^uHiyTa bifulaAnK , meaning (assumed tropical:) Such a one was destroyed: or (assumed tropical:) his destruction drew near. (TA.) And hence the saying in the Kur [xviii. 40], waA^uHiyTa bivamarihi (assumed tropical:) And its fruit became smitten by that which destroyed and spoiled it: (TA:) or (assumed tropical:) his possessions became destroyed: from A^aHaATa bihi AlEaduw~u [ the enemy surrounded him ]. (Bd.) [Hence also, in the same, ii. 75,] waA^aHaATato bihi xaTiyoy^atuhu (assumed tropical:) And over whom his sin hath gained the mastery, affecting all the circumstances of his case, so that he hath become as though he were entirely encompassed thereby: (Bd:) or (assumed tropical:) who hath died in the belief of a plurality of Gods. (TA.) You also say, AHAT bihi AlA^amoru (assumed tropical:) The thing beset him on every side, so that he had no place of escape from it. (TA.) And AHAT Ealayohi (assumed tropical:) He took it entirely to himself, debarring others from it: [see also 2.] (TA in art $rb .) ― -b3- AHAT bihi , (K,) or AHAT bihi EilomFA , (S, Msb, TA,) and AHAT bihi Eilomuhu , (S, TA,) (tropical:) [ He comprehended it, or knew it altogether, in all its modes or circumstances; ] he knew it extrinsically and intrinsically; (Msb;) or he attained the utmost particular thereof, and had a comprehensive and complete knowledge thereof: or he attained everything [ relating to it ], and the utmost knowledge thereof. (K, accord. to different copies. [In the CK, AaHoS`Y Eilomuhu is put, erroneously, for AHSY Eilomahu .]) It is said in the Kur [xxvii. 22], A^aHaTotu bimaA lamo tuHiTo bihi (tropical:) I have known in all its circumstances, or modes, that which thou hast not so known. (TA.) And you say also, Ealimahu Eiloma A_iHaATapK (tropical:) He knew it in all its circumstances, or modes; nothing of them escaping him. (TA.) ― -b4- See also 2.

definition: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ xadiynN (S, K) A friend: (S, TA:) or a secret, or private, friend; a friend in secrecy or privacy: (Mgh, Msb, and Ksh and Bd in iv. 29:) or a companion, or an associate, who converses, or talks, with one: (M, TA:) or [simply] a companion, or an associate: (K:) but accord. to Er-Rághib, mostly used as meaning an amorous companion or associate; a companion, or an associate, affected with sensual appetency: (TA:) the former is applied alike to the male and the female: (Ksh and Bd in v. 7:) and ↓ the latter signifies also one who is thy friend, &c., ( mano yuxaAdinuka , K,) and who is with thee, (TA,) in every affair, or case, open and secret: (K:) pl. (of the former, S, Mgh, Msb) A^axodaAnN (S, Mgh, Msb, TA) and [of the latter] xudanaA='u . (TA.) Hence, xidonu AljaAriyapi [ The friend, &c., of the girl ]: (S:) or he who converses, or talks, with the girl. (JK.) It is said in the Kur [iv. 29], walaA mut~axi*aAti A^axodaAnK , (S,) meaning [ Nor taking to themselves ] friends [or associates ] to commit fornication with them in secret. (Jel.) AlEulaY ↓ xadiynu is a metaphorical expression, used by a poet, [meaning (tropical:) Lover of eminence, ] like Ea$iyqu AlEulaY . (TA.)

definition: The utensils and furniture of a house or tent: (S, Mgh, K:) and the refuse, or the worthless or mean or vile articles, thereof;

AsY :) [pl. xaraAviY~N .] You say, naqaluwA xuroviY~a mataAEihimo They removed the worthless articles of their furniture and utensils. (L.) ― -b2- And xarida He was, or became, affected with shame, bashfulness, or pudency; (IAar;) as also ↓ Axrd (K.) ― -b3- He was, or became, abject. (Har p. 250.) [See also xaAridN .]

(Mgh, Msb, K) and , (K,) the former of which is the more chaste, (TA,) inf. n. xaroqN , (S, Mgh, Msb, KL,) He made a hole in it, perforated it, pierced it, or bored it; (Msb, * KL;) syn. jaAbahu [in this sense, as well as in another to be explained below], (K, [in the CK, erroneously, jA'a bhi ,]) and vaqabahu : (TA:) and he cut it [ so as to make a hole or a slit in it ]: (Msb:) and he rent it, or tore it. (JK, K, KL.) You say, xaraqa Alvawoba , (JK, S, Mgh, K,) aor. [and ], inf. n. as above, (Mgh,) He [ made a hole in, or] rent, or tore, the garment, or piece of cloth; (JK, K;) and Alxuf~a [ the boot ]; and the like. (Mgh.) And xaraqa AlS~axorapa He made a hole in the rock; syn. jaAbahu . (A in art. jwb .) [And xaraqa AlHaAy^iTa He made a hole in, or through, the wall: see xaroqN , below.] And xaraqahu biAlmivoqabi He made a hole in it or through it, perforated it, pierced it, or bored it, with a drill or the like; syn. vaqabahu . (Msb in art. vqb .) xaraqa Als~afiynapa [ He made a hole in the ship ], in the Kur xviii. 70, means that he did so by taking out, from the ship, with an axe, (Ksh, Bd, Jel,) a plank, (Jel,) or two planks. (Ksh, Bd.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xaraqa AlA^aroDa , (JK, S, Msb,) or AlmafaAzapa , (Mgh, K, *) (tropical:) He traversed, crossed, or cut through by journeying, (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) the earth, or land, (JK, S, Msb,) or the desert; (Mgh, K;) syn. qaTaEahaA ; (JK, Mgh, K; *) or jaAbahaA ; (S, Msb;) so as to reach the furthest part thereof. (Mgh, TA.) [See also 8.] It is said in the Kur [xvii. 39], A_in~aka lano taxoriqa AlA^aroDa , meaning, For thou shalt not reach the extremities of the earth: or, accord. to Az, thou shalt not traverse the earth in length and breadth: (TA:) or it means thou shalt not bore through the earth, (Jel, TA,) so as to reach the end thereof: (Jel:) or thou shalt not make a hole in the earth by thy vehement treading: (Ksh, Bd:) accord. to one reading, ln taxoruqa . (Ksh, TA.) ― -b3- [And xaraqati Alr~iyHu (assumed tropical:) The wind passed along: and (assumed tropical:) blew: for] the inf. n. xaroqN signifies (assumed tropical:) the passing of the wind: and (assumed tropical:) the blowing thereof. (KL.) [See also 7 and 8.] ― -b4- xaraqa Alka*iba (tropical:) He forged, or feigned, the lie; as also ↓ Axtrqhu . (K, TA.) It is said in the Kur vi. 100, waxaraquwA lahu baniyna wabanaAtK , i. e. (tropical:) And they have feigned Him to have, or falsely attributed to Him, sons and daughters. (Ksh, Bd, Jel. [See also 2.]) And xaraqa [alone, the object being understood], (K,) inf. n. as above, (KL,) signifies (tropical:) He lied; told a lie: (K, KL, TA:) and ↓ txr~q (tropical:) he forged, or feigned, a lie. (S, K, TA.) -A2- xariqati Al$~aApu , aor. , inf. n. xaraqN , The sheep had in its ear a xaroq , i. e. a round hole or perforation. (Msb.) -A3- xariqa fiY Albayoti , aor. , (JK, K,) inf. n. xuruwqN , (JK,) or xaraqN ; (TK;) and xaraqa , inf. n. xuruwqN ; (K;) He remained in the house, or tent, not quitting it. (JK, * K.) ― -b2- And xariqa , aor. , inf. n. xaraqN , said of a gazelle, or young gazelle, (Msb, K, TA,) when hunted, (TA,) or when overtaken by the dog, (IAar,) It was frightened, (Msb, K, TA, [in the CK, Aano yaEoraqa is erroneously put for A^ano yaforaqa ,]) so as to be unable to go away, (Msb,) or so as to be unable to rise, (K, TA,) and clave to the ground: (IAar, TA:) and in like manner said of a bird, (Msb, K,) it became frightened, (K,) or impatient, (TA,) so as to be unable to fly away. (K, TA.) ― -b3- And hence, (Msb,) the same verb, (S, Msb, K,) with the same aor., (Msb, K,) and the same inf. n., (S, Msb, K,) said of a man, (Msb,) He became confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course; or he became bereft of his reason or intellect, because of fear, or of shame: (S, Msb, K:) or he was confounded, perplexed, or amazed, [for yatahay~aba in the CK, I read yabohata , as in other copies of the K and in the TA,] opening his eyes, and looking: (K, TA:) and he remained confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course, by reason of anxiety, or of hardship, or distress. (TA.) waqaEa faxariqa [ He fell down and clave to the ground ], occurring in a trad, means he fell down dead. (TA.) -A4- xariqa , aor. , (JK, S, Msb, K,) inf. n. xaraqN ; (S, Msb, K; *) and xaruqa , aor. , (JK, K,) [of which xuroqN , said in the S and Msb to be a simple subst., may be the inf. n., like as HusonN is of Hasona ;] He was rough, ungentle, clumsy, or awkward, (S, Msb, K,) in doing, or making, a thing: (Msb:) and he was unskilful in work, and in the management of affairs: and he was foolish; stupid; or unsound, or deficient, in intellect or understanding: (K:) or he was ignorant: (JK:) or the latter verb signifies he knew not his work with his hand, or his handicraft. (Msb.) And xaruqa biAl$~aYo'i He was ignorant of the thing, (K, TA,) and did it not well. (TA.)

definition: A kerchief twisted for the purpose of beating therewith: (JK, S:) a genuine Arabic word: (S:) or a thing made of twisted rags, with which boys play: (TA:) or a twisted kerchief, or an inflated [ skin...
sourceDefinition: A kerchief twisted for the purpose of beating therewith: (JK, S:) a genuine Arabic word: (S:) or a thing made of twisted rags, with which boys play: (TA:) or a twisted kerchief, or an inflated [ skin such as is termed ] ziq~ , or the like, with which boys play, beating one another therewith: so called because it rends ( yaxoriqu ) the air when they make use of it: (Ham p. 702:) pl. maxaAriyqu . (S, TA.) 'Amr Ibn-Kulthoom says, kaA^an~a suyuwfanaA min~aA waminohumo maxaAriyqN biA^ayodiY laA EibiynaA [ As though our swords, ours and theirs, were kerchiefs twisted for beating therewith, in the hands of players ]: (S:) or mxAryq in this verse [written with tenween by poetic license] is the pl. of mixoraAqN signifying a wooden sword with which boys play: the poet means, we cared not for the smiting with the swords, like as the players care not for the smiting with the mxAryq . (EM p. 198.) [See also another ex., in a verse cited voce xariyjN .] 'Alee is related, in a trad., to have said that the lightning is the maxaAriyq of the angels; (S, TA;) meaning thereby the instruments with which the angels chide and drive the clouds. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A garment, or piece of cloth. (JK. [But this I find not elsewhere.]) ― -b3- And (tropical:) A sword [in the ordinary sense of the word]: so in the A and O and L: in the K, Als~ay~idu is erroneously put for Als~ayofu . (TA.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) A man goodly in body, or person, whether tall or not tall. (JK, K.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) One who falls not into a case without escaping, or extricating himself, therefrom. (Sh, TA.) ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) One who exercises art in the management of affairs. (K.) ― -b7- (tropical:) A wild bull: (As, K:) so called because he traverses far-extending districts: (As, TA:) or because the dogs pursue him and he escapes from them: said in the A to be called mixoraAqu AlmafaAzapi . (TA.) ― -b8- (assumed tropical:) A man who engages in wars, or fights, and is active therein. (S, K.) ― -b9- See also xiroqN .

definition: , (Mgh, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. yaxofaY , (Msb, K,) inf. n. xafaA='N , (Mgh, Msb, K,) has two contr. significations: (Mgh, Msb:) It was, or became, unperceived or imperceptible, [or hardly perceived or perceptible, by any of the senses, or only by the eye or ear, or by the mind; mostly] unapparent, or not apparent; (K;) [ latent; obscure; ] hidden, concealed, or covered; (Mgh, Msb;) [or unconspicuous; but also faint, or dim, to the sight; suppressed, or stifled, said of the voice; or low, faint, gentle, or soft, to the ear; and obscure to the mind, abstruse, recondite, occult, or covert; and secret, private, or clandestine: ] and the contr., i. e. it appeared; it was, or became, apparent, open, manifest, plain, or evident; (Mgh, Msb;) [as also ↓ AstxfY : (see musotaxofK , below:)] or, accord. to some, the particle that connects it with its subject distinguishes one meaning from the other: (Msb:) you say, xafiY Ealayohi , aor. and inf. n. as above, (S, Mgh, Msb, TA,) it (a thing, or an affair, Mgh) was, or became, unperceived or imperceptible, [&c., by him; ] unapparent, or not apparent, [or obscure, &c., to him; ] (TA;) or hidden, or concealed, from him: (Mgh, Msb:) and xafiYa lahu it appeared to him; it was, or became, perceptible, apparent, open, &c., to him: [but see what follows:] (Mgh, Msb:) whence the sayings of Mohammad, [app. the Hanafee Imám,] referring to spoils, faxafiY lahumo A^ano ya*ohabuwA bihaA wayakotumuwhaA A^ahola Al$~iroki , i. e. It appeared [ to them that they should go away with them, or take them away, and conceal them from the believers in a plurality of gods ], and xafiYa lahumo A^ano yuxorijuwhaA A_ilaY daAri AlA_isolaAmi [ It appeared to them that they should take them forth to the territory of El-Islám]: but this is said only in relation to that which appears from a state of concealment or from a hidden quarter. (Mgh.) [Hence,] bariHa AlxafaA='u The affair, or case, became manifest: (S, K:) or the state of concealment departed, or ceased; but the former explanation is better: or, as some say, ↓ AlxafaA='u here signifies the secret; and the meaning is, the secret became apparent: (TA:) or, lit., the low ground became high and apparent; meaning (assumed tropical:) what was concealed became revealed. (Har pp. 133-4. [See also art. brH .]) [And EalaY xafaA='K means Covertly, secretly, privately, stealthily, or clandestinely. (See also what follows.)] ― -b2- xafiytu lahu , aor. , (K,) inf. n. xufoyapN and xifoyapN (Msb, K) and xifowapN , (K,) the Y and w being interchangeable, (TA,) signifies ↓ Aixotafayotu [i. e. I made myself unapparent to him, lurked, or lay hid or in ambush, for him; cloaked, or disguised, myself to him; hid, or concealed, myself from him ]: (K:) [for] AxtfY signifies he hid, or concealed, himself, (Fr, * El-Fárábee, JK, * Msb, K,) minohu from him; (TA;) as also ↓ AstxfY , (Fr, * JK, * Msb, K,) and ↓ AxfY , (IAar, K,) and ↓ txf~Y also is syn. with AxtfY [in this sense]: (Z, TA:) or you say, ↓ Aisotaxofayotu minoka , meaning I hid, or concealed, myself from thee; but not ↓ Aixotafayotu : (IKt, Th, S, Msb:) or ↓ AxtfY in the sense of xafiYa is not of high authority, nor is it disallowed, (Az, Msb, TA,) but ↓ AstxfY is more usual. (Az, TA.) You say, faEalotuhu xufoyapF and xifoyapF [ I did it covertly, secretly, privately, stealthily, or clandestinely ]. (Msb) And qutila xfoyapF and xifowapF [ He was slain covertly, secretly, &c.]. (JK.) And yaA^okuluhu xifowapF [lit. He eats it covertly, &c.,] means he steals it. (K.) In the saying in the Kur [vii. 53], AudoEuw rab~akumo taDar~uEFA waxufoyapF , the meaning [of the last word] is, Submissively, devoting yourselves to his service: or, accord. to Zj, adhering to his service in your minds: or, accord. to Th, celebrating Him in your minds: or, accord. to Lh, in quietness, and stillness: (TA:) or secretly; and so in the similar passage in the Kur vi. 63. (Jel, and so Bd on this latter passage.) xufoyapN is from A^axofayotu AlS~awota [explained below in this paragraph]: (JK:) the intrans. v. whereof is ↓ AxtfY [signifying It (the voice) was, or became, suppressed, or stifled; or low, faint, gentle, or soft; like xafiYa , which is more common]. (Lth, TA.) -A2- xafaAhu , aor. yaxofiyhi , (JK, S, Msb, K,) inf. n. xafoYN (JK, Msb, * K) and xufiY~N , (K,) also has two contr. significations: (S, Msb, TA:) He made it perceptible, apparent, open, manifest, plain, or evident: (JK, S, Msb, K:) and he hid, or concealed, or covered, it; (S, Msb, K; [in this latter sense, erroneously written in the CK xaf~Ahu ;]) as also ↓ AxfAhu : (S, K:) or, accord. to some, this latter has the latter meaning; and the former verb has [only] the former meaning: but accord. to other, the reverse is the case: (Msb:) or, accord. to Aboo-' Alee El-Kálee, the former verb has the former meaning only; and ↓ the latter verb has both meanings: (IB, TA:) ↓ the latter is also explained as signifying he removed its xifaA=' , i. e. its covering: (TA:) and the former, as meaning he made it to come forth from a state of concealment: (JK:) and he drew it forth; (K;) as also ↓ AxtfAhu . (S, Msb, K.) One says, xafaY AlmaTaru AlfaA^ora The rain made the rats, or mice, to come forth from their holes. (S.) It is said in the Kur [xx. 15], A_in~a Als~aAEapa A=tiyapN A^akaAdu A^axofiyhaA , (JK, TA,) or ↓ A^uxofiyhaA , (JK, S, TA,) accord. to different readers: (TA:) the former means [ Verily the hour of the resurrection is coming: ] I am almost making it to appear: (JK, TA:) and the latter, I am almost removing that which conceals it: (S, IJ, TA:) or I almost conceal it: (JK, TA:) or, as Ubeí reads it, A^akaAdu A^uxofiyhaA mino nafoisY [ I almost conceal it from Myself ]: and Fr says [that the meaning is], I almost conceal it from Myself, and how then should I acquaint you therewith? (TA.) And it is said in a trad. respecting the flight [from Mekkeh], AxfY Ean~aA xabaraka [written without the vowel-signs, so that it may be AixofiY or ↓ A^axofiY ,] i. e. Conceal thou thine information from such as may ask thee respecting us. (TA.) And in another trad., kaAna yaxofiY Sawotahu biA^aniynK , thus with fet-h to the Y , meaning He used to make his voice perceptible [or audible, with moaning ]. (TA.) And you say, AlS~awota ↓ A^axofayotu [meaning I suppressed, or stifled, the voice; or made it low, faint, gentle, or soft ]. (Lth, JK, TA.) [And AlkalaAma ↓ AxfY He uttered speech, or the speech, in a low, faint, gentle, or soft, tone; he spoke in a low, faint, gentle, or soft, manner; lit. he made speech, or the speech, to be low, &c.] -A3- xafaY , aor. yaxofiY ; and xafiYa , aor. yaxofiY ; inf. n. of each xafoYN ; said of lightning: see xafaA , in art. xfw .

In the saying in the Kur [vii. 53], AudoEuw rab~akumo taDar~uEFA waxufoyapF , the meaning [of the last word] is, Submissively, devoting yourselves to his service: or, accord. to Zj, adhering to his service in your minds: or, accord. to Th, celebrating Him in your minds: or, accord. to Lh, in quietness, and stillness: (TA:) or secretly; and so in the similar passage in the Kur vi. 63. (Jel, and so Bd on this latter passage.) xufoyapN is from A^axofayotu AlS~awota [explained below in this paragraph]: (JK:) the intrans. v. whereof is ↓ AxtfY [signifying It (the voice) was, or became, suppressed, or stifled; or low, faint, gentle, or soft; like xafiYa , which is more common]. It is said in the Kur [xx. 15], A_in~a Als~aAEapa A=tiyapN A^akaAdu A^axofiyhaA , (JK, TA,) or ↓ A^uxofiyhaA , (JK, S, TA,) accord. to different readers: (TA:) the former means [ Verily the hour of the resurrection is coming: ] I am almost making it to appear: (JK, TA:) and the latter, I am almost removing that which conceals it: (S, IJ, TA:) or I almost conceal it: (JK, TA:) or, as Ubeí reads it, A^akaAdu A^uxofiyhaA mino nafoisY [ I almost conceal it from Myself ]: and Fr says [that the meaning is], I almost conceal it from Myself, and how then should I acquaint you therewith? (TA.) And it is said in a trad. respecting the flight [from Mekkeh], AxfY Ean~aA xabaraka [written without the vowel-signs, so that it may be AixofiY or ↓ A^axofiY ,] i. e. Conceal thou thine information from such as may ask thee respecting us. (TA.) And in another trad., kaAna yaxofiY Sawotahu biA^aniynK , thus with fet-h to the Y , meaning He used to make his voice perceptible [or audible, with moaning ]. (TA.) And you say, AlS~awota ↓ A^axofayotu [meaning I suppressed, or stifled, the voice; or made it low, faint, gentle, or soft ]. (Lth, JK, TA.) [And AlkalaAma ↓ AxfY He uttered speech, or the speech, in a low, faint, gentle, or soft, tone; he spoke in a low, faint, gentle, or soft, manner; lit. he made speech, or the speech, to be low, &c.] -A3- xafaY , aor. yaxofiY ; and xafiYa , aor. yaxofiY ; inf. n. of each xafoYN ; said of lightning: see xafaA , in art. xfw .

sourceDefinition: A well: (S, K:) or a deep well; because its water is not perceived, or not apparent: (TA:) or a well of ancient times, that has become filled up and then dug again: (JK, TA:) or any well that has been dug and then left until it has become filled up, then dug again, and cleared out: (ISk, S:) [opposed to badiYo'N :] accord. to A'Obeyd, it is so called because it is made to appear: (S:) pl. xafaAyaA and xafiy~aAtN . definition: One who acts in a suspicious manner, or so as to induce suspicion or evil opinion;
sourceDefinition: One who acts in a suspicious manner, or so as to induce suspicion or evil opinion; who acts vitiously, or immorally; or commits adultery, or fornication: (S, K:) pl. xunuEN (K, TA) and xanaEapN . (TA.) El-Aashà says, humo AlxaDaArimu A_ino gaAbuwA wa A_ino $ahiduwA wa laA yarawona A_ilaY jaAraAtihimo xunuEaA [ They are the bountiful, if they be absent and if they be present; and they do not see persons acting in a suspicious manner, &c., towards their wives ]. (TA.) [The latter hemistich of this verse is cited in the S; in one copy of which I find yurawona in the place of yarawona : and it seems to be there implied that xunuEN is pl. of xunoEapN ; but I do not know any instance of fuEulN as the measure of a pl. of a word of the measure faEolapN .] ― -b2- One who commits a foul action whereof the disgrace returns upon him, and is ashamed of it, and hangs down his head towards the ground. (As, on the authority of an Arab of the desert.)
