sourceDefinition: Locusts before their wings are fullgrown: (Lth, * K, TA:) [see jaraAdN :] or when they have upon them streaks of different colours, white and yellow: (S, K:) or when they have changed from their first black or yellow colour to red: (As, K:) or when yellowness has appeared in their red colour, but some of the redness remains: (AHát, TA:) or [in the CK “ and ”] emaciated red locusts of the brood of the next preceding year: (K:) accord. to Lh, you say jaraAdN xayofaAnN , meaning locusts of different colours: (TA:) [but xyfAn is generally used as a subst.:] the n. un. is with p . (S.) ― -b2- Hence the n. un. is applied to a mare, as meaning (assumed tropical:) Brisk, sprightly, active, or agile, and leaping. (S, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also, app.,] xayofaAnN mina Aln~aAsi (assumed tropical:) A multitude of men. (Ibn-'Abbád, K. *) -A2- Also A certain plant of the mountains; (Ibn-'Abbád, K;) a certain herb growing in the mountain, having no leaves, rising more than a cubit in height, having a sanamap [or head resembling an ear of corn ], which is green in the upper part and white below, with a white awn, or beard. (L.)

[Hence also, app.,] xayofaAnN mina Aln~aAsi (assumed tropical:) A multitude of men. (Ibn-'Abbád, K. *)

Also A certain plant of the mountains; (Ibn-'Abbád, K;) a certain herb growing in the mountain, having no leaves, rising more than a cubit in height, having a sanamap [or head resembling an ear of corn ], which is green in the upper part and white below, with a white awn, or beard. (L.)

sourceDefinition: , (M, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (T, M, TA,) or , (Msb, [but this is a deviation from a general rule, and is probably a mistake,]) inf. n. dafiyfN (Lth, T, S, M, Msb) and daf~N ; (M, TA;) and ↓ Adf~ ; (Ibn-' Abbád, M, Msb, K;) said of a bird, (Lth, T, S, &c.,) It beat its sides ( daf~ayohi , i. e., Msb, janobayohi , M, Msb) with its wings: (M, Msb:) this is what is meant by the following explanation: (Msb:) it moved [or flapped ] its wings (Msb, K) for its flight, (Msb,) as the pigeon (K) and the like: (TA:) and it went [or flew ] along a little above the ground: (S, K:) or it moved [or flapped ] its wings, with its feet upon the ground, (Lth, T, M, K,) flying, and then rose; (Lth, T;) and in like manner ↓ dafodafa and ↓ Astdf~ : (K:) [or] df~ and ↓ Adf~ signify also it (a bird) went along quickly, with its feet upon the ground, and then raised itself flying. (Msb.) It is said in a trad., yuw^okalu maA daf~a walaA uw^okalu maA Saf~a , (K, * TA,) i. e. What moves [or flaps ] its wings [ in flying ], as the pigeon (K, TA) and the like, (TA,) may be eaten; but [ what skims along without flapping, ] such as vultures (K, TA) and hawks and the like, (TA,) may not be eaten. (K, * TA.) [But] daf~a , aor. , said of an eagle, signifies It approached, or was near to, the ground in its flying. (T.) ― -b2- And, daf~a , aor. , (M, Msb,) inf. n. dafiyfN (S, M, Msb, K) and daf~N , (K,) He, or it, (said of a camel, K, TA, and of a bird, TA, or of a party of men, Msb,) went a gentle pace; (S, M, Msb, K;) as also ↓ dafodafa . (IAar, TA.) Dhu-r-Rummeh uses it metaphorically in relation to Ald~abaraAni [the asterism of the Hyades, or α of Taurus], describing Alv~uray~aA [the Pleiades]; saying, yadif~u EalaYA=vaArihaA dabaraAnuhaA falaA huwa masobuwqN walaA huwa yaloHaqu [ Their Debarán goes along gently near after them, so that it is not outstripped, nor does it overtake ]. (M.) [And ↓ tadaAf~a , accord. to ISd, seems to signify nearly the same: for it is immediately added in the M,] in the saying, A_ilayoka A^a$okuw ma$oyahaA tadaAfiyaA ma$oYa AlEajuwzi tanoqulu AlA^avaAfiyaA [app. complaining, to God, of the slowness of his she-camel, as though meaning To Thee I complain of her pressing on slowly and laboriously, like the gait of the old woman removing the three stones for the support of the cooking-pot ], the poet means tadaAfufFA . (M. [But I rather think that the meaning here intended is, going along with an inclining from side to side; perhaps from daf~N signifying the “ side. ” See also 6 in art. dfw .]) One says also, Aljayo$u yadif~uwna naHowa AlEaduw~i The troops go gently, or leisurely, towards the enemy. (S.) And daf~ato EalayonaA mino baniY fulaAnK ↓ daAf~apN [ A company coming gently, or leisurely, of the sons of such a one, so came to us ]. (S.) And mina AlA^aEoraAbi ↓ daf~ato Ealayohimo daAf~apN A company of Arabs of the desert journeying leisurely in search of herbage and sustenance [ so ] came to them. (Z, TA.) And humo qawomN yadif~uwna , inf. n. dafiyfN , They are a party journeying together not a hard pace. (AA, T.) And daf~a EalaY wajohi AlA^aroDi (IAar, T, TA,) inf. n. daf~N , (K, TA,) He went lightly upon the ground; (K, * TA;) and *af~a signifies the same. (IAar, T.) And dafiyfN also signifies The act of running. (T.) ― -b3- Also daf~uwA , aor. , [app. They journeyed to a region of green herbage and waters in consequence of drought: (see daAf~apN :) and hence,] they had rain after experiencing drought. (M.) ― -b4- See also 10, in two places. -A2- See also 3. -A3- daf~a Al$~aYo'a , aor. , (TK,) inf. n. daf~N , (Sgh, K,) He uprooted the thing; extirpated it. (Sgh, K.)

sourceDefinition: The side, syn. janobN , (Lth, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) of anything, (Lth, T, M, Msb, K,) for instance, of a bird, (Msb,) and of a camel; (S;) as also ↓ daf~apN : (Lth, T, Mgh, Msb:) or the surface ( SafoHap ) of the side; (M, K;) as also ↓ daf~apN : (K:) pl. dufuwfN . (T, M, Msb.) Hence, A^aSobaru mino EawodK bidaf~ayohi julabo [ More enduring than an old camel in whose sides are scabs formed over wounds: a prov.]. (TA. [See Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 737.]) And ↓ baAta yaq~alabu EalaY daf~atayohi [and daf~yohi , i. e. He passed the night turning over and over upon his sides ]. (TA.) The saying of' Antarah, describing his she-camel, wakaA^an~amaA tanoA^aY bijaAnibi daf~ihaA A@lo waHo$iY~i mino haziji AlEa$iY~i muw^aw~ami Perseus transcribers were unclear about the final character of line 1 and the initial character of line 2. means And as though she were shrinking from the quarter of her off side, bi being here used in the sense of Eano , from a creature that cries for food at supper-time; meaning a cat, of ugly form and big head, fearing to be scratched by it: as J says, [in art. wH$ ,] she shrinks with her off side because the rider's whip is in his right hand: (EM p. 233:) [or the meaning is, as though she were shrinking with the outside of her off side; lit, with the side of her off side; for, accord. to ISd,] this is an instance of the prefixing of a noun to another identical therewith [in signification]. (M.) [Hence also,] ramaAhu A@ll~`hu bi*aAti Ald~af~i i. e. *At Aljanobi [ May God smite him with the pleurisy ] (TA.) ― -b2- ― -b3- Also A bank; an acclivity; or a part that faces one, above the foot or base; of sand; and of land or ground: (K:) accord. to En-Nadr, [the pl.] dufuwfN signifies banks; acclivities; or parts that face one, above the foot or base; of land or ground; (T, TA;) as also dafaAdifu , of which the sing. is ↓ dafodafapN : (T, K:) accord. to Z, the dufuwf of valleys are the elevated parts of the sides. (TA.) ― -b4- See also the next paragraph. ― -b5- And daf~apN .

sourceDefinition: [inf. n. of dl~Y ] signifies The lowering a thing; like ↓ A_idolaA='N [inf. n. of 4]. (Bd in vii. 21.) You say, dl~Y Al$~aYo'a fiY mahowaApK He let down the thing, made it to hang down, or let it fall, into a pit or the like. (T, * M, TA.) And dal~aAhu mino saToHK biHabolK He let him, or it, down from a house-top by means of a rope. (Mgh.) And dl~Y rijolayohi mina Als~ariyri [ He hung down his legs from the couch ]; and ↓ AdlY occurs in the same sense. (Mgh.) It is said in a trad., dul~iYa EalaY~a jiraAbN mino $aHomK mino baEoDi HuSuwni xayobara , meaning [ A bag, or provision-bag, of fat ] was let down, or let fall, upon me [ from one of the forts of Kheyber ]. (Mgh.) See also 4. ― -b2- And dl~Y Al$~aYo'a He made, or brought, or drew, the thing near to another thing ( mino gayorihi ); like Ald~alowi ↓ A_idolaA='u . (Har p. 173.) ― -b3- dal~aAhu biguruwrK (assumed tropical:) He caused him to fall into that which he desired [ to bring about ] by exposing him to perdition, or destruction, or loss, without his knowledge; from Ald~alowi ↓ A_idolaA='u . (S.) [In the Kur vii. 21,] fadal~aAhumaA biguruwrK means (assumed tropical:) And he caused them to fall ( fdl~AhmA ) into disobedience by deceiving, or beguiling, them: so says Aboo-Is-hák [Zj]: or (assumed tropical:) he excited their cupidity [ with deceit, or guile ]; originating from the case of a thirsty man's being let down ( yudal~aY ) into a well in order that he may satisfy his thirst from its water, and his not finding water in it, so that he is let down into it with deceit, or guile: or it means he emboldened them to eat of the tree with deceit, or guile; originally dal~alahumaA . (T.)

sourceDefinition: , [in the CK, erroneously, dalayotu ,] and ↓ dalawotu (K;) or A^adolayotu Ald~alowa , (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_idolaA='N ; (T, Msb;) and Ald~alowa ↓ dalawotu , [and app. biAld~alowi ,] aor. A^adoluw , [inf. n. dalowN ;] (T, * Msb;) I let down the dalow [or bucket ] (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) into the well, (T, S, Mgh, K,) to fill it, (T,) or to draw water with it. (M, Msb.) A^adoli dalowaka fiY Ald~ilaA='i [ Let down thy bucket with the other buckets ] is a prov. used in urging [a person] to strive, or labour, for gain; (TA;) originating from a company's assembling at a well, and letting down their buckets in order that every one of them may take his share of the water, or what is easily procurable by him thereof: meaning, use means to acquire, like as do others. (Har p. 167.) See also 2, in four places. ― -b2- Hence, (Mgh,) AdlY biHuj~atihi (tropical:) He adduced his plea, or the like, (T, S, M, Mgh, K,) correctly, or validly; (T;) or he defended himself by adducing it or urging it: (S:) or he established his plea, or the like, and so obtained his claim or demand or suit. (Msb.) And in like manner you say, AdlY biHaq~ihi (tropical:) [ He urged, or established, his right or due ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And AdlY bimaAlihi (tropical:) He gave, ( dafaEa , M, K, TA,) or presented, or offered, ( rafaEa , S, TA,) his property, (S, M, K, TA,) A_ilayohi [ to him ], (M,) or AlY AlHaAkima [ to the judge ]. (S.) Hence, in the Kur [ii. 184], watudoluwA bihaA A_ilaY , AlHuk~aAmi , (S, K,) i. e. (tropical:) And [do not] give it, or offer it, as a bribe to the judges: (S, * TA:) or and do not endeavour to conciliate with it the judges in order that they may cut off for you what is the right of others: (T:) or and do not throw it to the judges to be decided by them, (Mgh, Bd, Jel,) or as a bribe. (Jel.) And in a letter of 'Omar, faA@fohamo A_i*aA A^udoliYa A_ilayoka And understand thou when an application is made to thee by litigants for the decision of a cause. (Mgh.) ― -b4- And AdlY biraHimihi (tropical:) He sought to bring himself near, to approach, or to gain access, [ A_ilaY gayorihi to another, ] by means of his relationship: (S, K, TA:) and he pleaded, or made intercession, thereby. (TA.) bihi A_ilayoka ↓ waqado dalawonaA , in a prayer for rain, of 'Omar, referring to El-' Abbás, i. e., accord. to the “ Ghareebeyn, ” (assumed tropical:) And we have sought to approach, or to gain access, to Thee by him, app. means that they sought to obtain the mercy and aid of God [by means of his intercession], like as one seeks to get at, or obtain, the water by means of the dalow [or bucket]. (M.) One says also, A^adolaY A_ilaY Almay~ati biAlbunuw~api wanaHowihaA , meaning (assumed tropical:) He was united to the dead by sonship, and the like; from A_idolaA='u Ald~alowi . (Msb.) And fulaAnN yudoliY A_ilaY Almay~iti bi*akirK (assumed tropical:) Such a one is united with the dead by a male. (Mgh.) ― -b5- AdlY fiyhi means (tropical:) He said of him what was evil, or foul. (M, K.) ― -b6- And AdlY said of a horse &c., He put forth his yard, for the purpose of staling or covering; (M, K;) as also ↓ dl~Y said of an ass, as is also the former verb. (M.) ― -b7- See also 1, first and second sentences.

definition: It was let down or lowered;
sourceDefinition: It was let down or lowered; it hung down, or dangled; it was let down; (T, * M, Mgh;) into, and over, a pit or the like; (M;) it hung (K) from ( mino ) a tree; (S, K) it hung down as a fruit [from a tree]. (Bd in liii. 8.) [Hence,] tdl~Y EalayonaA mino A^aroDi ka*aA [ He, or it, came down, or descended, upon us from such a land ]. (TA.) And tdl~Y biAl$~ar~i He descended upon one with evil, or mischief. (TA.) ― -b2- Also He drew near, or approached: (K in art. dlY :) or he drew near, or approached, [ from above, or] after being high. (IAar, T.) Accord. to Fr, vum~a danaA fatadal~aY [in the Kur liii. 8] means vam~a tadal~aY fadanaA , (T,) i. e. Then he (Gabriel) hung down from the highest region of the sky, and so drew near to the Apostle: showing that he took him up without becoming separated from his place: or the meaning of the phrase, as it stands, is, then he drew near to the Prophet, and he clung to him: (Bd:) but accord. to Zj, it means then he drew near, and drew nearer; and is like the phrase danaA fulaAnN min~iY waqaruba . (T. [See also another explanation in what follows.]) ― -b3- And He was, or became, lowly, humble, or submissive; or he lowered, humbled, or abased, himself. (IAar, T; and K in art. dlY .) ― -b4- In the saying of a poet, kaA^ana raAkibahaA guSonN bimarowaHapK A_i*aA tadal~ato bihi A^awo $aAribN vamilN tdl~t may be quasi-pass. of dalaA , inf. n. dalowN , signifying “ he drove, or urged on, gently: ” or it may be for tadal~alato : [so that the meaning may be, As though her rider were a branch of a tree in a place over which the wind was blowing, when she became urged on gently with him, or an intoxicated drinker: or, when she emboldened herself with him, &c.:] (M:) [for] tadal~aY is also syn. with tadal~ala : (S, K:) and [J says that] this is its meaning in the saying in the Kur [otherwise explained above] vum~a danaA fatadal~aY : being like yatamaT~aY in the Kur [lxxv. 33], i. e. yatamaT~aTu . (S.)

definition: [ A bucket, generally of leather;
sourceDefinition: [ A bucket, generally of leather; ] a certain thing with which one draws water; (S, TA;) a vessel with which one draws water from a well; (KL;) well known; (T, K;) in Pers. dwl [i. e. duwlo , pronounced “ dól ”]: (MA:) masc. and fem.; (M;) sometimes masc.; (K;) mostly fem., (M, Msb,) and thus accord. to the more approved usage: (M:) pl. (of pauc., T, S, Msb) A^adolK , (T, S, M, Msb, K,) of the measure A^afoEulN , [originally A^adoluwN ,] (S,) and (of mult., T, * S, Msb) dilaA='N (T, S, M, Msb, K) and duliY~N , (S, M, Msb, K,) which is of the measure fuEuwlN (S, Msb) originally, (Msb,) and diliY~N (T, M, K, omitted in the CK) and duliy~apN , omitted here by the author of the K but mentioned by him in art. nHw , (TA,) and ↓ dalaA ; (K; [there said to be like EalaY ; but correctly dalFA ;]) or dalFA is syn. with dilaA='N , and its sing. [or n. un.] is ↓ dalaApN ; (S, M;) like as that of falFA is falaApN ; (M;) [for] dalaApN is syn. with dalowN : (T:) or dalaApN signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (M,) a small dalow . (M, K. [But in the M, in one place, it seems to be stated that, accord. to some, dalaApN and dalFA signify the same, in a pl. sense: for, after the pls. of dalowN , it is added, wahiYa Ald~alaApu waAld~alaA . I think, however, that he who first said this meant thereby that Ald~alaApu and Ald~alaA signify, respectively, the same as Ald~alowu and Ald~ilaA='u &c.]) [Hence the saying, A^atobiEi Ald~alowa ri$aA='ahaA : see 4 in art. tbE .] As masc., it has for its dim. ↓ dul~aY~N : as fem., ↓ dulay~apN . (Msb.) See also daAliyapN . ― -b2- And hence, (M,) Ald~alowu (tropical:) [ The sign of Aquarius; ] one of the signs of the Zodiac. (S, M, K.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) The hopper of a mill. (Golius on the authority of Meyd.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) A certain mark made with a hot iron upon camels; (S, K;) app. in the form of a dalow [properly so called]. (TA.) ― -b5- And (assumed tropical:) Calamity, misfortune, or mischief. (S, K.) So in the saying, jaA='a fulaAnN biAld~alowi (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one brought calamity, &c.]. (S.)

definition: A [ water-wheel, or machine for irrigating land, such as is called ] manojanuwn , (S, M, K,) that is turned by an ox or a cow: (S:) and [ such as is called ] a naAEuwrap : (K:) or the nAEwrp is...
sourceDefinition: A [ water-wheel, or machine for irrigating land, such as is called ] manojanuwn , (S, M, K,) that is turned by an ox or a cow: (S:) and [ such as is called ] a naAEuwrap : (K:) or the nAEwrp is turned by water: (S:) and a thing made of palm-leaves (M, K) and pieces of wood, with which water is drawn [ for irrigating land ] by means of ropes, or cords, (M,) [app. held and drawn at one end by a man, and at the other end ] tied to a tall palm-trunk: (M, K:) it is a bucket ( dalow ), and the like, with pieces of wood made in the form of a cross, [i. e. with two pieces of wood placed across and so tied together, ] the two arms of which are bound to the top [or rim ] of the bucket; them one end of a rope is tied to it, and the other end to a palm-trunk standing at the head of the well; and one irrigates [ land ] with it [app. by drawing and swinging it up by means of another, or of the same, rope ]: the word is of the measure faAEilapN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlapN [because it is pulled up]: the pl. is dawaAlK : El-Fárábee deviates from others, by explaining it as meaning a manojanuwn ; and J follows him: (Msb:) [a similar apparatus for irrigating land is used in the northern parts of Egypt, called qaTowap and ↓ dalow : it consists of a bowl-shaped bucket, with four cords attached to its rim: two men, each holding two of the cords, throw up the water by means of it into a trough or trench: accord. to Mtr,] the daAliyap is a tall palm-trunk set in the manner of the machine with which rice is beaten [ to remove the husks ], having at its head a large bowl, with which water is drawn [ for irrigating land ]. (Mgh.) ― -b2- Also Land that is irrigated by means of the dalow [or bucket ] or the [ machine called ] manojanuwn [mentioned above]. (M, K.) ― -b3- And the pl., dawaAlK , Unripe dates hung, and eaten when they become ripe. (T, K.) Hung fruit. (Bd in liii. 8. [But perhaps Alvmr is there a mistranscription for Alt~moru .]) ― -b4- Also (i. e. the pl.) Black grapes, but not intensely black, (AHn, M, K,) the bunches of which are the largest of all bunches, appearing like goats hung [ upon the vines ]: the berries thereof are coarse, breaking in the mouth, and round; and are dried. (AHn, M.) [See also dawaAliY~u , in art. dwAl .) ― -b5- [The sing. also signifies A grape-vine itself: and a shoot of a grape-vine: pl. as above.]

sourceDefinition: , (JK, and so in some copies of the K,) or A_il~aA dahK falaA dahK , (As, IAar, S, TA, and so in copies of the K,) a saying of the Arabs, meaning If this thing be not now, it will not be after the present time: (As, S, K:) As says, I know not its origin, but I think it to be Pers., and to mean, if thou strike not him, or it, now, thou wilt not strike him, or it, ever: (S:) accord. to IAar, it is said to a man when he is at the point of accomplishing his want in respect of a creditor of his, or in respect of his blood-revenge, or in respect of paying honour to a friend of his; (TA;) and means if thou seize not the opportunity now, thou wilt never meet with it: (K, TA:) accord. to Lth, (TA,) it means, if thou avenge not his blood, or if thou slay him not in blood-revenge, now, thou wilt never do so. (JK, TA.) Accord. to As, one says also, laA dahK falaA dahK , meaning I will not accept either of the two actions proposed. (TA.) Az says that this saying shows dh to be Pers., and to mean The act of striking: you say to a man, ↓ diho , meaning Strike thou: and he says, I have seen it written with kesr in the book of AZ. (TA.) ↓ diho in Pers. means Give thou: and metonymically, the act of striking. (TA.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. *aboHN (S, Msb, K, &c.) and *ubaAHN , (K,) He cut, or divided, lengthwise; clave; split; slit; rent, or rent open; ripped, or ripped open. (S, Msb, K.) [Accord. to Fei,] this is the primary signification. (Msb.) [But see what follows.] You say, *abaHa faA^orapa Almisoka (assumed tropical:) He (a perfumer, A) ripped open the follicle, or vesicle, of mush, (A, TA,) and took forth the mush that was in it. (TA.) [In the A and TA this is said to be tropical; the authors evidently holding it to be from *abaHa in the sense here next following.] ― -b2- He slaughtered [for food, or sacrificed, ] (L, TA) and animal, (Msb,) or a sheep or goat, (S, TA,) or an ox or a cow, and a sheep or goat, and the like, (Mgh,) [ in the manner prescribed by the law, i. e.,] by cutting the wadajaAni [or two external jugular veins ], (Mgh,) or by cutting the throat, from beneath, at the part next the head: (L, TA:) accord. to the K, i. q. naHara : but correctly, Al*~aboHu is in the throat; and Aln~aHoru is in the pit above the breast, between the collar-bones, where camels are stabbed: the latter word is used in relation to camels and bulls and cows; and the former, in relation to other animals: or, not improbably, both may have originally signified the causing the soul to depart by wounding the throat, or the pit above the breast, which is the stabbing-place in the camel; and may then have been applied in peculiar [and different] senses by the lawyers. (MF. [See also *akaApN , in art. *kw .]) Also (assumed tropical:) He slaughtered, or slew, in any manner. (L.) [You say, *abaHa Eanohu He slaughtered, or sacrificed, for him, by way of expiation. ] And *abaHa baEoDuhumo baEoDFA (assumed tropical:) [ They slaughtered, or slew, one another ]. (S, K.) definition: An animal prepared for slaughter [or sacrifice;
sourceDefinition: An animal prepared for slaughter [or sacrifice; i. e. an intended victim ]: (T, A, Msb, TA:) [see also *abiyHN , which occurs in this sense in a trad. as applied to a human being:] or an animal that is slaughtered [or sacrificed ]; (S, Mgh, K, TA;) and so ↓ *abiyHapN ; (Mgh, Msb;) or this signifies a slaughtered [or sacrificed ] sheep or goat; (TA;) and is [nominally] fem. of *abiyHN , but the p is affixed only because the quality of a subst. is predominant in it: (S:) or the *abiyHN is added to denote that the word is applied to a sheep, or goat, [ to be slaughtered or sacrificed, ] not yet slaughtered [or sacrificed ]; and when the act has been executed upon it, it is [said to be] *abiyHN : (M, voce ramiy~apN :) *iboHN is applied to an animal that is slaughtered either as a sacrifice on the occasion of the pilgrimage or otherwise; and is like TiHonN in the sense of maToHuwnN , and EiTofN in the sense of maEoTuwfN , &c.: (TA:) the pl. of ↓ *abiyHapN is *abaAy^iHu . (Mgh, Msb.) It is said in the Kur [xxxvii. 107], wafadayonaAhu bidiboHK EaZiymK [ And we ransomed him with a great victim ]. (S, A.) Aljin~i ↓ *abaAy^iHu means Animals sacrificed to the Jinn, or Genii: for it was customary for a man, when he bought a house, or drew forth [for the first time] the water of a spring, and the like, to sacrifice an animal to the Jinn with the view of avoiding ill luck, (A, TA,) lest some disagreeable accident should happen to him from the Jinn thereof: (A:) and the doing this is forbidden. (A, TA.) -A2- See also *ubaHapN .

sourceDefinition: A certain plant which ostriches eat: (S:) this word and ↓ *ibaHN signify the plant called Aljazaru Alb~arY~u , (K, TA,) which is of a red colour: and, accord. to the K, another plant: but correctly a red plant ( nabotN A^aHomaru , not nbt A=xaru ,) having a stem, or root, ( A^aSolN ) from which is peeled off a black peel, whereupon there is taken forth a white substance, resembling a white xzrp [or bead, but perhaps this is a mistranscription for jazarap , i. e. a carrot ], which is sweet and good, and is eaten: [each word is a coll. gen. n.;] and the n. un. is *ubaHapN and *ibaHapN : so says AHn, on the authority of Fr: and he says also, on the authority of AA, that the *ubaHap is a tree that grows upon a stem, and in a manner resembling the krAv [app. karaAv , not kur~aAv ], and then has a yellow flower; its root is like a jzrp [i. e. jazarap , or carrot ], and it is sweet, and of a red colour: (TA:) or the *ubaH is a plant having a stem, or root, ( A^aSolN ,) which is peeled, and there comes forth what resembles the jizr [i. e. jizar or jazar , meaning carrot ]; and a black skin is peeled from it; and it is sweet, and is eaten; and has a red flower. sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of 1]. saEodu Al*~aAbiHi , (S, K,) or saEodN Al*~aAbiHu , (so in one copy of the S,) (assumed tropical:) Two bright stars, between which is the space of a cubit ( *iraAE ), over against one of which ( fiYnaHori waAHidK minohumaA ) is a small star that, by reason of its nearness, is as though it [app. meaning the bright star, or the pair of bright stars,] were about to slaughter it; (S, K;) whence the appellation of Al*~aAbiH : (S:) the two stars [ alpha and beta ] which are in one of the horns of Capricornus; so called because of the small adjacent star, which is said to be the sheep or goat ( $Ap ) of Al*AbH , which he is about to slaughter: (Kzw:) it is one of the Mansions of the Moon; (S, Kzw;) [namely, the Twenty-second Mansion: see also art. sEd : some give this appellation to the Twenty-third Mansion: and some, to the Twenty-fifth; but the two stars above mentioned are clearly the Twenty-second, with the place of which they agree accord. to those who make Aln~aw'u to signify “ the auroral rising ” and those who make it to signify “ the auroral setting: ” see manaAzilu Alqamari , in art. nzl .] The Arabs [used to] say, A_i*aA TalaEa Al*~aAbiHu A@nojaHara Aln~aAbiHu (assumed tropical:) [ When Al*AbH rises aurorally, the barker enters, or betakes itself to, its hole: the period of its auroral rising, in Central Arabia, about the commencement of the era of the Flight, being the 16th of January, O. S.]. (TA.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) A mark made with a hot iron across the throat: or (assumed tropical:) the instrument with which it is made. (L, K.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) Hair growing between the part immediately beneath the lower jaw and the part [ of the throat ] in which an animal is slaughtered. (K.)

sourceDefinition: The place of [ the slaughter termed ] Al*~aboH : (K:) i. e. the place, or spot of ground, where Al*bH is performed: and the part of the throat which is the place of Al*bH , which is that below the part beneath the lower jaw; (MF, TA;) or the Huloquwm [i. e. windpipe ]. (Msb.) ― -b2- (tropical:) The chancel of a church; i. e. the part of a church that is like the miHoraAb of a mosque: (A, * K, * Msb:) pl. ma*aAbiHu : (A, Msb, K:) the ma*aAbiH are the maHaAriyb (S, A, K) of the Christians; (A;) so called because of the oblations ( qaraAbiyn ) there offered; (S, TA;) the maqaASiyr (K, TA) in churches, pl. of maqoSuwrapN ; said to be the same as the mHAryb : (TA:) and the places, (A,) or chambers, (K,) of the books of the Christians. (S, A, L.) You say, gaAdara Als~ayolu fiY AlA^aroDi ma*aAbiHa (assumed tropical:) [ The torrent left in the ground trenches about a span wide ]. (S.)

definition: and ↓ rutayolaA='u A certain genus of hawaAm~ [or venomous creeping things ];
sourceDefinition: and ↓ rutayolaA='u A certain genus of hawaAm~ [or venomous creeping things ]; (S, M, K;) [the genus of insects called phalangium; applied thereto in the present day; and (perhaps incorrectly) to the tarantula: ] there are several species thereof; (K;) many species; (TA;) the most commonly known thereof is [ in its body, app.,] like the fly ( *ubaAb ) that flies around the lamp; another is black speckled with white ( sawodaA='u raqoTaA='u ); another is yellow and downy; and the bite of all causes swelling and pain; (K;) and sometimes is deadly. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, the latter (↓ rutayolaA='u ), A certain plant, the flower of which resembles that of the lily; [app. the plant called (like the insect above mentioned) phalangium, (as Golius states it to be,) and, by Arabs in the present day, zahoru AlEanokabuwti ;] good as a remedy against the bite of the venomous creature above mentioned, (K,) for which reason it is thus called, (TA,) and against the sting of the scorpion. (K.)

definition: Uncleanness, dirt, or filth: or an unclean, a dirty, or a filthy, thing: syn.
sourceDefinition: Uncleanness, dirt, or filth: or an unclean, a dirty, or a filthy, thing: syn. qa*arN : (S, A, Msb, K, TA: [in the CK, Alqadaru is put by mistake for Alqa*arN :]) or $aYo'N qa*irN : (TA:) anything that is disliked, or hated, for its uncleanness, dirtiness, or filthiness: stink, or foul odour: accord. to Az, filth that comes forth from the body of a man: En-Nakkásh says that it is syn. with nijosN ; and it is said in the Bári' that sometimes they say Alr~ajaAsapu waAln~ajaAsapu , meaning that they make these two words syn.: (Msb:) it is also written ↓ rajisN and ↓ rajasN : (A, K:) you say rijosN nijosN , and rajisN najisN ; and IDrd says, I think that they also said rajasN najasN : Pr says that when rjs is followed by njs , the j is with kesr; but when njs is mentioned without rjs , the j and n are with fet-h. (TA.) You say also $aYo'N rijosN [ An unclean, a dirty, or a filthy, thing ]. (A.) And ↓ mar~abinaA jamaAEapN rajisuwna najisuwna , meaning, A company of unbelievers passed by us. (IAar and TA.) As used in the Kur vi. 125, Mujáhid explains Alr~ijos as meaning That in which is no good. (TA.) ― -b2- Any action that is disliked, or hated, for its uncleanness, dirtiness, or filthiness: (Zj, A, K:) a sin, or crime: (Ibn-El-Kelbee, A, K:) so in the Kur v. 92, and vi. 146: (Ibn-El-Kelbee:) an action that leads to punishment: (T, A, K:) as rajosN signifies “ vehemence of sound, ” [see 1,] rijosN seems to mean an action the mention whereof is evil, and highly evil: (TA:) sometimes it signifies a thing that is unlawful, or forbidden: and unbelief: infidelity: (L:) and doubt: (Aboo-Jaafar, A, K:) so in the Kur xxxiii. 33. (Aboo-Jaafar.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) Punishment; (Fr, T, S, A, K;) a sense which Z makes tropical, as being the recompense of rijos [in the sense of “ sin ”], (TA;) and anger: (Fr, S, A, K:) so in the Kur x. 100: like rijozN , which is perhaps formed from it by the change of s into z : (Fr, S:) and sometimes, malediction, or execration. (L.) -A2- A light, or slight, motion. (TA.) -A3- Suggestion of the devil. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A stone which is tied to the end of a rope, and which is then let down into a well, and stirs up its black mud, after which the water is drawn forth, and thus the well is cleansed: (S, K: *) or a stone which is thrown into a well in order that one may know, by the sound thereof, its depth; or that one may know whether there be in it water or not: (IAar, K:) or, accord. to ISd, the name by which this is known is mirodaAsN . (Fr, TA.) And ra$iHa , aor. , inf. n. ra$aHN and ra$aHaAnN , He, or it, was, or became, moist with sweat. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] ra$aHati Alqirobapu biAlmaA='i (tropical:) [ The water-skin sweated with the water ]: and ra$aHa bimaA fiyhi (tropical:) [ It sweated with what was in it ] is said of a [porous] mug, and of any [porous] vessel. (A.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] lamo yaro$aHo lahu bi$aYo'K (assumed tropical:) He gave him not anything. (S, K.) And ra$aHa jalomaduhu , said of one known to be a niggard, (assumed tropical:) He gave something. (Har p. 95.) ― -b4- ra$aHa is also said of a young gazelle, meaning (tropical:) He walked, being trained, or accustomed, to do so by his mother: [because the training him to walk causes him to sweat: see 2: and see also 5.] (A.) Also, said of a gazelle, (assumed tropical:) He leaped, or bounded, and exulted [or was brisk or lively or sprightly ]. (K.) Also, inf. n. ru$awHN , said of a young weaned camel, (assumed tropical:) He became strong: [see, again, 5:] and the inf. n. is metaphorically used in relation to small clouds [app. when they collect together to give rain]. (L.) -A2- See also 2, as said of a she-camel.

sourceDefinition: [ r$~H app. He, or it, caused to sweat: this seems to be the primary signification, whence the other significations here following.] ― -b2- ra$~aHato waladahaA , inf. n. taro$iyHN , (tropical:) She (a gazelle) trained, or accustomed, her young one to walk, so that he was caused to sweat ( fayura$~aHu [perhaps a mistranscription for fayaro$aHu so that he sweated ]): (A, TA:) or she (a wild animal), when her young one became able to walk, walked with him, until, or so that, he was caused to sweat ( Hat~aY yura$~aHa EaraqFA ), and became strong. (Mtr, on the authority of Kh, in De Sacy's “ Chrest, Ar., ” sec. ed., iii. 231.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) She (a camel) rubbed the root of her young one's tail, and pushed him on with her head; and went before him, and waited for him until he overtook her; and sometimes gently urged him on, and followed him; as also ↓ ra$aHatohu and ↓ Ar$Hthu . (L.) ― -b4- ra$~aHato waladahaA biAll~abani Alqaliyl , inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) She (a mother) fed her child with a little milk, putting it into his mouth by little and little, until he became strong enough to such. (S, TA.) ― -b5- taro$yHN also signifies (tropical:) A doegazelle's licking her young one so as to remove the moisture that was upon it at the time of its birth; (K, TA;) and so ↓ tara$~uHN . (TA.) ― -b6- r$~H Aln~baAta , (A, TA,) or Aln~abota , inf. n. as above, (Msb,) (tropical:) It (the moisture, or dew, A, Msb, TA, or the rain, TA) fostered the herbage. (Msb, TA.) ― -b7- r$~H waladahu (assumed tropical:) He fed his child well. (Mtr, on the authority of Kh, in De Sacy's “ Chrest. Ar ” ubi suprà.) ― -b8- And ru$~iHa , (S, A, K,) inf. n. as above, (K, TA,) (tropical:) He was reared, brought up, or educated, and rendered fit, (S, A, K, TA,) and prepared, (TA,) lil$~aYo'i [ for the thing ], and liA^amori [ for the affair ], (TA,) or lilowizArapi [ for the office of wezeer ], (S,) or lilomuloki [ for the office of king ], (K,) or liloxilaAfapi [ for the office of khaleefeh ]; from ra$~aHato waladahaA in the sense expl. in the second sentence of this paragraph; (A;) or ru$~iHa liloxilaAfapi means (tropical:) he was made the appointed successor of the khaleefeh: (TA:) and fulaAnu lika*aA ↓ A^uro$iHa and ↓ tara$~aHa (tropical:) [ Such a one was reared, &c., for such a thing ]. (A, TA.) ― -b9- And ra$~aHa maAlahu , (A,) inf. n. as above, (K,) (tropical:) He managed, or tended, or took care of, his property, or cattle, well. (A, K.) It is said in a trad., yura$~iHuwna HaSiydahaA , meaning (tropical:) They tend [ the place of seed-produce thereof ], and put it into a good, or right, state, or make it to thrive, in order to its becoming productive; like as is done to grape-vines and palm-trees. (TA.)

(A, * Msb.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) A mountain moist in the lower part, (K, TA,) and at the base of which there sometimes collects a little water: when this is much [in comparison with what thus collects, though still little abstractedly], it is termed wa$alN : (TA:) pl. rawaA$Hu . (K.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) What one sees, like sweat, running in the interstices between stones. (K, * TA.) You say, kamo bayona AlfuraAti AlT~aAfiHi waAlwa$ali Alr~aA$iHi (tropical:) [ How great a difference is there between the overflowing Euphrates and a little water that distils scantily in interrupted drops from a rock or mountain, appearing, like sweat, running in the interstices between stones! ]. (A, TA.) ― -b4- The pl. rawaA$iHu also signifies (assumed tropical:) The vuEol [which means a small teat in excess ], (K,) or the A^aTobaA=' [or teats ], (TA,) of a ewe or she-goat, particularly. (K, TA.) ― -b5- And the sing., (tropical:) A young gazelle that walks, being trained, or accustomed, to do so by his mother, so that he is caused to sweat. (A.) And (assumed tropical:) A young weaned camel that has become strong enough to walk, or able to walk with strength: (S, K:) or that has become strong, (As, S, L,) and walks with his mother: (As, S:) pl. ru$~aHN . (L.) ― -b6- And (tropical:) What creeps upon the earth, of such as are termed its xi$aA$ and its A^aHonaA$ . (K, TA.) ― -b7- See also muro$iHN .

(TA.) ― -b2- rafawotu Alr~ajula , (ISk, S, M,) third pers. rafaA , (K,) [aor. and inf. n. as above,] (tropical:) I appeased, or quieted, or calmed, the man; (ISk, M, TA;) as also rafaA^otuhu ; (M and K in art. rfA^ ;) [i. e.] I quieted the man's fear; (S, K, TA;) did away with his fear, like as one does away with a rent, or hole, by Alr~afow [i. e. darning ]. definition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. raqoEN , (Msb, TA,) He patched it; pieced it; put a piece of cloth in the place thereof that was cut or rent; (Msb;) repaired it, (K,) and closed up the hole or holes thereof, (TA,) with [ a patch or] patches; (S, K;) namely, a garment, or piece of cloth; (S, Msb, K;) and in like manner, a skin, or hide; (TA;) as also ↓ rq~Ehu , (K,) inf. n. taroqiyEN : (TA:) or trqyE signifies the patching a garment, or piece of cloth, in several places. (S, TA.) ― -b2- He stopped it up, or closed it up; namely, any hole, or aperture; and so ↓ rq~Ehu ; as in the saying of 'Omar Ibn-Abee-Rabee'ah, wakun~a A_i*aA A^aboSaronaniY A^awosamiEonaniY xarajona faraq~aEona AlkuwaY biAlmaHaAjiri [ And they (referring to women) used, when they saw me, or heard me, to come forth, ( xarajona being used for yaxorujona ,) and close up the apertures in the walls with the eyes and the parts immediately around them ]. (L.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) [ He repaired it in a figurative sense; as also ↓ rq~Ehu .] You say, yaroqaEu diynahu bitawobatihi (assumed tropical:) [ He repairs his religion by his repentance ]. (TA.) And ↓ rq~E dunoyaAhu baA=xiratihi (assumed tropical:) [ He repaired his state, or condition, in the present word by sacrificing his blessings in the world to come ]: whence the saying of 'AbdAllah Ibn-El-Mubárak, nuraq~iEu dunoyaAnaA bitamoziyqi diyninaA falaAd diynunaA yaboqaY walaA maA nuraq~iEu (assumed tropical:) [ We repair our state, or condition, in the present world by the rending, or marring, of our religion, so that neither our religion remains nor what we repair ]. (TA.) And HaAlahu wamaEiy$atahu ↓ rq~E (tropical:) He repaired, amended, or put to rights, his state, or condition, and his means of subsistence; syn. A^aSolaHa , (TA,) and raq~aHa : (K, * TA:) with which latter ↓ rq~E is also syn. as signifying (tropical:) he gained, acquired, or earned, property; accord. to an explanation of its inf. n., trqyE . (TA.) And yaSilu AlkalaAma fayaroqaEu baEoDahu bibaEoDK (tropical:) [ He connects the language, and repairs one part thereof by inserting another ]: said of a poet. (TA.) And ↓ taroqiyEN also signifies (assumed tropical:) [The act of interpolating: or] the adding to a tradition, or story, or narrative. (TA.) ― -b4- ↓ maA raqaEa maroqaEFA [lit. He did not patch a place of patching, or place to be patched; ] means (tropical:) he did not, or made not, or wrought not, anything. (TA.) ― -b5- kaAna muEaAwiyapu yaloqamu biyadK wayaroqaEu biA^uxoraY (assumed tropical:) [ Mo'áwiyeh used to put morsels into his mouth with one hand, ] and spread another hand in order that the portions of his morsels that fell might become scattered upon it. (IAth, Sgh, K.) ― -b6- raqaEa Alr~akiy~apa , (Ibn-' Abbád, K,) and raqaEahaA biAlr~iqaAEi , inf. n. raqoEN , (TA,) (tropical:) He lined, or cased, the interior of the well for the space of the stature of a man, or twice that measure, fearing its becoming demolished, (Ibn-'Abbád, K, TA,) in its upper part. (TA.) ― -b7- raqaEa xal~apa AlfaArisi [lit. He closed up the interval between him and the horseman; ] means (tropical:) he reached, or overtook, the horseman, and pierced him, or thrust him; Alxal~apu signifying the interval, or intervening space, between the piercer, or thruster, and the pierced, or thrust. (O, K, TA.) ― -b8- raqaEa AlgaraDa bisahomK , [and Alr~aqoEapa ,] (tropical:) He hit, or struck, the butt, or target, with an arrow. (K, TA.) raqoEu ruqoEapK also signifies (assumed tropical:) Any hitting, or striking. (TA.) And raqaEa (assumed tropical:) He struck, or beat, in any manner; with a whip; and otherwise; as in the phrases raqaEahu kaf~FA (assumed tropical:) [ He struck him a slap with the hand ]; and huwa yaroqaEu AlA^aroDa birijolihi (assumed tropical:) [ He beats the ground with his foot ]. (TA.) And raqaEa Al$~ayoxu (tropical:) The old man supported himself, or bore, upon his two palms, [as though meaning he struck the ground with the palms of his hands, ] in order to rise. (TA.) ― -b9- [And hence,] raqaEahu , (S, K,) or raqaEahu bqawolihi , (TA,) (tropical:) He censured him, reviled him, or satirized him. (S, K, TA.) -A2- raquEa , (S, TA,) inf. n. raqaAEapN , (S, K,) (tropical:) He was, or became, stupid, foolish, deficient in sense; (S, K, TA;) shattered, or marred, in his intellect; (TA;) such as is termed raqiyE . (S.)

sourceDefinition: A patch; i. e. a piece of cloth, or rag, with which a garment, or the like, is patched, or pieced, or repaired: (S, Msb, K:) pl. riqaAEN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and ruqaEN . (TA.) Hence the saying, AlS~aAHibu kaAlr~uqoEapi fiY Alv~awobi faA@Tolubohu mu$aAkilFA [ The companion is like the patch in the garment; therefore seek thou the one that is suitable ]. (A, TA.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A [ patch, or] trace, or mark, of mange, or scab: (TA:) the commencement of the mange, or scab: (K, TA: [in some copies of the K, AlHarob is erroneously put for Aljarab :]) pl. riqaAEN . (TA.) ― -b3- ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) A piece of land, or ground, adjoining another piece [ which is in some manner distinguished therefrom; i. e. a patch of land, or ground: and in like manner, of herbage]: pl. riqaAEN . (TA.) You say, riqaAEu AlA^aroDi muxotalifapN (assumed tropical:) [ The patches of the land, or ground, are various, or diverse ]. (TA.) And h`*ihi ruqoEapN mina AlkalaA^i (assumed tropical:) [ This is a patch of herbage ]: and maA wajadonaA gayora riqaAEK mino Eu$obK (assumed tropical:) [ We found not aught save patches of green herbage ]. (TA.) ― -b5- [ A note, billet, or short letter: and particularly a short written petition or memorial, addressed to a prince or governor: a ticket: a label: ] a certain thing that is written: pl. riqaAEN (S, K) [and accord. to modern usage ruqaEN also]. Hence the saying in a trad., yajiYo'u A^aHadukumo yawoma AlqiyaAmapi EalaY raqabatihi riqaAEN taxofiqu [ One of you will come, on the day of resurrection, having, suspended upon his neck, billets fluttering ]; meaning, by the rqAE , the claims to be made upon him, or the dues incumbent on him, written on the rqAE . (TA.) ― -b6- A butt, or target, at which to shoot; also termed ruqoEapu garaDK . (TA.) ― -b7- A chess-table; also termed ruqoEapu Al$~iToranoji : so called because it is patched [with squares]. (T A.) ― -b8- (assumed tropical:) The original matter; the substance; (S, TA;) of a garment, or piece of cloth; (S, TA;) or of a thing: (TA:) or (tropical:) the thickness of a garment, or piece of cloth. (Mgh.) You say, ruqoEapu h`*aA Alv~awobi jay~idapN (tropical:) The [ substance or] thickness of this garment, or piece of cloth, is good. (Mgh.) ― -b9- [The pl.] riqaAEN also signifies (tropical:) The lining, or casing, which is constructed in the upper part of the interior of a well when one fears its becoming demolished. (TA.) [See raqaEa Alr~ikiy~apa .]

(TA.) ― -b2- And hence, (O, Msb,) (tropical:) Stupid, foolish, deficient in sense; (S, O, K;) in whose intellect is something needing repair; [so I render fiY Eaqolihi maram~apN ;] (S, TA;) shattered, or marred, in his intellect; (TA;) as also ↓ A^aroqaEu , (TA,) and ↓ maroqaEaAnN ; (S, K;) or unsound in intellect; likened to a ragged, or old and worn-out, garment; as though patched: (Msb:) or a man whose judgment, and state of affairs or circumstances, have become shattered, disorganized, dissipated, marred, or impaired: (A, TA:) fem. [of ↓ A^aroqaEu ] raqoEaA='u , (K,) but this is post-classical; (L, TA;) and [of maroqaEaAnN ] ↓ maroqaEaAnapN . (K.) ― -b3- Hence also, (TA,) Alr~aqiyEu (tropical:) The first heaven; (K;) i. e. (TA) the heaven of the lower world; (S, TA;) [agreeing with the Hebrew term; an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates; for Als~amaA='u Alr~aqiyEu ; and therefore, properly, fem.; though an instance occurs of its being used as a masc. noun, as will be seen below;] so called because it is [as though it were] patched with the stars, or with the lights which are therein; as also ↓ AlA^aroqaEu : (TA:) or the heaven, or sky: (Msb, K:) and also each one of the seven heavens; (S;) each of them being a cover to that which is next to it [beneath, so that each, except the highest, is as though it were patched over by the next above it, the highest being in like manner covered over by the kurosiY~ ,] like as the garment is patched with the ruqoEap : (TA:) pl. A^aroqiEapN . (S, Mgh, Msb.) It is said in a trad., laqado Hakamotu biHukomi A@ll~`hi mino fawoqi saboEapi A^aroqiEapK (S, * Mgh) (tropical:) Verily I have decreed by the decree of God written upon the preserved tablet above seven heavens: (Mgh:) the speaker thus making rqyE masc., as though he regarded it as meaning saqofN . (S, TA.) [See also raqoEN .]

definition: A certain garment worn by the devout Soofees;
sourceDefinition: A certain garment worn by the devout Soofees;; so called because of the [many] patches that are in it. (TA.) [A garment of this kind, a gown, or long coat or cloak, is worn in the present day by many devotees, reputed saints, and darweeshes; and passing from one to another at the death of the former, at length consists almost entirely of patches; and therefore, the more it is patched, the more is it esteemed: it is also called xiroqapN ; and dalaqN , or daliqN , or daloqN , or (now generally by the vulgar) diloq , from the Persian dalaho .] ― -b2- Also thought by A'Obeyd to mean A quiver, or a pouch, much patched: whence the prov., zanodaAni fiY muraq~aEapK [ Two pieces of stick for producing fire, in a quiver, or pouch, much patched: ] an allusion to a poor and unprofitable man. (Meyd.)

definition: , (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. rahaqN , (S, Mgh, Msb,) He, or it, came upon, properly as a thing that covered, him, or it; or came to him, or it; syn. ga$iyahu : (S, K:) and (K) reached, or overtook, him, or it: (ElFárábee, Msb, K:) or it signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (S,) he drew near to, or approached, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) whether he took, or did not take, (S, K,) him, or it: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) or he followed him, and was near to reaching, or overtaking, him. (JK.) It is said in the Kur [x. 27], walaA yarohaqu wajuwhahumo qatarN walaA *il~apN , meaning (assumed tropical:) And there shall not come upon, or overspread, their faces [ blackness, or darkness, nor abjectness, or ignominy ]. (S, TA.) And you say, rahiqahu Ald~ayonu , (Msb, TA,) or dayonN , (Mgh,) Debt, or a debt, came upon him. (Mgh, Msb, TA.) And rahiqatonaA AlS~alaApu , (inf. n. ruhuwqN , Msb, or rahaqN , TA,) (tropical:) The time of prayer came upon us. (Mgh, * Msb, TA.) And it is said in a trad., A_i*aA Sal~aY A^aHadukumo A_ilaY Al$~aYo'i faloyarohaqohu , i. e. [ When any one of you prays towards the thing, ] let him come near to it. (JK, S. [In the Mgh, A_ilaY sutorapK faloyarohaqohaA , i. e. towards a thing that he has set up for that purpose, &c.]) One says also, Talabotu fulaAnFA Hat~aY rahiqotuhu , inf. n. rahaqN , I sought such a one until I drew near to him, and, as it sometimes means, took him, or, as it sometimes means, did not take him. (S.) And Talabotu Al$~aYo'a Hat~aY rahiqotuhu wakidotu A=xu*uhu A^awo A^axa*otuhu [ I sought the thing until I came near to it, and I almost took it, or I took it ]. (Az, Msb.) And rahaqa $uxuwSu fulaAnK , i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one's going, or going forth or away, ] drew near. (S.) ↓ A^arohaqotuhu also signifies I drew near to it; syn. daAnayotuhu . (Msb.) And one says, All~ayolu ↓ A^arohaqakumu faA^asoriEuwA , i. e. (tropical:) The night has drawn near [ to you, therefore hasten ye ]; syn. danaA . (TA.) ― -b2- You say also, rahiqahu bimaA yakorahu , inf. n. rahaqN , He did to him that which he disliked, or hated. (JK.) ― -b3- And rahiqotu A_ivomFA : see 4. -A2- rahiqa as an intrans. v.: see rahaqN , which is its inf. n., below.

definition: i. q. A^ago$aAhu A_iy~aAhu [i. e. He made excessive disobedience to come upon him, properly as a thing that covered him ]; (S, K;) and A^aloHaqahu bihi [i. e. made it to reach him, or overtake him,...
sourceDefinition: i. q. A^ago$aAhu A_iy~aAhu [i. e. He made excessive disobedience to come upon him, properly as a thing that covered him ]; (S, K;) and A^aloHaqahu bihi [i. e. made it to reach him, or overtake him, or befall him ]. (K.) It is said in the Kur xviii. 79, faxa$iynaA A^ano yurohiqahumaA TugoyaAnFA wakuforFA , meaning [ And we disapproved ] that he should make excessive disobedience, and ingratitude, to come upon them twain, by his undutiful conduct, so bringing evil upon them: or that he should couple with the faith of them twain his excessive disobedience and his ingratitude, so that there would be in one house two believers and one who was excessively disobedient and ungrateful: or that he should communicate to them twain his excessive disobedience and his ingratitude. (Ksh, Bd. [See also xa$iYa .]) And one says, A^arohaqaniY fulaAnN A_ivomFA ↓ Hat~aY rahiqotuhu , meaning Such a one made me to hear the burden of a sin, [ as though he made the sin to come upon me as a burden, ] so that I bore it. (S.) And A^arohaqotu Alr~ajula A^amorFA I made, required, or constrained, the man to bear, or endure, a thing, or an event. (Msb.) And rAhqhu EusorFA He made, required, or constrained, him to do a difficult thing: (AZ, S, Mgh, K:) or he made a difficulty to come upon him, properly as a thing that covered him; syn. A^ago$aAhu A_iy~aAhu . (Ksh and Bd in xviii. 72.) And Arhqhu , alone, He demanded of him a difficult thing. (S, Msb, K.) You say, laA turohiqoniY laA A^arohaqaka A@ll~`hu Demand not thou of me a difficult thing: may God not demand of thee a difficult thing. (AZ, S, K.) And A_irohaAqN signifies also The inciting, or urging, a man to do a thing that he is not able to do. (Az, K, TA.) ― -b2- You say also, A^arohaqonaAhumu Alx~ayola We made the horsemen to overtake them, or come up with them: (TA:) or to be near doing so. (JK.) ― -b3- And Arhq AlS~alaApa (tropical:) He delayed the prayer (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA) until it approached the other [ next after it ], (JK,) or until it almost approached the other, (Mgh, K, TA,) or until the time of the other approached. (S, Msb.) ― -b4- And A^arohaqotuhu A^ano yuSal~iYa i. q. A^aEojalotuhu EanohaA [i. e. I hurried him so as to prevent him from praying: see similar phrases in art. Ejl ]. (K.) ― -b5- See also 1, near the end of the paragraph, in two places: ― -b6- and see 3. -A2- Arhqt Ald~aAb~apu Als~aroja : see 4 in art. zhq .

And rAhqhu EusorFA He made, required, or constrained, him to do a difficult thing: (AZ, S, Mgh, K:) or he made a difficulty to come upon him, properly as a thing that covered him; syn. A^ago$aAhu A_iy~aAhu . (Ksh and Bd in xviii. 72.) And Arhqhu , alone, He demanded of him a difficult thing. (S, Msb, K.) (S, Msb.) ― -b4- And A^arohaqotuhu A^ano yuSal~iYa i. q. A^aEojalotuhu EanohaA [i. e. I hurried him so as to prevent him from praying: see similar phrases in art. Ejl ]. definition: The doing of forbidden things: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) wrongdoing;
sourceDefinition: The doing of forbidden things: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) wrongdoing; wrongful, unjust, in jurious, or tyrannical, conduct: (Fr, S, K:) it has this meaning in the Kur lxxii. 13, (S, TA,) accord. to Fr; or, as some say, the former mean ing: (TA:) the doing evil: (AA, K:) and a subst. from A_irohaAqN signifying the inciting, or urging, a man to do a thing that he is not able to do: (Az, K:) lightwittedness; or lightness and hastiness of disposition or deportment; (S, K;) and excessive disobedience: so in the Kur lxxii. 6, (S, TA,) accord. to some: (TA:) foolishness, or stupidity: lightness, or levity: (K:) or ignorance, and lightness of intellect: (JK:) and illnature, or evil disposition: (TA:) and haste: (K:) and lying: (Mgh, K:) in all these senses, [i. e. in all that have been mentioned above as from the K, and app. in others also, above and below,] its verb is ↓ rahiqa , aor. , [meaning He did forbidden things: acted wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically: &c.:] (K, TA:) of which it is the inf. n.: (TA:) and the following meanings also are assigned to it [app. by interpreters of the passages in which it occurs in the Kur]: sus picion, or evil opinion: and sin: accord. to Katádeh: lowness, vileness, or meanness; and weakness; accord. to Zj: error; accord. to Ibn El-Kelbee: and bad, or corrupt, conduct: and pride: and so ↓ rahoqapN , in these two senses: and the commission of a sin or crime or fault; syn. sourceDefinition: , aor. yariy$u , (S, A, Msb, K,) inf. n. rayo$N , (S, Mgh, TA,) He feathered it, namely, an arrow; stuck the feathers upon it: (S, A, * K:) or he repaired it, or put it into a right state, by putting the feathers upon it: (Mgh:) or he repaired, or put into a right state, its feathers: (Msb:) and ↓ ry~$hu , (K,) inf. n. taroyiy$N , (TA,) signifies the same; (K;) and so ↓ ArtA$hu . (TA.) It is said in a prov., fulaAnN laA yariy$u wa laA yaboriY [lit., Such a one neither feathers nor pares arrows]; meaning, (assumed tropical:) Such a one neither profits nor injures. (TA.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) He fed him, and gave him drink, and clad him; namely, a friend: (K:) (assumed tropical:) he clad him, and aided him; namely, a poor man; because such is like a bird with a clipped wing: (TA:) (assumed tropical:) He (God) restored him, from a state of poverty, to wealth, or competence: (TA:) (tropical:) he strengthened his wing, [or power, ] by beneficence to him: (A:) (tropical:) he rectified, or made good, or amended, his state, or condition, (S, K,) and profited him: (K:) (assumed tropical:) he did that which was a means of good to him: or he caused him to attain good: (Msb:) (assumed tropical:) he did good to him: (assumed tropical:) he strengthened him, and aided him to obtain his subsistence. (TA.) In the saying of Dhu-r-Rummeh, raA$a AlguSuwna $akiyruhaA (assumed tropical:) [ Their shoots clad the branches: or surpassed in length the branches: ] it is said to mean kasaA : or, accord. to AA, TaAla : but the former meaning is the better known. (TA.) [It is also doubly trans.:] you say, raA$ahu A@ll~`hu maAlFA (assumed tropical:) God gave him property. (TA, from a trad.) -A2- raA$a , (K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) [seems to have originally signified, when used intransitively, He became feathered. ― -b2- And hence,] (assumed tropical:) He collected ry$ , meaning, property, and A^avaAv [or household goods, or furniture and utensils, &c.]. (K, * TA.) ― -b3- And He (a man) became rich, or in a state of competence: (Fr:) and ↓ try~$ (assumed tropical:) he became wealthy, or abundant in wealth. (Bd in vii. 25.) [See also 8]. -A3- He (a bird) shed many feathers. (TA.)

(IJ, K.) ― -b2- Hence, (B,) (tropical:) Clothing: (ISk, B:) or superb, or excellent, clothing; as also ↓ riyaA$N : (S, K:) or both signify what appears of clothing: (Kt:) the former occurs in the Kur vii. 25, accord. to one reading; (S;) and ↓ the latter accord. to another reading: (TA:) and hence also, the former signifies (tropical:) ornament; and beauty: (A, TA: *) or ↓ both signify (assumed tropical:) property; and plenty, or abundance of the produce of the earth and of the goods or conveniences and comforts of life: (S:) or the former signifies (assumed tropical:) good; or prosperity; or wealth: (Msb:) and (assumed tropical:) state; or condition: (TA:) and ↓ the latter, (assumed tropical:) property: (Msb:) and (tropical:) goodness of state or condition; (A, TA;) or a goodly state or condition: (Msb:) or the former signifies, (K,) and ↓ the latter also, (TA,) (assumed tropical:) plenty, or abundance of the produce of the earth and of the goods or conveniences and comforts of life; and the means of subsistence: (K, TA:) and (assumed tropical:) property which one has acquired for himself: and A^avaAv [or (assumed tropical:) household-goods, or furniture and utensils, &c.]: (TA:) the Benoo-Kiláb say that ↓ the latter word means (assumed tropical:) household-goods of whatever kind, consisting of clothes, or stuffing for mattresses or the like, or outer garments: and sometimes it means (tropical:) clothes, exclusively of other articles or kinds of property. (ISk, TA.) You say, A_in~ahu laHasanu Alr~iy$i (tropical:) Verily he is goodly in clothing, or apparel. (TA.) Respecting the saying, A^aEoTaAhu miAy^ipF biriy$ihaA , it is said, (S, A, * K,) by AO, (S,) that kings, when they gave a gift, put upon the humps of the camels [that bore it] ostrich-feathers, (S, K,) or [other] feathers, (A, TA,) in order that it might be known to be the king's gift; (S, A, K;) and the meaning is, accord. to As, [ He gave him a hundred camels ] with their saddles (S, A *) and their coverings: (S:) or with their coverings and their cloths beneath the saddles. (K.)

(A, and Ham p. 147.) ― -b2- [Hence,] zaj~a biAl$~aYo'i (tropical:) He cast, or threw, the thing from himself: (A:) or zaj~a biAl$~aYo'i mino yadihi , aor. , (TA,) inf. n. as above, (K, TA,) (tropical:) he cast, or threw, the thing from his hand. You say of the ostrich, zaj~a birijolayohi , (A, TA,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) He ran, (A, TA,) throwing out his legs. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence also,] nazalonaA biwaAdK yazuj~u Aln~abaAta (tropical:) We alighted in a valley putting forth herbage; as though casting it from itself. (A, TA.) ― -b5- See also 4. -A2- zaj~a , sec. pers. zajijota , aor. , inf. n. zajajN , It (an eyebrow) was, or became, narrow and long: (TK:) or arched: (MA:) [or narrow and long and full and arched: see zajajN below.]

sourceDefinition: see 4. -A2- zaj~ajato HaAjibahaA , (S, A,) or zj~j HaAjibahu , (K, TA,) inf. n. tazojiyjN , (TA,) She, or he, made her, or his, eyebrow narrow and long: (S, K:) [or made it arched: (see 1, last sentence:) or made it narrow and long and arched: (see zajajN below:)] or clipped the redundant portions of the hair thereof: or lengthened it [ in appearance ] with A_ivomid [i. e. antimony, or ore of antimony, or a black collyrium; like as the ancient Egyptians were accustomed to do, as appears from their paintings and sculptures; and like as some of the Arab women still do; extending a black line towards the ear, and also a similar line from the outer angle of the eye]. (TA.)

definition: [The pointed iron foot, or heel, or shoe, of a spear;
sourceDefinition: [The pointed iron foot, or heel, or shoe, of a spear; ] the iron at the lower extremity of a spear; (S, A, Msb, K;) i. e. the iron which is fixed upon the lower extremity of a spear, and with which the spear is stuck into the ground: the iron which is fixed upon its upper extremity, and with which one pierces, being called sinaAnN : (ISd, TA:) pl. [of mult.] zijaAjN and zijajapN (S, Msb, K) and [of pauc.] A^azojaAjN and A^azij~apN , (TA,) or this last is not allowable, (S, Msb, TA,) accord. to ISk. (Msb.) Zuheyr says, wamano yaEoSi A^aToraAfa Alz~ijaAji faA_in~ahu yuTiyEu AlEawaAliY ruk~ibato kul~a laho*ami [ And he who refuses to yield to the points of the iron feet of the spears shall yield to the upper extremities thereof mounted with every sharp spear-head ]: ISk says, he means that he who refuses to yield to a small thing will encounter a great thing: and Khálid Ibn-Kulthoom says, they used to meet their enemies, when they desired peace, with the iron feet of their spears turned towards them; and if they refused peace, they turned their spears' heads to them, and combated them. (TA.) [By a synecdoche, the pl.] zijaAjN is also used to signify Spears, altogether. (Ham p. 147.) ― -b2- Hence, as being likened to the zuj~ of the spear, (L,) (tropical:) The extremity of the elbow, (S, L, K,) which is pointed: (L:) or the part [or joint ] between the lower extremity of the os humeri and the extremity of the ulna at the elbow: (T in art. Abr :) or [simply] the elbow. (A.) You say, Ait~akaA^a EalaY zuj~ayohi (tropical:) He leaned upon his elbows: and Ait~akaw^uwA EalaY zijaAji maraAfiqihimo (tropical:) [ They leaned upon the extremities of their elbows ]. (A.) ― -b3- [Hence also, (tropical:) A tush, or canine tooth: ] zijaAju AlfaHoli signifies (tropical:) the tushes of the stallion-camel. (A, K.) ― -b4- [Hence also a signification mentioned by Golius on the authority of Meyd, (assumed tropical:) An iron pivot (“ subscus ferrea ”) round which a mill-stone turns. ] ― -b5- Also An arrow-head: (IAar, K:) pl. zijajapN and zijaAjN (K) and A^azij~apN . (TA.)

[of mult.] zijaAjN and zijajapN (S, Msb, K) and [of pauc.] A^azojaAjN and A^azij~apN , (TA,) or this last is not allowable, (S, Msb, TA,) accord. to ISk. (Msb.) Zuheyr says, wamano yaEoSi A^aToraAfa Alz~ijaAji faA_in~ahu yuTiyEu AlEawaAliY ruk~ibato kul~a laho*ami [ And he who refuses to yield to the points of the iron feet of the spears shall yield to the upper extremities thereof mounted with every sharp spear-head ]: ISk says, he means that he who refuses to yield to a small thing will encounter a great thing: and Khálid Ibn-Kulthoom says, they used to meet their enemies, when they desired peace, with the iron feet of their spears turned towards them; and if they refused peace, they turned their spears' heads to them, and combated them. (TA.) [By a synecdoche, the pl.] zijaAjN is also used to signify Spears, altogether. (TA.) ― -b3- zal~a , inf. n. zaliylN and zuluwlN , also signifies He (a man) passed along quickly: (ISh, K:) and zal~a , inf. n. zaliylN , he ran: and zaliylN , a light, or an agile, walking or pacing: (TA:) [and zalalN , mentioned above as an inf. n., seems to have the same, or a similar, signification:] a rájiz says, (S,) namely, Aboo-Mohammad El- Hadhlemee, (TA,) or Aboo-Mohammad ElFak'asee, (O,) A_in~a lahaA fiY AlEaAmi *iY Alfutuwqi wazalali Aln~iy~api waAlt~aSofiyqi riEoyapa mawolFY naASiHK $afiyqi (S in the present art., * and in art. Sfq , * and art. ftq , but in this last with rab~K in the place of mawolFY , and TA,) [i. e. Verily they have, in the year of little rain, (thus Alftwq , as here used, is expl. in the S in art. ftq ,) and in the passing along lightly to the place which is the object of the journey, and in the being removed from a tract which they have depastured to a place in which is pasture, (thus AltSfyq , as here used, is expl. in the S in art. Sfq ,) the tending of a master honest in his conduct, or desirous of their good, benevolent, or compassionate ]: he is speaking of his camels: (S in art. ftq :) he means that they pass along lightly [so I render tazil~u ] from place to place in search of herbage: and Alny~p means the place to which they purpose journeying. (S.) ― -b4- [Hence,] zal~a Eumuruhu (assumed tropical:) His life went, or passed, [or glided, ] away. (K, TA.) ― -b5- zal~ati Ald~araAhimu , (S, Msb, * K,) aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. zuluwlN , (S, K,) or zaliylN , (Msb,) The dirhems, or pieces of money, poured out, or forth: (K:) or were, or became, deficient in weight. (S, Msb, * K.) ― -b6- zal~a , inf. n. zalalN , (K,) said of a man, (TA,) [and app. of a wolf, (see A^azal~u ,)] He was, or became, light [ of flesh ] in the hips, or haunches: (K:) or zalalN signifies a woman's having little flesh in the posteriors and thighs. (S.) -A2- zal~a , aor. yazil~u , accord. to analogy, as an intrans. v., from A^azolalotu A_ilayohi meaning “ I gave to him ” of food &c., should signify He took, or received: and hence the saying of the lawyers, wayazil~u A_ino Ealima Alr~iDaY And he shall take, or receive, or the food [ if he have knowledge of permission, or consent ]. (Msb.) -A3- zul~a i. q. duq~iqa [app. as meaning He, or it, was made, or rendered, thin, or slender ]. (IAar, TA.)

A_izolaAlN , (TA,) He, or it, made him, or caused him, to slip in mud, (K, TA,) or in speech, or in judgment, or opinion, or in religion; (TA;) and ↓ Astzl~hu signifies the same. (S, * MA, K, * PS. (TA.) And in the same, iii. 149, ↓ A@sotazal~ahumu Al$~ayoTaAnu The Devil made them, or caused them, to slip: (Jel:) or, as some say, sought to make them commit a slip, or wrong action. (TA.) ― -b2- One says also, A^azal~a fulaAnFA A_ilaY Alqawomi He sent forward such a one to the people, or party. (TA.) ― -b3- And A^azal~ahu Eano raA^oyihi He made him to turn from his opinion. sourceDefinition: , (S, * Msb, K, &c.,) inf. n. zalozalapN and zilozaAlN and zalozaAlN and zulozaAlN , (K,) or the first of these is an inf. n. [by universal consent], (S,) and so is the second, but the third is a simple subst., (Zj, S, Msb,) though this and the fourth [which is the least known] have the authority of certain readings of passages of the Kur, namely, xcix. 1 for both of these, and xxxiii. 11 for the latter of them, (TA,) He put it, or him, into a state of motion, commotion, or agitation: (Msb, K, TA:) or into a state of convulsion, or violent motion. (Zj, TA.) You say, zalozala A@ll~`hu AlA^aroDa [i. e. God made the earth to quake: or to quake violently: ] (S:) [or] put the earth into a state of convulsion, or violent motion. (Zj, TA) And jaA='a biAlA_ibili yuzaloziluhaA He came with, or brought, the camels, driving them with roughness, violence, or vehemence. (TA.) Some say that zalozalapN is from Alz~alalu fiY Alr~aA^oYi [i. e. “ the making a slip in judgment, or opinion ”]: so when one says, zulozila Alqawomu the meaning is, The people, or party, were turned away from the right course, and fear was cast into their hearts. (TA.) It is said in a trad., Aall~`hum~a A@hozimi AlA^aHozaAba wazalozilohumo i. e. [ O God, rout, defeat, or put to flight, the combined forces, and ] make their state of affairs to be unsound, or unsettled. (TA.) Accord. to IAmb, A^aSaAbati Alqawoma zalozalapN means An affrighting befell the people, or party; from the saying in the Kur [ii. 210], wazuloziluwA Hat~aY yaquwla Alr~asuwlu i. e. And they were affrighted [ so that the Apostle said ]: (L, TA:) or were vehemently agitated. (Ksh, Bd.) ― -b2- maA zalozalotu qaT~u maA='F A^aborada mino maA='i Alvgwbi [or Alv~agabi , as it is written in the explanation of this saying, the latter being app. the right reading], said by Aboo-Shembel, means I have not put into my throat, or fauces, ever, water slipping into it cooler than the water of the vagab [or pool left by a torrent in the shade of a mountain ]. (Az, TA.)

definition: A slip (S, Msb, * K) in mud, or in speech;
sourceDefinition: A slip (S, Msb, * K) in mud, or in speech; a subst. from 1 meaning as expl. in the first sentence of this art.; (S, K:) as also ↓ zil~iylaY : (S: [but this latter is mentioned by Lh and in the K as an inf. n.:]) a slip, or lapse; (K:) a fault, a wrong action, a mistake, or an error; (Msb, K;) or a sin, or crime; (K, * TA;) a fall into sin or crime. (Msb in art. Evr .) One says, zal~a Alr~ajulu zal~apF qabiyHapF The man [ made a foul slip; or] fell into the commission of a disapproved, or hateful, or foul, act; or committed an exorbitant, an abominable, or a foul, mistake: whence the trad., naEuw*u biA@ll~`hi mino zal~api AlEaAlimi [ We seek protection by God from the slip of the learned man]: and the well-known saying, zal~apN AlEaAlimi zal~apu AlEaAlami [ The slip of the learned man is the slip of the world at large ]. (TA.) ― -b2- A benefit, or good action; (Mgh, * K;) as also ↓ zul~apN : (K:) a gift. (Msb.) ― -b3- A feast, or repast, that is prepared for guests. (Lth, O, Msb.) One says, Ait~axa*a fulaAnN zal~apF [ Such a one made, or prepared, a feast for guests ]. (Lth, O, Msb.) Hence, (Lth, TA,) it is also a name for Food that is carried from the table of one's friend or relation: a word of the dial. of El-'Irák: (Lth, Msb, K:) or in this sense it is a vulgar word, (K, TA,) used by the common people of El-'Irák (TA.) And i. q. EurosN [as meaning A marriage-feast ]. (ISh, Az, Msb, K.) So in the saying, kun~aA fiY zal~api fulaAnK [ We were at the marriage-feast of such a one ]. (ISh, Az, Msb, TA.)

definition: One who walks in the manner described in the first sentence of this art.
sourceDefinition: One who walks in the manner described in the first sentence of this art.; as also ↓ zayofN , which is an inf. n. used as an epithet: (TA:) [and so ↓ zay~aAfN , but properly in an intensive sense:] and ↓ zay~aAfapN a she-camel proud and self- conceited [ in her gait ]. (S.) Hence, (TA,) Alz~aAy^ifu signifies The lion; as also ↓ Alz~ay~aAfu ; (O, K;) but the latter has an intensive meaning: (TA:) so called because of his proud and selfconceited walk. (O, TA.) -A2- Also, and ↓ zayofN , (S, Kr, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) the latter an inf. n. used as an epithet, (Msb,) or, accord. to IDrd, this is a vulgar term, (O,) or bad, (K,) applied to a dirhem, or piece of money, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) to gold and to silver, (Har p. 369, referring to the latter word,) Bad: (Kr, Msb, and Har ubi suprà:) or such as are rejected, or returned, because of adulterating alloy therein: (Mgh, O, K:) or, as some say, such as are less bad than what are termed bahoraj , being such as are rejected by [ the officers of ] the government-treasury; whereas the bhrj are such as are rejected by the merchants, or traders: (Mgh:) the pl. is ziyaAfN and A^azoyaAfN , (O, K,) [the latter a pl. of pauc.,] or the pl. of ↓ zayofN is zuyuwfN , and the pl. of zaAy^ifN is zuy~afN : (Mgh, * Msb:) accord. to some, the zuyuwf are such as are done over with a compound of quicksilver and sulphur. (Msb.) [It is implied in the Msb that ↓ zayofN is the more common term, though, as has been stated above, it is said by IDrd to be vulgar: and it is also applied to human beings: for ex.,] a poet says, taraY Alqawoma A^a$obaAhFA A_i*aA nazaluwAmaEFA wafiY Alqawomi zayofN mivolu zayofi Ald~araAhimi [ Thou seest the people to be likes when they alight together; but among the people are bad like the bad of dirhems. ] (TA.)

definition: signifies The pardoning, or forgiving, with goodness.
sourceDefinition: signifies The pardoning, or forgiving, with goodness. (S, O, K.) One says, malakota faA^asojiHo ; (S, A, O, TA;) a prov., relating to pardoning, or forgiving, when having power [to punish or to take vengeance]; (TA;) meaning [ Thou hast become possessed of power, then pardon, or forgive, with goodness; or] thou hast attained thine object, then act with goodness; (A, * TA;) and thou hast obtained power, then pardon, or forgive, in an easy and a good manner: (TA:) it was said by the Prophet to Ibn-ElAkwa', and by 'Áïsheh to 'Alee on the “ Day of the Camel. ” (O.) (Mgh, Msb.)

sourceDefinition: aor. , inf. n. suruwbN , He went forth: and he went away. (M.) You say, saraba fiY AlA^aroDi , (M, A, Mgh, Msb,) aor. as above, (M, Msb,) and so the inf. n., (M, A, Msb,) He went away [ into the country, or in the land ]. (M, A, Mgh, Msb.) And saraba fiY HaAjatihi He went, or went away, (A'Obeyd, M,) or, as some say, during the day, (M,) for the accomplishment of his want. (A'Obeyd, M.) And huwa yasorubu Aln~ahaAra kul~ahu fiY HawaAy^ijihi [ He goes, or goes away, all the day, accomplishing his wants ]. (A.) ― -b2- saraba [or rather saraba fiY AlA^aroDi ] also signifies He (a man) went away at random into the country, or in the land. (Har pp. 448 and 511.) A poet says, (S,) namely, Keys Ibn-El-Khateem, (TA,) ↓ A^an~aY saraboti wakunoti gayora saruwbi [i. e. Whence hast thou gone away at random? for thou wast not one wont to go away at random: ] (S, TA:) thus, srbt , as related by IDrd: accord. to others, [ sarayoti ,] with Y . (TA.) ― -b3- sarabati AlA_ibilu , aor. and inf. n. as above, The camels went away into the country, or in the land, going forth whithersoever they would: and in like manner saraba is said of a stallion [camel]': (Az, TA:) or saraba , (S, K,) said of a stallion [camel], aor. as above, (S,) and so the inf. n., signifies he repaired, or betook himself, to the place of pasture: (S, A, K:) and saraba AlmaAlu , aor. , inf. n. sarobN , the camels, or cattle, pastured during the day without a pastor. (Msb.) ― -b4- saraba AlmaA='u , (A, Mgh, Msb,) aor. as above, (Msb,) inf. n. suruwbN ; (Mgh, Msb;) or sariba , [aor. ,] inf. n. sarabN ; (M;) The water ran (A, Mgh) upon the surface of the ground: (A:) or flowed; as also ↓ Ansrb : (M:) [or the latter signifies it ran swiftly: (see Har p. 586:)] and in like manner one says of the saraAb [or mirage], yasorabu , inf. n. sarabN , it runs. (AHeyth, TA.) And saribati AlEayonu , inf. n. sarabN ; and sarabato , aor. , inf. n. suruwbN ; The Eyn [or source, or perhaps (assumed tropical:) eye, (see masorabN ,)] flowed; as also ↓ tsr~bt : so says Lh. (M.) And saribati AlmazaAdapu , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. sarabN , (S,) The mzAdp [or leathern water-bag ] flowed. (S, K.) And xaraja AlmaA='u sarabFA The water came forth from the punctures made in sewing the skin. (TA.) [Or] saribato said of a new [water-skin such as is termed] qirobap , or of a mazaAdap , signifies It had water poured into it in order that the thong [ with which it was sewed ] might become moistened, so as to swell, and fill up the holes made in the sewing. (M.) ― -b5- See also sarabN , below. ― -b6- [Golius explains saraba , inf. n. sarabaAnN , as on the authority of the KL, as signifying “ Ingressus fuit in rem, totum subivit implevitve locum: ” but this is a mistake, evidently occasioned by his finding sarabaAnN , explained in this sense, instead of sarayaAn , the reading in my copy of the KL.] -A2- sarobN [as an inf. n.] is [also] syn. with xarozN [signifying The sewing of a skin or the like]. (Kr, K, TA. [In a copy of the M, I find Als~arabu Alxarazu erroneously written for Als~arobu Alxarozu .]) You say, sarabotu Alqirobapa , inf. n. sarobN , I sewed the qrbp [i. e. water-skin, or milk-skin ]. (TK.) -A3- suriba , (M, K,) like EuniYa , [i. e. pass. in form but neuter in signification,] (K,) said of a man, (TA,) He became affected with suppression of the feces, or constipation of the bowels, ( A^axa*ahu HuSorN or HaSarN accord. to different copies of the K,) by the entrance of the fume of [ molten ] silver [see A^usorub~N ] into the innermost parts of his nose, and other passages, (K,) or into his mouth, and the innermost parts of his nose, and his anus, (M, * TA,) and other passages: (TA:) the epithet applied to a man thus affected is ↓ masoruwbN : (K:) sometimes he recovers, and sometimes he dies. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ sr~b app. signifies, primarily, He sent camels in a herd or drove, together, to pasture. And hence, ― -b2- ] sr~b EalaY~a AlA_ibila (tropical:) He sent [ against me ] the camels [app. with armed riders], one detached number after another: (As, S, A, K, TA:) and in like manner, Alxayola (tropical:) [ the horsemen ]. (S, A, Mgh, TA.) It is said in a trad. of ' Áïsheh, [referring to girls who were her playmates,] kaAna yusar~ibuhun~a A_ilaY~a fayaloEabona maEiY (assumed tropical:) He used to send them to me [app. party after party, and they would play with me ]. (TA.) And one says, sar~abotu A_ilayohi Al$~aYo'a (assumed tropical:) I sent to him the thing, one by one; or rather, portion by portion. (L, TA.) And sar~abotu A_ilayohi AlA^a$oyaA='a (tropical:) I gave him the things, one after another. (A, TA.) And sar~abahu He sent him back in his srb [i. e. sarob ], meaning way [by which he had come]. (Har p. 20.) ― -b3- See also 4. -A2- sr~b sarabFA He made a subterranean excavation. (M, A.) ― -b2- sr~b AlHaAfiru , (As, TA,) inf. n. tasoriybN , (S, K,) The digger [of a well], in digging, took [i. e. dug ] towards the right and left: (As, S, * K, * TA:) in some copies of the K, [and in the S,] right or left: but the former is the correct explanation. (TA.) -A3- sr~b Alqirobapa , (S, M, A,) inf. n. as above, (K,) He poured water into the qrbp [i. e. water-skin, or milk-skin ], in order that the holes made in the sewing might become filled up (S, M, A, K) by their being moistened, (S, K,) or by the moistening, and consequent swelling, of the thong [ with which it was sewed ]; the qrbp being new. (M.)

definition: Pasturing maAl , (M, A, TA,) i.
sourceDefinition: Pasturing maAl , (M, A, TA,) i. e. camels: (M, TA:) or camels, and maAl [here meaning cattle in general], that pasture: (S:) or maAl [i. e. camels or cattle ] pasturing during the day without a pastor; an inf. n. used as a subst. in this sense; and ↓ saAribN [meaning maAlN saAribN ] signifies the same: (Msb:) or, accord. to IAar, (M,) any maA$iyap [i. e. camels and other cattle ]; (M, K;) thus say IJ and Ibn-Hishám El-Lakhmee: and accord. to Kz, ↓ sirobN also, [q. v.,] with kesr, signifies maAlN [syn. with maA$iyapN ]; and IO says the like: (TA:) pl. of the former suruwbN , (M, TA,) and some say A^asoraAbN [which is a pl. of pauc.]. (TA.) Hence the saying, Ai*ohabo falaA A^anodahu sarobaka , i. e. Go thou away, for I will not drive back thy [ pasturing ] camels; (S, Msb; *) they shall go, (S,) or I will leave them to pasture, (Msb,) where they will; (S, Msb;) meaning, I have no need of thee: (S:) in the Time of Ignorance, they used to divorce by saying thus, (S, M, Msb,) Ai*ohabiY falaA A^anodahu sarobaki . (S, M, A.) ― -b2- [Freytag also explains it, from the Deewán el-Hudhaleeyeen, as meaning A sheep-fold. ] -A2- Also A way, or road; (AZ, S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) and so ↓ sirobN with kesr; (M, K;) the latter accord. to Aboo-' Omar and Th, but' disallowed by Mbr, who knew only the former in this sense; said by Ibn-Es-Seed to have been pronounced by AZ with fet-h, and by Aboo-' Omar with kesr: (TA:) and one's way, or course; (M, K, * TA;) the way by which one goes. (T, TA. [See also surobapN , and masorabN .]) One says, xal~i sarobahu Leave thou free, or unobstructed, his way (T, M, Mgh, Msb, TA) by which he goes, (T, TA,) and his course; (M, TA;) and so ↓ sirobahu , with kesr; (M, TA;) accord. to Aboo-' Omar: (TA:) or xal~i lahu sarobahu leave thou free, or unobstructed, to him his way. (S, A.) And A^aTolaqa AlA^asiyra waxal~aY sarobahu [ He loosed the captive and left free to him his way ]. (A.) Hence, in a trad., mano A^aSobaHa A=minFA fiY sarobihi , meaning fiY mutaqal~abihi and mutaSar~afihi [i. e. He who has become secure in his scope, or room, for free action ]: or, accord. to one reading, the last words are fiY ↓ sirobihi , meaning, (tropical:) in respect of his wives, or women under covert, and his household, or family; a metaphorical sense, from the sirob of gazelles &c. (A, and so in the Fáïk. [See also sirobN .]) Hence also the saying, A_i*aA kaAn muxal~aY Als~arobi , meaning When he is made to be in ample circumstances; not straitened. (Mgh.) And you say waAsiEu Als~arobi , instead of Als~irobi ; meaning Whose way that he pursues is ample. (TA. [But see what follows.]) -A3- Also The bosom, or breast; or the mind; syn. SadorN . (Mbr, M, K.) A_in~ahu lawaAsiEu Als~arobi means Verily he is of ample bosom, or mind; and judgment; and love: (M, TA:) or, as some say, ample of bosom, or mind; slow of anger. (M. [The latter meaning is assigned in the Msb and TA to waAsiEu Alsirobi : see the next paragraph.])
