sourceDefinition: : see saAribN . ― -b2- [Hence, app.,] A qaTiyE , (S, M, K,) or jamaAEap , (Mgh, Msb,) [i. e. herd, ] of gazelles, (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) and of oxen, (M, Mgh, Msb,) [app. meaning wild oxen,] and of [wild] asses, (M,) and of wild animals [in general], (S, Msb,) and [ a flock or herd ] of sheep or goats, (M,) and [ a flock ] of the birds called qaTFA , (S, Msb,) and of birds [in general], (M,) and [ a party, or bevy, ] of women, (S, M, Msb, K,) &c.; (K;) and, as used by El-' Ajjáj, it is of men also: (Sh, TA:) and a poet of the Jinn, as they assert, used it metaphorically in speaking of a sirob of the [lizards called] EaZaA=' : (M:) it signifies also (assumed tropical:) a collection of palm-trees; (M, K; in some copies of the latter of which Aln~aHol is erroneously put for Aln~axol ; TA;) so says AHn; and Abu-l-Hasan thinks it to be by way of comparison: and ↓ surobapN is like it [in its meanings]: (M: [particularly mentioned in the K as used in the last of the senses above mentioned:]) each of these words is said to be applied to a qTyE of the birds called qaTFA , and of gazelles, and of sheep or goats, on the authority of As; and the latter [or each] of them is applied to a qTyE of women as being likened to gazelles: (TA:) the pl. of the former is A^asoraAbN ; (Sh, M, Msb, TA;) and of ↓ the latter, surubN , (K, accord. to the TA,) with two dammehs, (TA,) [in the CK suruwbN ,] or surobN , (so in my MS. copy of the K, [either a contraction of the former pl. or a coll. gen. n. of which surobapN is the n. un.,]) or both. (TA. [See also surobapN below, where the pl. is said to be surabN .]) ― -b3- [Hence, as some explain them, two phrases mentioned below in this paragraph.] ― -b4- See also sarobN , first sentence. -A2- It is also syn. with sarobN as meaning A way, or road: and a course: see sarobN in two places. ― -b2- Also i. q. baAlN [app. as syn. with HaAlN , i. e. State, or condition ]. (S, Msb, K.) One says, fulaAnN waAsiEu Als~irobi , meaning raxiY~u AlbaAli [i. e. Such a one is in an ample, or unstraitened, state or condition: or the meaning may be, such a one is easy, or unstraitened, in mind: see what follows, and see also baAlN ]: (S, Msb:) or, as some say, ample of bosom, or mind; slow of anger: (Msb, TA:) [see also waAsiEu Als~arobi , in two places near the end of the next preceding paragraph:] MF thinks that for baAl we should read maAl , agreeably with an explanation of a phrase in what here follows. (TA.) ― -b3- Also The qalob [meaning heart, or mind ]: (M, K:) and the nafos [meaning self ]. (IAar, M, Msb, K.) One says, huwa A=minN fiY sirobihi He is secure in, or in respect of, his heart, or mind: or, himself: (M:) but IDrd disallows this latter explanation; and says that the meaning is, his family, and his maAl [or camels, or cattle, or other property ], and his, children; as though the phrase A=mn fY srbh were originally used in relation to the pastor, and the stallion [camel], and then extended in its relation to others, metaphorically: (TA:) or the meaning is [simply], his maAl : or, his people, or party: (M, TA:) or as expl. above, voce sarobN , q. v.: or, accord. to Kz, his way. (TA.) The pl. is siraAbN . (El-Hejeree, M, TA.) -A3- See also masorubapN .

definition: A subterranean excavation: (M, K:) or a habitation (S, Mgh, Msb, TA) of a wild animal, (S, * Msb,) in, (S, Mgh, Msb,) or beneath, (TA,) the earth, or ground, (S, Mgh, Msb, TA,) having no passage through it;
sourceDefinition: A subterranean excavation: (M, K:) or a habitation (S, Mgh, Msb, TA) of a wild animal, (S, * Msb,) in, (S, Mgh, Msb,) or beneath, (TA,) the earth, or ground, (S, Mgh, Msb, TA,) having no passage through it; also called wakorN : (Msb:) such as has a passage through it is termed nafaqN : (Mgh, Msb:) the burrow, or hole, (M, K,) of a wild animal, (K,) or of a fox, and likewise [the den ] of a lion, and of a hyena, and of a wolf; and the place into which a wild animal enters: (M:) pl. A^asoraAbN . (M, A, Msb.) In the saying in the Kur [xviii. 60], faA@t~axa*a sabiylahu fiY A@lobaHori sarabFA [ And it (the fish) took its way into the sea &c.], Fr says that when the fish was restored to life by the water that came upon it from the fountain [of life], and fell into the sea, its way became congealed, and like a sarab [or subterranean excavation, &c.]: Zj says that srbA may be considered as put in the accus. case in two ways; either as a second objective complement of the verb, or as an inf. n. [of ↓ sariba , q. v.]: and AHát thinks that it here means *ahaAbFA [ going away ]: or, accord. to IAth, sarabN signifies a secret, or hidden, place of passage: or, as used by El-Moatarid Edh-Dhafaree, it means [simply] a road, or way. (TA.) It signifies also A subterranean channel or conduit, by which water enters a HaAy^iT [or garden, or walled garden of palm-trees ]. (M, K.) And TariyqN sarabN means A way, or road, in which people follow one another continuously. (M.) ― -b2- Also Flowing water: (M, K: [see also saribN :]) or water flowing from a mazaAdap [or leathern water-bag ] and the like: (S:) or water dropping from the punctures made in the sewing of a water-skin. (A.) ― -b3- And Water that is poured into a qirobap [or skin for water or milk ], (M, K,) when it is new, or into a mazaAdap [or leathern water-bag ], (M,) in order that the thong [ with which it is sewed ] may become moistened, (M, K,) so as to swell, and fill up the holes made in the sewing. (M.)

sourceDefinition: A short journey; (IAar, M;) or so ↓ sarobapN . (K. [But I think that the former is the right.]) You say, A_in~aka laturiydu surobapF Verily thou desirest a short journey. (IAar, M.) definition: Going forth: and going away;
sourceDefinition: Going forth: and going away; as also ↓ sirobN ; the latter expl. by IAar as syn. with *aAhibN and maADK : (M: [in one place in the TA the latter is erroneously written syrb :]) or going away at random into the country, or in the land. (S, K.) See also sarobN , first sentence. You say maAlN saAribN , (A,) and faHolN saAribN , (TA,) i. e. [ Camels, or cattle, and a stallion-camel, ] repairing to the place of pasture: (A, TA:) and ZayobapN saAribN (M) or saAribapN (TA) [ a she-gazelle ] going away in her place of pasture. (M, TA.) A poet says, (S, M,) namely, El-Akhnas Ibn-Shiháb ElTeghlibee, (TA,) wakul~u A^unaAsK qaArabuwA qayoda faHolihimo wanaHonu xalaEonaA qayodahu fahuwa saAribu [ And all other men have contracted the shackles of their stallion-camel; but we have pulled off his shackles, and he is going away whithersoever he will in his place of pasture ]: (S, M, TA: but in the last, HalalonaA is put in the place of xalaEonaA : [in the Ham (p. 347) it begins thus: A^araY kul~a qawomK :]) this, says As, is a prov.; meaning [other] men have abode in one place, not daring to remove to another, and have contracted the shackles of their stallion, that is, confined him, that he may not advance, and be followed by their [other] camels; fearing a hostile attack upon them: but we are people of might, wandering about the land, and going whithersoever we will; and we have pulled off the shackles of our stallion, that he may go whither he will; and whithersoever he hastes away to herbage produced by the rain, thither we follow him: (IB, TA:) or it may be that by the fHl he means the chief, whom, Abu-l-'Alà says, he likens to the stallion-camel. (Ham p. 347.) And hence the saying in the Kur [xiii. 11], musotaxofK biA@ll~ayoli wasaAribN biA@ln~ahaAri , (S, M, TA,) i. e. [ Hiding himself by night, and ] appearing by day: (S:) or appearing by day in his way, or road, or in the roads: or, as is related on the authority of Akh, appearing by night, and hiding himself by day; and Ktr says the same of sArb . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. suEaAlN (S, O, K) and suEolapN , (K,) or the latter of these is the inf. n., and the former is a simple subst., (Msb,) [ He coughed: ] suEolapN signifies [the having ] a motion whereby nature expels somewhat hurtful from the lungs and the organs connected therewith: (Ibn-Seenà, K, TA:) wherefore the ducts of the lungs are called qaSabu Als~uEaAli [ the tubes of coughing, meaning the bronchial tubes, ] because it [i. e. what is hurtful in the lungs] has its exit by them. (TA.) One says, A_in~ahu yasoEulu suEolapF munokarapF [ Verily he coughs with an abominable coughing ]. (TA.) And bihi suEolapN [ In him is a coughing; i. e. he has a coughing, or cough ]. (TA.) And A^agoS~aka Als~uw^aAlu faA^axa*aka Als~uEaAlu [ The question, or petition, has choked thee, and consequently coughing has seized thee ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence the saying, ramaAhu fasaEala Ald~ama [ He shot him, and he consequently coughed up blood ]; i. e., he threw [ up ] blood from his chest. (TA. [See the part. n., saEilN , below.])

sourceDefinition: and ↓ siEolaA='u (S, O, K [app. thus, without tenween, as a fem. noun, though fiEolaA' without tenween is unusual,]) and ↓ siEolaY (S, O, TA) The [ kind of goblin, demon, devil, or jinnee, called ] guwl : (K:) or the female of the guwl : (Abu-l-Wefee El-Aarábee, TA in art. gwl ; and Har p. 76:) or the worst, most wicked, or most guileful, of the giylaAn [pl. of guwl ]: (S, O:) or an enchantress of the jinn, or genii: (K:) pl. [of the first] saEaAlK [written with the article Als~aEaAliY ] (S, O, K) [and of the second saEaAliY~u ] and of the third siEolayaAtN , which is said to signify the females of the giylaAn . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] siEolaApN signifies (tropical:) A very clamorous, foul-tongued, woman: (S, O, TA:) accord. to Aboo-'Adnán, a woman foul in face, evil in disposition, is likened to the siEolaAp : but some of the Arabs say that the Arabs do not apply the epithet siEolaApN to any but an old woman. (TA.) ― -b3- And [the pl.] Als~aEaAliY signifies (tropical:) Horses; as being likened to what are [properly] so termed. (K.)

sourceDefinition: Diseased, disordered, distempered, sick, or ill; (S, K, TA;) as also ↓ saqimN : (TA:) or long diseased &c.: (Msb:) pl. of the former siqaAmN , (Msb, K,) like kiraAmN pl. of kariymN . (Msb.) See also misoqaAmN , and musoqimN . The phrase A_iniy saqiymN , occurring in the Kur [xxxvii. 87], as a saying of Abraham, is expl. by some as meaning [ Verily I am ] smitten with the TaAEuwn [or pestilence ]: or the meaning is, I shall be diseased at a future time, when the period shall have come; and it is said that he inferred, from looking at the stars, the time of a fever's coming to him: or it means (assumed tropical:) verily I am sick of your worshipping what is not God: IAth says that, in truth, it is one of his three lies; all of which were for the sake of God and his religion. (TA.) You say also qalobN saqiymN (tropical:) [ A diseased, a sickly, or an unsound, heart ]: and fahomN saqiymN (tropical:) [ Diseased, unsound, faulty, or weak, understanding ]: and kalaAmN saqiymN (tropical:) [ Unsound, faulty, or weak, language ]. (TA.) And huwa saqiymu AlS~adori Ealayohi (tropical:) He is affected with rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite, against him. (TA.)

definition: A kind of tree resembling the xilaAf [q.
sourceDefinition: A kind of tree resembling the xilaAf [q. v.], but not the same as this latter: (TA:) or a kind of large tree, (AHn, K, TA,) exactly like the A^avoA^ab , (AHn, TA,) which is a tree of the figkind, (TA in art. vA^b ,) except that it is taller than the latter, and less broad, having a fruit like the fig ( Altiyn ), which, when green, is [ like ] stone in hardness, but when it ripens it becomes somewhat yellow, and soft, and very sweet, and of a pleasant odour, and people send it, one to another, as a present. (AHn, TA.) [Forskål, in his Flora Aegypt. Arab., p. cxxiv., mentions sqm , which is evidently a mistranscription for swqm , and which he writes in Italic letters “ sokam, ” as one of the names of the ficus sycomorus; and app. of another species or variety of fig which he terms ficus sycomoroides. ]

definition: and ↓ sulaAjimN Tall, or long;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ sulaAjimN Tall, or long; (S, K;) as epithets applied to a horse, and to a man, and to the iron head or blade of an arrow &c.: (K:) or, applied to this last, the former word signifies long and broad: (AHn, TA:) or slender; as also salomajN : and the pls. of these two words are salaAjimu and salaAmiju : which, applied to such iron heads or blades, signify [also] sharpened, or pointed, or sharp-pointed: (TA:) and salaAjimu applied to arrows signifies long in the iron heads. (S.) salojamN and ↓ sulaAjimN are also applied as epithets to a camel: (S, K: [in the former it is implied that in this case they have the first of the significations above; but see what follows:]) thus applied, they signify Advanced in age, and strong: (K:) or the former, so applied, signifies strong: (S voce SaloxadN :) the pl. of each is salaAjimu , with fet-h [to the s ]. (S, K.) ― -b2- Also the former, applied to the laHoY [or jaw-bone], Strong, (K, TA,) full-sized, (TA,) and thick, or compact. (K, TA.) And, applied to a head, Long in the laHoyaAni [or jaw-bones ]. (K, TA.) ― -b3- Also A well ancient ( EaAdiy~apN ) and having much water. (K.) -A2- salojamN is also the name of A certain well-known plant; (K, TA;) of those termed buquwl ; which is eaten; (TA;) [namely, colza; or brassica napus oleifera: so in the present day:] it is an arabicized word, [from the Pers. $alogamo ,] originally with $ , but pronounced by the Arabs with s : (AHn, TA:) one should not say valojamN , nor $alojamN , or this is a word of weak authority: (T, K, TA:) Az says that some pronounce it with $ , but that it is correctly with s . (TA.)

definition: Clarified butter;
sourceDefinition: Clarified butter; ghee; i. e. silaA=' of fresh butter, (M, L, K,) or of milk; (L;) it is of the cow, and sometimes of the goat: (S, L:) what comes forth, (Mgh,) or is made, (Msb,) [or clarified, by cooking it, or boiling it, sometimes with an admixture of sawiyq (or meal of parched barley or wheat ), or dates, or globules of gazelles' dung, (see xulaASapN , and qi$odapN , and qilodapN ,)] from the milk of cows, and of goats, (Mgh, Msb,) or sheep: (Msb:) [n. un. with p :] pl. (K.) ― -b2- samonu Alhabiydi [ Decocted juice of the colocynth, or of its pulp, or seed ]. (TA voce xawolaEN , q. v.)

sourceDefinition: [ An hour; ] one of the divisions of the night and the day; (Lth, K, TA;) both of which together consist of four and twenty of those divisions; each of them, when they are of equal length, consisting of twelve such divisions; (TA;) [also termed saAEapN falakiy~apN ( an astronomical hour; fifteen darajaAt of time; sixty minutes of time; ) because sAEp alone is often used in a vague sense, as meaning what is termed saAEapN zamaAniy~apN ; i. e.] a time of night or of day: but used absolutely by the Arabs as meaning a time; a while; a space, or period; an indefinite [ short ] time; and a little while; (Msb;) a [ short or] little portion, or division, [or space, or period, ] of the night and of the day: (TA:) and Als~aAEapu signifies the pre- sent time: (S, K:) pl. saAEaAtN and ↓ saAEN , (S, Msb, K,) [or the latter is rather a coll. gen. n. of which sAEp is the n. un.,] and siwaAEN . (Msb.) It is used unrestricted in the Kur [vii. 32 and in other places], where it is said, laA yasotaA^oxiruwna saAEapF (Msb) They will not remain behind (Bd) for a time, or any while, (Msb,) or the shortest time: or they shall not seek to remain behind, by reason of intense terror. (Bd.) And so in a trad., where it is said, mano raAHa fiY Als~aAEapi AlA^uwlaY Whoso goeth in the first time; not in the first astronomical sAEp , for then it would necessarily mean that he who should come in the latter part thereof would be on a par with the former person, which is not the case. (Msb.) [ saAEapF signifies, as shown above, For, or during, an hour: and awhile; for a little while; during a short time; as in the phrase,] jalasotu Einodaka saAEapF I sat with thee, or at thine abode, for a little while, or during a short time. (TA.) [And fiY saAEapK , In a short time: in a moment. And Als~aAEapa , Now: just now: this moment. And saAEatay^i*K , Then; at that time: or in that hour. ] And mu*o saAEapNK [ A little while ago; ] in the first time near to us: (K in art. Anf :) or this signifies Als~aAEapa [expl. above]. (Zj, T and M in art. Anf .) [And mino saAEatihi At the moment thereof; instantly. Hence, sam~a saAEapK An instantaneous poison. ] ― -b2- Als~aAEapu also signifies (tropical:) The resurrection; (S, K, TA;) the raising of mankind for the reckoning; also termed Als~aAEapu AlkuboraY : (Er-Rághib, B:) or the time thereof: (K:) because of the quickness with which its reckoning will be accomplished: (TA:) or because it will come suddenly upon mankind, in a moment, and all creatures will die at one cry. (Zj, Az, TA.) Hence, in the Kur [liv. 1], Aiqotarabati Als~aAEapu (tropical:) The resurrection [or the time thereof ] hath drawn nigh. (Jel, TA.) And [in vii. 186 and lxxix. 42,] yasoA^aluwnaka Eani Als~aAEapi (tropical:) They ask thee concerning the resurrection [or the time thereof ]. (Bd, Jel, TA.) And [in xxxi. last verse and xliii. 85,] Einodahu Eilomu Als~aAEapi (tropical:) With Him is the knowledge of the resurrection, (TA,) or of the time thereof. (Bd, Jel.) ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) The death of one generation; termed, for distinction, Als~aAEapu AlwusoTaY : as in the saying of Mohammad, when he saw 'AbdAllah Ibn-Uneys, A_ino yaTulo Eumoru h`*aA AlgulaAmi lamo yamuto Hat~aY taquwma Als~aAEapu (assumed tropical:) [ If the life of this boy last long, he will not die until the death of the generation shall come to pass ]: accordingly it is said that he was the last that died of the Companions. (Er-Rághib, B.) ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) The death of any man; termed, for distinction, Als~aAEapu AlS~ugoraY : as in the Kur [vi. 31], qado xasira A@l~a*ayna ka*~abuwA biliqaA='i A@ll~`hi Hat~aY A_i*aA jaA='atohumu A@ls~aA`Eapu bagotapF (assumed tropical:) [ They have suffered loss who disbelieved in, or denied as false, the meeting with God until, when death came to them suddenly ]. (Er-Rághib, B) ― -b5- Also (assumed tropical:) Difficulty, distress, or affliction; and so ↓ Als~aAEu . (TA.) ― -b6- And (assumed tropical:) Distance, or remoteness. (TA.) -A2- See also saAy^iEN .

definition: (S, L, K [in the CK $ajanN , but expressly said in the S to be biAlt~asokiyni ]) A road of a valley;
sourceDefinition: (S, L, K [in the CK $ajanN , but expressly said in the S to be biAlt~asokiyni ]) A road of a valley; (S, L;) or a road in a valley: or in the upper, or uppermost, part thereof: as also ↓ $aAjinapN : (K:) pl. of the former $ujuwnN : (S, L, K:) and of ↓ $awaAjinu : (K:) or ↓ $aAjinapN signifies a valley in which are many trees; (S, L;) or a place in which are $ujuwn , which means tangled trees; (Ham pp. 761-2;) and $awaAjinu is its pl.: (S, L, and Ham p. 762:) or ↓ $aAjinapN signifies a sort of valley producing good herbage: or, as some say, $awaAjinu signifies the upper, or uppermost, parts of a valley; and its sing. is ↓ $ajanN [thus written in the L in this instance], as ISd mentions on the authority of A'Obeyd, but adding that, as such, it is irregular, and that it is more properly to be regarded as pl. of ↓ $aAjinapN . (L.) ― -b2- [Hence,] one says, AlHadiyvu *uw $ujuwnK , (S, Meyd, L, K,) $ujuwn being pl. of $ajonN , with the j quiescent; (Meyd;) a prov., (Meyd, L,) meaning (assumed tropical:) The story is involved, or intricate; (S, Meyd, L;) or has several ways [ in which it may be understood ]; (Meyd;) or has several modes, or manners; and objects of aim: (L, K:) applied to a story by which one calls to mind another: (A'Obeyd, Meyd, L:) the first who said it was Dabbeh Ibn-Udd Ibn-Tábikhah: he had two sons, named Saad and So'eyd: and some camels belonging to him ran away by night, so he sent his two sons to seek them; and they separated; and Saad found them and restored them; but So'eyd went on seeking them; and El-Hárith Ibn-Kaab met him; and there were upon the young man two [garments such as are called] burds ( burodaAni ), which El-Hárith asked him to give to him, but he refused to comply with his desire; whereupon he slew him, and took his two burds: and Dabbeh, when he saw a dark object in the night, used to say, A^asaEodN A^amo suEayodN [“ Is it Saad or So'eyd? ” (see saEodN )]; and this saying of his became current as a prov.: some time after this, having gone on pilgrimage, he met El- Hárith Ibn-Kaab at 'Okádh, and saw upon him the two burds of his son So'eyd, and asked him respecting them; and he answered that he had met a young man wearing them, and slain him, and taken them: Dabbeh said, “ With this thy sword? ” and he answered, “ Yes: ” and he said, “ Give it me that I may look at it, for I think it to be sharp: ” and El-Hárith gave it him: and he took it, and shook it, and said, A_in~a AlHadiyva *uw $ujuwnK ; and slew him with it: whereupon it was said to him, “ O Dabbeh, in the sacred month? ” and he said, sabaqa Als~ayofu AlEa*ola [“ The sword preceded the censure ”): these three provs. he originated. (Meyd.)

definition: Pieces, or cuttings, of trees;
sourceDefinition: Pieces, or cuttings, of trees; (As, A 'Obeyd, K;) n. un. with p : (As, A 'Obeyd:) or bark of trees: (K:) pieces of bark, and pieces of wood, or sticks, or twigs or branches, in a dispersed, or scattered, state; (O, K;) pl. A^a$o*aAbN : (K:) what fall from, or of, the branches of a tree, [ when it is pruned, ] in a dispersed, or scattered, state: or, as some say, the thorns: and the bark: (Msb:) the stumps of the cut branches upon the trunk of a palm-tree, and other portions, which are lopped off; (O;) [i. e., also] the branches thereof which are lopped off: (TA:) and in like manner, (O,) as pl. of $a*abapN , (S,) [or rather as a coll. gen. n. of which the n. un. is with p ,] what are cut off from, or of, the branches of trees, (S, O,) others than palm-trees, (O,) i. e. of the straggling branches, (S,) such as are not in the choice, or best, part thereof: (S, O:) also the superfluous portions of the straggling extremities of the sprigs of sweet-smelling plants, which are pruned, or cut off. (Mgh.) ― -b2- Anything in a scattered, or dispersed, state. (Kt, TA.) ― -b3- (tropical:) Somewhat remaining of herbage [&c.]: (S, A, O, K: [in the first and third of which is added wahuwa AlmaA^okuwlu , app. referring to the herbage of which the remainder is thus called, meaning, “ it being what has been eaten: ”]) pl. as above, i. e. A^a$o*aAbN . (S, O, K. *) One says, fiY AlA^aroDi $a*abN mino kalaA^ (tropical:) In the land is somewhat remaining of herbage. (A, TA.) And one says also, baqiYa Einodahu $a*abN mino maAlK (tropical:) [ There remained in his possession a remnant of property ]. (A, TA.) And maA baqiYa lahu A_il~aA $a*abN mina AlEasokari (tropical:) [ There remained not to him save a relic of the army ]. (A, TA.) ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) Household goods, or furniture and utensils, consisting of what are termed qumaA$ [q. v., perhaps here meaning the meaner sorts thereof, ] &c.: (A 'Obeyd, O, K:) pl. as above. (K, * TA.) -A2- And A dam; or thing constructed, or raised, to keep back the water of a torrent. (S, O, K.)

rawSourceText: A palm-trunk pared (S, O, TA) of its prickles (TA) [or of the stumps of its branches or of its lower branches: see the verb of which it is the pass. part. n.]. ― -b2- (tropical:) Tall; (S, A;) as also ↓ $awo*abN ; (S;) the former as an epithet applied to a horse, (S, A,) from the same epithet as applied to a palm-trunk: (A:) and (assumed tropical:) tall, and goodly in make; (A, K;) and so ↓ $awo*abN ; (Mgh, K;) as though pruned: (Mgh:) and ↓ the latter, applied to anything [meaning any animal], (assumed tropical:) tall, and excellent or of high breed or strong and light and swift: A 'Obeyd says that the former signifies (assumed tropical:) excessively tall, and is applied in this sense to anything [i. e. a man and any animal]: Kt says, after explaining $a*~abotu AlmaAla as it has been expl. above, that he who is excessively tall is as though his frame were disconnected, and not compact; and therefore he is thus termed: but IAmb says that Kt has made a mistake in asserting that this epithet signifies (assumed tropical:) tall, conspicuous for tallness, and that it is from the palm-tree from which the branches have been lopped off, (in consequence of which, as is said in the Fáïk, it becomes taller, MF, TA,) and that he who is (assumed tropical:) conspicuous for tallness is not thus called unless somewhat deficient in flesh: it is applied to a horse as meaning (tropical:) tall, and not very fleshy. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. $irFY (S, Mgh, Msb, TA) and $iraA='N , (S, * Mgh, Msb, * TA,) the former inf. n. the more in repute, (Msb, TA,) and this is of the dial. of Nejd, the latter being of the dial. of El-Hijáz, or the latter may be said to be with medd for the purpose of assimilating it to a preceding word, accord. to El-Munádee, or it may be regarded as an inf. n. of $aAraAhu , (TA,) i. q. baAEahu [in the sense in which this is generally used, i. e. He sold it ]; (S, Mgh, K;) he gave it for a price: (Msb:) and i. q. ↓ Ai$otaraAhu [in the sense in which this is generally used, i. e. he bought it ]; (S, Mgh;) i. e. $araAhu signifies also he took it, or acquired it, for a price: (Msb:) or this and ↓ A$trAh both signify baAEahu [as meaning he sold it ]; (T, * K, TA;) but the former is more used than the latter in this sense: (T, TA:) and both signify also [ he bought it; i. e.] he possessed it by sale; (K;) which is the more usual meaning of the latter: (T, TA:) thus the former has two contr. meanings, (S, Msb, K,) and the latter also: (K:) for the two persons selling and buying sell and buy the price and the thing upon which the price is put; so that each of the things given in exchange is sold in one point of view and bought in another. (Msb, TA.) It is said in the Kur [ii. 203], wamina A@ln~aAsi mano ya$oriY nafosahu A@botigaA='a maroDaApi A@ll~`hi i. e. [ And of men is he ] who sells [ himself in the endeavour to obtain the approval of God ]. (S, * TA.) And in the same, [xii. 20], wa$arawohu bivamanK baxosK i. e. And they sold him [ for a deficient, or an insufficient, price ]. (S, TA.) And in the same [ii. 15], A^uwlaAy^ika A@l~a*iyna A@lD~alaAlapa biA@lohudaY ↓ A@$otarawuA , originally A@$otarayuwA , (S,) [lit. Those are they who have purchased error with right direction, ] meaning, (tropical:) who have taken AlDlAlp in exchange for AlhdY : (Ksh, Bd, Jel:) or (tropical:) who have preferred AlDlAlp to AlhdY : (Ksh, Bd:) [for] of any one who relinquishes a thing and lays hold upon another thing, one says A$trAh ; (K, TA;) which is thus tropically used [as meaning (tropical:) he took it in exchange bigayorihi by giving up another thing ]; (TA;) and hence this saying in the Kur-án. (K, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] $araY binafosihi Eani Alqawomi (tropical:) He advanced before the people, or party, (K, TA,) to their enemy, (TA,) and fought in defence of them: or (tropical:) he advanced to the Sultán, and spoke for the people: (K, TA:) [as though he sold himself for them; the b in bnfsh being app. redundant:] or, as in the Tekmileh, $araY binafosihi A_ilaY Alqawomi (tropical:) he advanced to the people, or party, and fought them. (TA.) ― -b3- And $araY fulaAnFA , (K,) inf. n. $irFY , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He mocked at, scoffed at, laughed at, derided, or ridiculed, such a one: (K:) [and] so ↓ $ar~aAhu . (TA voce jad~aEahu [q. v.: thus there written, perhaps for the purpose of assimilating it to jad~aEahu ].) ― -b4- And i. q. A^arogamahu (assumed tropical:) [ He angered such a one; or did evil to him, and angered him ]: (Lh, K, TA:) and so A^aworamahu , and gaTaAhu [or perhaps EaZaAhu , for both are expl. alike]: all said of God. (Lh, TA.) And faEala bihi maA $araAhu (assumed tropical:) He did to him that which occasioned evil to him; or that which displeased, grieved, or vexed, him; syn. saA='ahu . (TA.) And laHaAhu A@ll~`hu wa$araAhu (assumed tropical:) [ May God remove him far from good or prosperity, or curse him, and do evil to him, or displease or grieve or vex him ]. (TA.) -A2- $araY A@ll~`hu fulaAnFA , (K,) inf. n. $irFY , (TA,) also signifies God smote him, or may God smite him, with the eruption termed $arFY [q. v.]. (K, TA.) -A3- And $araAhu , (K,) aor. , inf. n. $irFY , (TA,) i. q. $ar~arahu , (K, TA,) i. e. He spread it [ to dry ]; (TA;) [in copies of the K, in art. $r , written, in this sense, ↓ $ar~aAhu ;] namely, flesh-meat, and a garment, or piece of cloth, and [the preparation of curd called] A^aqiT . (K.) -A4- $ariYa , aor. , inf. n. $arFY , (S, K,) said of lightning, (S, K, &c.,) It shone, or gleamed, much: (S:) or it shone, or gleamed, (K, TA,) and spread in the face of the clouds, or, as in the T, became dispersed in the face of the clouds: (TA:) and ↓ A$rY signifies the same; (K;) or it shone, or gleamed, consecutively: the latter verb mentioned by Sgh. (TA.) ― -b2- And hence, (S,) said of the nose-rein of a camel, (S, TA,) It was, or became, in a state of commotion, (TA,) or, of much commotion. (S, TA.) [See also 12.]) ― -b3- Also, (K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) He (a man) was, or became, angry: (K, TA:) or he was, or became, flurried by reason of anger. (S, TA.) ― -b4- And, said of evil, or mischief, It spread, bayonahumo among them: (K, TA:) or became great, or formidable; and in like manner said of an affair, or event. (Nh, TA. [See also 10.]) ― -b5- Also, and ↓ Ast$rY , He (a man, S) persisted, or persevered, (S, K,) in an affair, (S,) or in his error, and his corrupt conduct: and the former, said of a man, is like gariYa in measure and meaning [i. e. he persisted, or persevered, in his anger ]. (TA.) One says of a horse, $ariYa fiY sayorihi , (S, K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He per- sisted, or persevered, in his pace, or going; as also ↓ Ast$rY : (S:) or he exceeded the usual bounds therein, (K, TA,) and went on without languor: (TA:) and fiY Eadowihi ↓ Ast$rY he (i. e. a horse) persisted, or persevered, in his running: (Mgh:) and $ariYa fiY lijaAmihi he (a horse) strained his bridle. (A, TA.) And $ariyato Eayonuhu biAld~amoEi His eye persisted, or persevered, in the shedding of tears, the tears pouring forth consecutively. (TA.) -A5- And $ariYa , (S, K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. $arFY , (K, * TA,) He, (TA,) or his skin, broke out with the eruption termed $arFY [q. v.]. (S, K, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. mu$aAraApN and $iraA='N , i. q. baAyaEahu [as signifying He sold and bought with him: and he bartered, or exchanged commodities, with him: that $ArAh has both of these meanings (like bAyEh ) is shown by the fact that mu$aAraApN is also expl. in the TA, on the authority of Er-Rághib, as signifying the same as qibaADN ]. (K.) ― -b2- Also, (Mgh,) inf. n. mu$aAraApN , (TA,) He persisted in contention, litigation, or wrangling: (Mgh:) one says, huwa yu$aAriyhi (T, M, K) He persists in contention, litigation, or wrangling, with him: (M, TA:) or he contends in altercation, disputes, or litigates, with him; or does so vehemently, or obstinately; syn. yujaAdiluhu : (K, TA:) and it is said of the Prophet, in a trad., kaAna laA yu$aAriY walaA yumaAriY [ He used not to persist in contention, &c.]: (Mgh, TA:) meaning accord. to Th, biAl$~ar~i ↓ kaAna laA yasota$oriY [ he used not to persist, or persevere, with evil conduct ]: (TA:) from Aisota$oraY fiY Eadowihi [expl. above (see 1 near the end)] as said of a horse: (Mgh:) or, accord. to Az, (TA,) originally yu$aAriru ; one of the r s being changed into Y . (K, * TA. [See 3 in art. $r : and see also 3 in art. jrY .])

sourceDefinition: and ↓ $aroyaAnN , (S, K,) the former of which is the more in repute, (TA,) the former said to be quasi-quadriliteral, like jiroyaAlN , [and therefore mentioned also in the TA in art. $rn ,] but held by IB to be of the measure fiEolaAnN , (TA in art. $rn ,) A kind of tree, (S, K, TA,) of the EiDaAh [q. v.] of the mountains, (TA,) of which bows are made: (S, K, TA:) n. un. with p : the tree thus called grows in the manner, and of the height and width, of the [ species of lote-tree called ] sidor , and has a yellow, sweet nabiqap [or drupe ]: so says AHn: and he adds, Aboo-Ziyád says, bows are made of the $ryAn , and the bow made thereof is good, but black tinged with redness; its wood being of those woods of which good bows are [ commonly ] made; and they assert that it seldom, or never, becomes crooked: Mbr says that the naboE and $awoHaT [q. v.] and $ryAn are one kind of tree, but differing in name and estimation according to the places of growth; such thereof as is upon the summit of the mountain being the nbE ; and such as is at the base, or foot, or lowest or lower part, thereof, the $ryAn . (Mgh.) ― -b2- Also, (S, TA,) and ↓ $aAriY~N , in which latter the Y is not the Y of a rel. n. but is an affix corroborative of the epithet, as in the cases of A^aHowaru and A^aHowariY~N [or A^aHomaru and A^aHomariY~N ] and Sul~abN and Sul~abiY~N , (TA,) One of the people to whom is applied the appellation Al$~uraApu , (S, TA,) which means the [ heretics, or schismatics, commonly known by the name of ] xawaArij [pl. of xaArijiY~N , q. v.]: (S, M, Mgh, K, &c.:) so called because they said, We have sold ourselves in obedience to God, i. e., for Paradise, when we separated ourselves from the erring Imáms: (S:) or because they sold themselves for the sake of what they believed: or because they said, Verily God has purchased us and our possessions: (Mgh:) but ISk says, because of their vehement hatred of the Muslims: and the author of the K says that it is from $ariYa signifying “ he was angry, ” and “ he persisted, or persevered; ” and he charges J with error in his explaining it as above, from their saying “ we have sold ourselves ” &c.; but this charge is senseless, for J has followed herein more than one of the leading authorities: the author of the K has followed ISd, who, however, adds, as to themselves, they say “ We are the $uraAp ” because of the saying in the Kur ii. 203 [cited in the first paragraph of this art.], and the saying [in ix. 112] “ Verily God hath purchased, of the believers, themselves ” [&c.]; and the like is said in the Nh, with this addition, that $uraApN is the pl. of $aArK ; i. e., it is from $araY , aor. ya$oriY ; or it may be from Almu$aAraApu meaning AlmulaAj~apu : moreover, the part. n. of $ariYa is $arK ; and this has not $uraApN for its pl. (TA.)

definition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor. , (M, Msb,) inf. n. $aq~N , (S, M, Msb,) He cut it [or divided it ] lengthwise; (TA in art. qd ;) [i. e.] he clave it, split it, rived or rifted it, or slit it; so as to separate it; [i. e. he clave, split, rived or rifted, slit, rent, ripped, tore, broke, or burst, it asunder; ] or without separating it; [i. e. he cracked, chapped, incided or incised, gashed, slashed, furrowed, or trenched, it; or clave, split, &c., or cut, it open; ] syn. SadaEahu ; (K;) or [more explicitly] Al$~aq~u signifies AlS~adoEu AlbaAy^inu [ the cleaving &c. that separates ]; or gayoru AlbaAy^ini [ that which does not separate ]; or AlS~adoEu [ the cleaving, &c.,] in a general sense: (M:) and in like manner, [but with an intensive signification, or implying frequency or repetition of the action, or its application to several objects, generally meaning he clave it, &c., much, or in pieces, or in several places, ] ↓ $q~qhu : (M, K:) you say, $q~q AlHaTaba (S, K) wagayorahu (S) i. e. $aq~ahu [but properly meaning He clave in pieces the firewood &c. ]. (K. [In the CK, $aq~a AlHaTaba is erroneously put for $q~q AlHTb .]) ― -b2- [ $aq~a raA^osahu generally means He clave his head, or his pericranium: and sometimes, as in an instance in the K voce $aqaA^a , he divided the hair of his head. ] ― -b3- $aq~a AlEaSaA [lit. He split the staff ] means (tropical:) he separated himself from the community; (S, K, TA;) and particularly, that of the Muslims: because the staff is not thus called but when it is whole, not when it is split: accord. to Lth, ya$uq~u EaSaA Almusolimiyna and ↓ yu$aAq~uhumo signify alike: but they differ in meaning, as will be shown hereafter. (TA.) $aq~a EaSaA Almusolimiyna , K, TA,) said of a xaArijiY~ [i. e. heretic or schismatic], also means (assumed tropical:) He effected disunion and dissension in the body of the Muslims. (TA.) And one says also, $aq~a EaSaA AlT~aAEapi (assumed tropical:) [ He broke the compact of allegiance, or obedience; became a rebel ]. (M.) ― -b4- laA waAl~a*iY $aq~a Alr~ijaAla liloxayoli waAljibaAla lils~ayoli [app. meaning (assumed tropical:) No, by Him who clave men for the riding upon horses, and the mountains for the flowing of the torrent, ] is a saying mentioned by IAar, but not expl. by him. (M. [It is there added, waEinodiY A^an~ahu jaEala Alr~ijaAla waAljibaAla jumolapF waAHidapF vum~a xaraqahumaA fajaEala Alr~ijaAla lih`*ihi waAljibaAla lih`*aA : an expression of opinion which is, to me, by no means clear, though reconcilable with my rendering.]) ― -b5- AlmaAlu bayonanaA $aq~a AlA^abolamapi and AlA^ubolumapi [ The property is divided between us as in the dividing of the Ablmp ; or the cattle are divided &c.;] means we are equal in respect of the property, or cattle: for the Ablmp means the [kind of leaf called] xuwSap , which, when it is split lengthwise, splits in halves: (M:) or, accord. to Aboo-Ziyád, the Ablmp is a herb, or leguminous plant, ( baqolapN ,) to which there come forth pods, like [those of] the bean; and when you split them lengthwise, they split in halves, equally, from the first part to the last thereof: $aq~a is in the accus. case as an inf. n., ma$oquwqN being understood. (Har p. 639.) [See also $iq~N .] ― -b6- $aq~a , (S, M, K,) aor. , inf. n. $uquwqN , (M,) said of the canine tooth of a camel, (tropical:) It [ clave the gum and ] came forth: (S, M, K, TA:) [said to be] a dial. var. of $aqaA^a : (S:) and said of the canine tooth of a child, (M, TA,) in like manner, (TA,) meaning it made its first appearance: (M:) and said also of a plant, [as meaning it came forth ] on the ground's first cleaving open from it. (M, TA.) ― -b7- Also, aor. , inf. n. $aq~N , said of the dawn, (tropical:) It rose; as though it clave the place of its rising and came forth therefrom. (TA.) ― -b8- Also, aor. , (TA,) inf. n. $aq~N , said of lightning, (tropical:) It [ clave the clouds, and ] extended high, into the midst of the sky, without going to the right and left: (K, TA:) so says A'Obeyd: (TA: [see $aqiyqN :]) and ↓ An$q~ and ↓ t$q~q , said of lightning, signify AinoEaq~a [probably meaning the same; (see EaqiyqapN ;) or, as expl. in the S and also in the O, in art. Eq , it was, or became, in a state of commotion, ( taDar~aba ,) in the clouds ]: (M, TA:) or ↓ t$q~q said of lightning means it spread wide and long. (JK.) ― -b9- $aq~a Als~abiyla (K in art. Ebr ) (assumed tropical:) He passed along the way; as though he cut it, or furrowed it. (TK in that art.) And $aq~a Aln~ahora (assumed tropical:) He crossed the river by swimming. (TA in art. qTE .) ― -b10- $aq~a AlmaA='a (assumed tropical:) He opened a way, passage, vent, or channel, for the water to flow forth; syn. bajasahu . (A and K in art. bjs .) ― -b11- $aq~a A^amorahu , aor. , inf. n. $aq~N , (assumed tropical:) He, or it, discomposed, deranged, or disordered, so that it became incongruous, or inconsistent, his affair, or state of affairs. (M, TA.) [A phrase similar to $aq~a AlEaSaA , mentioned above. And so, app., what next follows.] ― -b12- $aq~a AlkalaAma , i. q. qad~ahu [also expl. as syn. with qaTaEahu , which generally means (assumed tropical:) He cut short, or broke off, the speech; or ceased from speaking; but sometimes, and perhaps in this case, he articulated speech, or the speech: compare a signification of 2.]. (M and L in art. qd .) ― -b13- See also 8. ― -b14- $aq~a baSaru Almay~iti i. q. $axaSa [i. e. (assumed tropical:) The eye, or eyes, of the dying man became fixedly open; or his eyelids became raised upwards, and he looked intently, and became disquieted, or disturbed ]: (M, TA:) and (TA) the dying man looked at a thing, his sight not recoiling to him: (S, K, TA:) said of him to whom death is present: (S, TA:) or [simply] the eyes of the dying man became open: (TA:) one should not say $aq~a Almay~itu baSarahu : (S, M, K:) and $uq~a , with damm to the $ , is not approved. (IAth, TA.) ― -b15- $aq~a Ealayohi , (M, K, in the S EalaY~a , and in the Msb EalayonaA ,) aor. , (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. $aq~N (S, M, K) and ma$aq~apN , (S, K,) [or the latter is a simple subst., as seems to be indicated in the M and Msb,] (assumed tropical:) It (a thing, S, or an affair, or event, M, Msb, K) affected him severely; had a severe effect upon him; distressed, afflicted, troubled, molested, inconvenienced, fatigued, or wearied, him: (M:) it was difficult, hard, distressing, grievous, or severe, to him; (K, TA;) and onerous, burdensome, oppressive, or troublesome, to him. (TA.) And $aq~a Ealayohi , [inf. n., app., $aq~N only,] (assumed tropical:) He caused him to fall into a difficult, hard, distressing, grievous, or severe, case: (K, TA:) imposed upon him that which was onerous, burdensome, oppressive, or troublesome. (TA.) And $aq~ati Als~aforapu (assumed tropical:) The journey was [ difficult, hard, or] far-extending. (Msb.) -A2- $uq~a , said of the solid hoof, and of the pastern of a horse or the like, It was, or became, affected with the disease termed $uqaAq , occasioning cracks. (M, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (M, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. mu$aAq~apN (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and $iqaAqN , (S, M, Msb, K,) the latter inf. n. occurring in the Kur ii. 131 and iv. 39 [&c.], (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He acted with him contrariously, or adversely, (S, * M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and inimically; (K;) properly, each of them doing to the other that which was distressing, grievous, or troublesome, so that each of them was in a $iq~ [or side ] other than that of his fellow; (Msb;) or as though he became in a $iq~ , i. e. side, in respect of him: (Mgh:) accord. to Er-Rághib, the inf. n. signifies the being in a $iq~ [or side ] other than that of one's fellow: or it is from $aq~u AlEaSaA bayonaka wabayona SaAHibika [meaning “ the effecting disunion and dissension between thee and thy fellow ”], so that it is tropical: (TA:) or the primary meaning of Al$~iqaAqu is the being [ mutually ] remote. (Ham p. 326.) See also 1, in the first quarter of the paragraph.

sourceDefinition: quasi-pass. of $aq~ahu as expl. in the first sentence of this art.: [i. e. it signifies It became divided lengthwise, cloven, split, riven or rifted, slit, rent, ripped, torn, broken, or burst, asunder; or it became cracked, chapped, incided or incised, gashed, slashed, furrowed, or trenched; or cloven, or split, &c., or cut, open: or it clave, split, &c.:] (S, M:) and in like manner, ↓ t$q~q is quasi-pass. of $aq~aqahu : [i. e. it signifies it became cloven or split &c., or it clave or split &c., much, or in pieces, or in several or many places: ] (M:) or the former signifies [sometimes] it opened so as to have in it an interstice. (Msb.) waA@no$aq~a Alqamaru , in the Kur liv. I, means And the moon hath been cloven (Bd, Jel) in twain, (Jel,) as a sign to the Prophet: (Bd, Jel:) or shall be cloven on the day of resurrection: but the former is confirmed by another reading, waqadi A^ono$aq~a Alqamaru : (Bd:) or, accord. to Er-Rághib, the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) the case hath become manifest. (TA.) One says, An$q~ Al$~aYo'u biniSofayoni [ The thing became cloven, &c., in halves ]. (S.) [And An$q~ minohu It became cloven, &c., from it: and it branched off from it; as a river from another river, and the like. And An$q~ Eanohu It clave asunder from over it, so as to disclose it: see also 8.] ― -b2- [Hence,] An$q~ flaAnN mina AlgaDabi (assumed tropical:) Such a one was as though his interior were filled with anger so that he split. (TA.) ― -b3- And Aino$aq~ati AlEaSaA (assumed tropical:) The affair, or state of affairs, became discomposed, deranged, or disordered: (S, K, TA:) and An$q~t AlEaSaA biAlbayoni , and ↓ t$q~qt , (Lth, M, TA,) (assumed tropical:) the affair, or state of affairs, became discomposed, deranged, or disorganized, by separation: (Lth, TA:) and An$q~ AlA^amoru (assumed tropical:) the affair, or state of affairs, became discomposed, deranged, or disorganized, being incongruous, or inconsistent. (M, TA.) And An$q~t EaSaA AlT~aAEapi (assumed tropical:) [ The compact of allegiance, or obedience, became broken ]. (M.) ― -b4- An$q~ said of lightning: see 1, in the latter half of the paragraph.

definition: signifies The taking the $iq~ of a thing, (S, K,) i.
sourceDefinition: signifies The taking the $iq~ of a thing, (S, K,) i. e. the half thereof. (S.) One says, A$tq~ Al$~aYo'a He took the $iq~ [or half ] of the thing. (TK.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) The taking [or deriving ] a word from a word, (S, K,) with the condition of reciprocal relation in meaning and [ radical ] composition, and of reciprocal difference in form: [and it is of three kinds:] AlAi$otiqaAqu AlS~agiyru is that derivation in which there is a reciprocal relation between the two words in the letters and in the order [ thereof ]; as in Daraba from AlD~arobu : AlA$tqAq Alkabiyru is that in which there is a reciprocal relation between the two words as to the letter and the meaning, exclusively of the order; as in jaba*a from Alja*obu : AlA$tqAq AlA^akobaru is that in which there is a reciprocal relation between the two words in the place [or places ] of utterance; as in naEaqa from Aln~ahoqu . (KT.) [You say, A$tq~ HarofFA or kalimapF or lafoZFA , and A@somFA , He derived a word, and a name, mino A=xara from another; and ↓ $aq~ahu sometimes signifies the same, as is shown by a citation voce raHimN .] ― -b3- [And, as syn. with AixotiraAEN , (see 8 in art. xrE ,)] The constructing, or founding, ( bunoyaAn ,) of a thing of, or from, what is originated without premeditation. (M.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) The taking to the right and left, (S, K, TA,) not pursuing the right, or direct, course, (S, TA,) in speech, and in contention, or disputation, or litigation: (S, K, TA:) or Ai$otiqaAqu AlkalaAmi signifies the taking to the right and left in speech: (so in a copy of the M: [but I think that the right reading is AlAi$otiqaAqu fiY AlkalaAmi , agreeably with what here follows:]) you say, A$tq~ fiY AlkalaAmi , and fiY AlxuSuwmapi . (TK.) See also 6. And [in like manner] one says of a horse, A$tq~ fiY Eadowihi (assumed tropical:) He went to the right and left in his running. (M. [See also A^a$aq~u .]) ― -b5- A$tq~ AlT~ariyqu fiY AlfalaApi (tropical:) The road went [or branched off ] into the desert. (TA. [See also 7.])

sourceDefinition: sing. of $uquwqN ; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) originally an inf. n.; (S, Msb;) An opening forming an interstice in a thing: (Msb:) or a fissure, cleft, chink, split, slit, rent, crack, or the like, syn. SadoEN , in wood or a stick, or in a wall, or in a glass vessel [&c.]: (T, TA:) [or] a place that is ma$oquwq [i. e. cloven or cleft, split, &c.: (see 1, first sentence: and see also ma$aq~N :) and often signifying an incision, a gash, or a furrow, or trench ]: (M, K:) as though an inf. n. used as a subst. in this sense: pl. as above, $uquwqN : (M:) it differs from $uqaAqN , (S, Mgh,) by having a general signification: (Mgh:) accord. to Yaakoob, one says, biyadi fulaAnK $uquwqN (S, Mgh) and birijolihi (S) [i. e. In the hand, or arm, of such a one are cracks, or the like, and in his foot, or leg ]: but [it is asserted that in this case] one should not say $uqaAqN : (S, Mgh: [see, however, this word:]) and hence, $aq~u Alqabori The trench, or oblong excavation, in the middle of the grave: and accord. to As, $uquwqN signifies SuduwE [i. e. fissures, &c.,] in mountains, and in the earth, or ground. (Mgh.) ― -b2- The rima vulvæ of a woman; i. e. the gap [or chink ] between the two edges, or borders, of the labia majora of her vulva: as also ↓ ma$aq~N . (M, K.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) The daybreak. (S, K, TA.) -A2- See also the next paragraph, first and fifth sentences. -A3- And see the last two sentences of the same paragraph.

definition: The half (S, Mgh, Msb, K) of a thing (S, Msb, K) of any kind;
sourceDefinition: The half (S, Mgh, Msb, K) of a thing (S, Msb, K) of any kind; as also ↓ $aq~N : (K:) or the half of a thing when it is cloven, or split, or divided lengthwise; (M;) as also ↓ $iq~apN . sourceDefinition: primarily signifies The half of a garment [ consisting of two oblong pieces sewed together, side by side ]: then it was applied to [ such ] a garment as it is [ when complete: in both of these senses it is used in the present day]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or a piece ( qiToEapN ) of a garment: (Mgh:) or the $uq~ap of viyaAb [thus, and thus only, in the S, meaning of garments and of cloths, for it is of both,] is an oblong piece; syn. sabiybapN musotaTiylapN : (M, K:) [it is often applied to an oblong piece of cloth of those pieces of which a tent is composed: ] pl. $uqaqN and $iqaAqN . (M, Mgh, TA.) One says, fulaAnN yabiyEu $iqaAqa Alkat~aAni [ Such a one sells pieces, or oblong pieces, &c., of linen ]. (Mgh.) ― -b2- Also A piece of a mazaAdap [q. v.]. (B, TA in art. bSr .) ― -b3- And A piece, or portion, [or tract, ] of Hell; likewise pronounced ↓ $iq~apN . (Ham p. 816.) ― -b4- And A far journey; as also ↓ $iq~apN , (S, M, K,) sometimes thus pronounced with kesr: (S:) a far, long journey: a far-extending space: (TA:) or a road difficult to him who travels it: (Mgh:) or [simply] a journey: and i. q. vnyA [so in my copy of the Msb, app. a mistranscription for vaniy~ap , i. e. a mountain-road, &c.]: pl. $uqaqN . (Msb.) ― -b5- And A part, region, quarter, or tract, (Ibn-'Arafeh, Er-Rághib, K, TA,) towards which one draws near, (Ibn-'Arafeh, TA,) or towards which the traveller directs himself, (K, TA,) [like $uk~apN ,] or in the reaching of which one is overtaken by difficulty, or distress; (Er-Rághib, TA;) And ↓ $iq~apN signifies the same. (K.) ― -b6- And Distance; and so ↓ $iq~apN . (K.) ― -b7- See also $iq~N , last sentence but one.

(Mgh.) See also A^asoEadu : and $arajN .

sourceDefinition: [accord. to Golius, A fissure; as from the KL; but not so expl. in my copy of that work. ― -b2- ] An intervening space or tract between two elongated, or extended, tracts of sand, (S, M, * O, K, * [in the last of which Aljabalayoni is erroneously put for Aljabolayoni ,]) thus expl. to AHn by an Arab of the desert, (TA,) producing herbage: (S, M, O, K:) or a rugged tract between two elongated, or extended, tracts of sand, producing good herbage; (M, TA;) so in the T, as expl. to its author by an Arab of the desert: (TA:) pl. $aqaAy^iqu , (T, S, O, K, TA,) expl. by some as meaning sands themselves: (TA:) or a great piece of sand: or a piece of sand between two pieces thereof. (Ham p. 282.) ― -b3- [In the A and TA voce qiT~u , it is used as meaning A slice cut off of a melon &c.] -A2- A rain, (M,) or a violent rain, consisting of large drops, (K, TA,) wide in extent: so called because the clouds cleave asunder from it: (M, K, TA:) pl. as above. (TA.) ― -b2- The pl., $aqaAy^iqu , is expl. by Az as signifying Clouds that have cloven asunder with copious rains. (O, TA.) ― -b3- $aqiyqapu baroqKi , (O, K,) and Eaqiyqatuhu , both as expl. by Aboo-Sa'eed, (O,) A flash of lightning that has spread (O, K) in the horizon, (O,) or from the horizon: (K: [but see $aqiyqu Albaroqi :]) or $aqiyqapN signifies a flash of lightning that has spread in the breadth of the clouds, and filled the sky: pl. as above. (Ham p. 557.) -A3- A headache, (JK, T, TA,) or a pain, (S, O, K,) or a certain disease, (M,) in the half of the head, (JK, T, S, M, O, K,) [i. e. hemicrania, ] and of the face: (JK, T, S, O, K:) or, accord. to IAth, a sort of headache in the fore part of the head and towards the sides thereof. (TA.) -A4- $aqaAy^iqu Aln~uEomaAni , used alike as sing. and pl., (S, O, K,) having no proper sing., (Msb,) or its sing. is $aqiyqapN ; (M, O, Msb;) [The red, or blood-coloured, anemone; ] a certain plant; (M;) a certain red flower; (Lth, O;) well known; (S, K;) the $aqir ; (Msb;) or, as AHn says, on the authority of AA and Aboo-Nasr and others, it is the $aqirap [n. un. of $aqirN ]; and the sing. of $qAy^q is $aqiyqapN : (O, TA:) it is called $qAy^q AlnEmAn because of its redness, as being likened to the $aqiyqap of lightning: (M, K:) or from Aln~uEomaAn as meaning “ blood, ” as resembling blood in colour; (Msb, TA;) so that it signifies “ pieces of blood: ” (TA:) or in relation to En-Noamán Ibn-El-Mundhir, because he prohibited to the public a piece of land in which it abounded: (S, K, TA:) or because he alighted upon $aqaAy^iq of sand that had produced red $aqir , and he deemed them beautiful, and commanded that they should be prohibited to the public; so the $aqir were called the $qAy^q of En-Noamán, by the name of the place of their growth. (TA.) -A5- See also $aquwqapN .

definition: [The bursa faucium, or faucial bag, which is placed behind the palate of the he-camel, and which, when excited, he inflates, and blows out from the side of his mouth;
sourceDefinition: [The bursa faucium, or faucial bag, which is placed behind the palate of the he-camel, and which, when excited, he inflates, and blows out from the side of his mouth; ] a thing resembling the lungs, or lights, which the he-camel protrudes from his mouth when he is excited by lust; (S, O, K;) a skin in the fauces of the Arabian camel, which he inflates with wind, and in which he brays; whereupon it appears from the side of his mouth; so says En-Nadr; and he adds that it does not pertain to any but the Arabian camel, [as is said in the M, and] as Hr says; but this requires consideration; (TA;) [also expl. as] the lahaAp [q. v.] of the he-camel, (M, and Har p. 16,) which he protrudes from his mouth when he brays: (Har ubi suprá:) pl. $aqaA$iqu . (TA.) ― -b2- To this is likened the tongue of the chaste, or eloquent, and able speaker; himself being likened to the braying stallion-camel: (O:) and hence they say of an orator, or a preacher, that he is *uw $iqo$iqapK : (S:) one says likewise of an orator, or a preacher, that is loud in voice and skilful in speech, huwa A^ahoratu Al$iqo$iqapi [lit. He is wide, or ample, in respect of the $q$qp ]: (TA:) and one says, hadarato $iqo$iqatuhu (assumed tropical:) [meaning His utterance was sonorous and fluent ]. (A and TA in art. hdr .) Orators, or preachers, are also termed $aqaA$iq [for *awuw $aqaA$iqa ]: and one says, fulaAnN $iqo$iqapu qawomihi , meaning (assumed tropical:) Such a one is the noble, and the chaste in speech, or eloquent, of his people. (M.) And in a trad. of 'Omar, (M, O, TA,) accord. to A'Obeyd and others, or of 'Alee accord. to Hr, (TA,) $aqaA$iq are assigned to the Devil, in his saying, A_in~a kaviyrFA mina AlxuTabi mino $aqaA$iqi Al$~ayoTaAni [lit. Verily many of the orations, or harangues, are from the $qA$q of the Devil ]; because of the lying introduced into them. (M, O, * TA. *)

(A.) ― -b2- [It is sometimes used in a good sense, but more frequently in a bad sense; and often means He adulterated, vitiated, or sophisticated, it. ] It is said in a trad., ya$ohadu bayoEakumu AlHalifu waAll~agowu fa$uwbuwhu biAlS~adaqapi (assumed tropical:) [ Swearing, and unprofitable speech, attend your selling; therefore mix ye it with alms ]. (TA.) And it is said in a prov., huwa ya$uwbu wayaruwbu (assumed tropical:) He mixes, or confounds, or makes a confusion or disorder, in speech and in actions: (S, TA:) or he says right one time and wrong another time: (As, TA:) or he defends without energy: (TA:) or he is sometimes incited to motion, or action, and defends himself, but without energy, and sometimes he is motionless, and does not become excited to motion, or action; and it is not from [the words $awobN and rawobN applied to] milk: so says Aboo-Sa'eed [i. e. (TA.) [See also art. rwb .] ― -b3- $Ab also signifies He acted treacherously, perfidiously, or unfaithfully: (Fr, TA:) he lied: he deceived in selling or buying: and he acted dishonestly, insincerely, or with dissimulation. (IAar, TA.) ― -b4- [See also Har p. 448; where it is implied that it signifies also He spoke truth, or was veracious. ]

sourceDefinition: inf. n. of 1 [q. v.]. (S, A, &c.) ― -b2- [Hence,] laA $awoba walaA rawoba , occurring in a trad., means There is, or shall be, no dishonesty, insincerity, or dissimulation, nor mixing, in the selling, or buying: so says IAar: or I am irresponsible with respect to this commodity: or, as he is related to have said, thou art irresponsible for its being faulty, or defective. (TA. [See also $awobapN .]) ― -b3- And $awobN (TA) and ↓ $iyaAbN , (S, TA,) [each an inf. n. used as a subst. properly so termed,] or ↓ $iyaAbapN , (so in one copy of the S,) signify A mixture; an admixture; or a thing mixed with another thing. (S, TA.) Thus $awobFA signifies in the Kur xxxvii. 65: (TA:) or, accord. to one reading, the word there is ↓ $uwbFA , meaning a thing with which another thing is mixed. (Bd.) Al$~awobu also signifies [particularly] What is mixed [ with something else ], of water or of milk: (K:) one says, saqaAhu Al*~awoba biAl$~awobi He gave him to drink honey with water, or milk, mixed [ therewith ]: (TA:) or saqaAhu Al$~awoba biAl*~awobi He gave him to drink milk [ mixed ] with honey. (IDrd, TA.) And Mixed honey; as in the saying, maA EinodiY $awobN walaA rawobN I have not mixed honey nor milk such as is termed raAy^ib [q. v.]: (IAar, TA:) or [simply] honey &c.; (A, Msb, TA;) so called because they mix it with beverages; (Msb;) as in the saying, saqaAhu Al$~awoba biAlr~awobi He gave him to drink honey with clarified butter, or with milk. (A.) And Broth; as in the saying, maA Einodahu $awobN walaA rawobN He has not broth nor milk. (S, K: but in the latter, maA lahu .) And $awobN signifies also A piece of dough. (K.) ― -b4- And [the pl.] A^a$owaAbN signifies (assumed tropical:) A medley, or mixed multitude, of sundry sorts: a less particular term than A^awobaA$N , which signifies a medley, or mixed multitude, of the low, or lower, or lowest, sort: (TA, from a trad.:) accord. to El-Jawáleekee, it is an arabicized word, from the Pers. A=$uwbN . (TA in art. w$b .)

sourceDefinition: A virgin in the night of her devirgination: (Ibn-Abi-l-Hadeed, MF:) [either from $aAba having for its aor. ya$uwbu , signifying “ he mixed, ” or from $aAba having for its aor. ya$iybu , signifying “ he became white-headed, or hoary; ” as shown by what follows:] one says, baAtato bilayolapi $ayobaA='a , (S and A in art. $yb , and K in the present art.,) and bilayolapi Al$~ayobaA='i , (K,) She passed the night of a virgin then devirginated, (S, A, K,) and of the virgin then devirginated: (K, TA:) said of a virgin-bride when she is devirginated by the bridegroom in the night in which she has been first brought to him: (A, K, TA:) in the contr. case, when she is not devirginated, one says, baAtato bilayolapi Hur~apK : (S, TA:) and one says also, bilayolapK $ayobaA='a and bilayolapK Hur~apK : (TA in art. Hr :) Z, in the A, mentions the first phrase in art. $yb , and makes it to be tropical, as though the bride were in that night afflicted by an event so severe as to cause the locks of her hair to become white: in the L it is said that the Y in $ybA' is substituted for w , because of [the allusion of the phrase to] the mixing of the sperma genitale of the man with that of the woman; but that `$awobaA=' has not been heard instead of $ybA' : ISd, in the M, mentions it in arts. $wb and $yb ; observing that the Y is said to take the place of w : J, as well as Z and others, mentions it in art. $yb [q. v.]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, M, A, K,) inf. n. SaborN , (M, K,) He confined him; held him in custody; detained, retained, restrained, or withheld, him, or it; (S, M, A, K;) Eanohu from it. (M, A, K.) [Accord. to a copy of the A, ↓ Sb~rhu signifies the same; but this may be a mistranscription. Hence,] Sabarotu nafosiY I restrained, or withheld, myself, or my soul; (S, Mgh;) EalaY ka*aA [ to endure such a thing ]. (Mgh.) 'Antarah says, mentioning a battle in which he was engaged, faSabarotu EaArifapF li*`lika Hur~apF tarosuwA A_i*aA nafosu AljabaAni taTal~aEu meaning Habasotu nafosFA SaAbirapF [i. e. And I restrained thereat a soul patient and ingenuous, that is firm when the soul of the coward yearns: the last word (for tataTal~aEu ) I have here rendered on the supposition that the poet describes the soul of the coward as one that is yearning for home]. (S.) [And hence,] Sabara is also used intransitively: (Msb:) [or as a trans. verb of which the objective complement, namely, nafosahu , is understood:] you say, Sabara , aor. and inf. n. as above, (S, M, Msb, K,) He was, or became patient, or enduring; contr. of jaziEa : (M, K:) or he restrained, or withheld, himself, or his soul, from impatience: (S, Msb:) or he restrained, or withheld, himself, or his soul, from impatience, and his tongue from complaint, and his members from broil: or, accord. to Dhu-n-Noon, he shunned acts of opposition, and was calm in suffering the pangs of afflictions, and made a show of competence in a state of protracted poverty in places where the means of subsistence were found: or, as some say, he endured trial, or affliction, with good manners: or he was contented in trial, or affliction, without show of complaint: or he constrained himself to attempt things that he disliked: or, accord. to 'Amr Ibn-'Othmán, he maintained constancy with God, and received his trials with an unstraitened mind: or, accord. to El-Khowwás, he steadily adhered to the statutes of the Kur-án and the Sunneh: or, as some say, he was content to perish for gaining the approval of him whom he loved: or, accord. to El-Hareeree, he made no difference between a state of ease, comfort, and affluence, and a state of affliction; preserving calmness of mind in both states: (B:) and you also say ↓ AiSoTabara , (S, M, Msb, K,) and ↓ AiS~abara , (S, M, K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, ASobar~a ,]) changing the T into S , but not AiT~abara , for S is not to be incorporated into T ; (S;) and likewise ↓ tSb~r ; (M, K;) both syn. with Sabara ; (M;) or ↓ tSb~r signifies he constrained himself to be patient; (S, TA;) [or he took patience: and ↓ ASTbr , he acquired patience; and he was tried with patience: see SaAbirN .] One says, Sabara fulaAnN Einoda AlmuSiybapi Such a one was patient on the occasion of affliction. (S.) And Sabarotu EalaY maA A^akorahu [ I was patient of, or I endured with patience, or bore with, what I dislike ]. (A.) And Sabarotu Eam~aA A^uHib~u [ I endured with patience the withholding of myself, or the being debarred, from what I love, or like; or I was patient of the loss, or want, of what I love, or like ]: (A:) and Eanohu ↓ taSab~arotu [ I constrained myself to endure with patience the withholding myself, or the being debarred, from it, or him; or I constrained myself to be patient of the loss, or want, of it, or him ]. (L, voce tajal~ada .) And ↓ A^afoDalu AlS~abori Alt~aSab~uru [ The most excellent kind of patience is the constraint of oneself to be patient ]: a saying of 'Omar. (IAar.) And badaniY laA yaSobiru EalaY Albarodi (tropical:) [ My body will not be patient of cold, or will not endure patiently cold ]. (A.) And SaborN signifies also The being bold or daring [ in enduring, or attempting, a thing ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also He made him, or it, firm, or fast; or bound, or tied, him, or it, firmly, or fast. (TA.) [Hence,] Sabarahu EalaY Alqatoli , inf. n. as above, He confined him, namely, a man, and other than man, [ with bonds or otherwise, ] (K, TA,) alive, (TA,) and shot, or cast, at him until he died: (K, TA:) or he set him up for slaughter: (M:) and you say also, qatalahu SaborFA ; (S, M, Msb, K;) and Sabarahu ; meaning he confined him (i. e. a man) to die, until he died; and in like manner you say ↓ ASbrhu ; (S;) which latter signifies also he slew him in retaliation. (T in art. bwA^ .) And qutila SaborFA He (i. e. any living thing) was confined alive, and then shot at, or cast at, until he was put to death: (S:) or he (any living thing) was bound until he was put to death: (Msb:) or he (a man) was bound hand and foot, or held by another man, until he was beheaded: (Mgh:) or he was slain [ deliberately, ] not on the field of battle, nor in war or fight, nor by mistake: (A 'Obeyd:) and Subira he was confined, (A,) or held and confined, (B,) to be put to death. (A, B.) Saboru Alr~uwHi [signifies The confining the living, and shooting, or casting, at him until he dies; as is shown in the TA: but it] occurs in a trad., in which it is forbidden, as meaning the act of gelding, or castrating. (A, TA.) ― -b3- Also, (S, Msb,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (Msb,) He confined him to make him swear, until he swore, or took an oath; as also ↓ ASbrhu : (S:) or he made him to swear a most energetic oath; (Msb;) as also Sabara yamiynahu , (A, Mgh,) which is a tropical phrase: (A:) and ↓ ASbrhu , (TA in art. blt ,) or EalaY yamiynK ↓ ASbrhu , (TA in the present art.,) he (the judge, or governor,) constrained him to swear, or take an oath. (TA.) And Subira He was confined, or held in custody, in order that he might be made to swear, or take an oath. (A.) And Halafa SaborFA He swore, or took an oath, being confined, or held in custody, (S, M,) by the judge, or governor, (M,) in order that he might be made to do so. (S, M.) And Sabara yamiynFA He swore, or took an oath: (TA in art. blt :) and he compelled one to take an oath. (Mgh.) ― -b4- See also 2. ― -b5- Also He clave to him; namely, a man; syn. lazimahu . (M, K.) -A2- Sabaraminohu : see 8. -A3- Sabarotu , (S, [thus in my copies, without any complement,]) or Sabarotu bihi , (M, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. SaborN (S, M, Msb, K) and SabaArapN , (S, Msb, K,) I became responsible, or surety, for him, or it. (S, M, Msb, K.) ― -b2- And AuSoburoniY Give thou to me a surety. (S, K.) -A4- SabaruwA TaEaAmahumo , (so in the CK, [agreeably with an explanation of the pass. part. n. maSobuwrN , q. v.,]) or ↓ Sab~aruwhu , (so in the M, and in my MS. copy of the K, [both probably correct,]) They collected their wheat together without measuring or weighing it; made it a Suborap [q. v.] (M, K.)

sourceDefinition: (S, M, Msb, K) and ↓ SaborN , which latter is allowable only in cases of necessity in poetry, (S, Msb, K,) or it is allowable in other cases, as also ↓ SiborN , agreeably with analogy, (Ibn-Es-Seed, Msb,) [ Aloes; ] a certain bitter medicine; (S, Mgh, Msb;) the expressed juice of a certain bitter tree; (M, K;) the expressed juice of a certain tree of which the leaves are like the sheaths of knives, long and thick, with a dusty and dull hue in their greenness, of rough appearance, from the midst of which there comes forth a stalk whereon is a yellow flower, vmd [but what this means I know not] in odour; (Lth, TA;) it grows like the green suwsan [or lily ], save that the leaves of the Sbr are longer and broader and much thicker, and it contains very much juice; (AHn, M, O, TA;) it is crushed and thrown into the presses, then bruised with pieces of wood, and trodden with the feet until its expressed juice flows, when it is left until it thickens, then it is put into leathern bags, and exposed to the sun until it dries: (AHn, O:) the best sort is the suquToriY~ [i. e. of the Island of Sukutrà ]: and it is also known by the name of ↓ Sab~aArapN [a name now applied to the plant]: (TA:) the n. un. is SabirapN [and SaborapN and SiborapN ]: and the pl. is SubuwrN . A poet says, (S,) namely, El-Aashà, (M,) or 'Amr Ibn-Milkat Et-Tá-ee, addressing 'Amr Ibn-Hind, who had a brother slain, (IB,) mano muboligN EamorFA biA^an~a Almaro'a lamo yuxolaqo SubaAraho (so in the S; but in the M and TA this verse is given differently, with $ayobaAna and A^an~a in the places of EamorFA and biA^an~a ; and it is said in the M that accord. to one relation the last word is SiyaAraho , [with Y ,] which, it is added, is like SubaArah in meaning;) [i. e. (TA.) -A2- See also SabiyrN .

Zj],) ↓ AlS~abuwru signifies The Clement, or Forbearing, who does not hastily avenge Himself upon the disobedient, but forgives, or defers: (Aboo-Is-hák, K:) [it may be well rendered The Long-suffering: ] it is an intensive epithet. sourceDefinition: Stones: or smooth stones: and one thereof is termed SafaApN : [i. e. the former word is a coll. gen. n., and the latter is its n. un.:] the two words being like HaSFY and HaSaApN : (Msb:) or SafaApN signifies a smooth rock: (S:) or a hard and smooth stone, large, and such as does not give growth to anything: (M, K:) and the pl. of this is SafFA [improperly thus termed a pl.] (S, M, K) and SafawaAtN , (M, K,) and (S, M, K) that of SafFA , (M, K, *) not of SafaApN , (M,) A^aSofaA='N and SufiY~N (S, M, K) and SifiY~N : (M, K:) or SafFA signifies stones that are broad and smooth: (ISk, TA:) and [accord. to F,] ↓ SafowaA='u signifies the same as SafaApN , as also SafowaAnapN [in the CK erroneously written SafowaAp ], of which the pl. is ↓ SafowaAnN and ↓ SafawaAnN , (K,) which last is said by El-Háfidh to be a mistaken pronunciation of SafowaAnN ; (TA;) [but correctly,] ↓ SafowaA='u [which is a quasi-pl. n.] and ↓ SafowaAnN [a coll. gen. n.] (As, T, S, M, TA) of which the sing. or n. un. is SafowaAnapN (S, M, TA) signify the same as SafFA , (As, T, M, TA,) or stones, (S,) or soft, smooth stones; (TA;) or ↓ SafowaAnN is used as a pl. and as a sing.; as a pl. meaning smooth stones, one of which is termed SafowaAnapN ; and as a sing., stone, or a stone: (Msb:) the dual of SafFA is SafawaAni . (ISk, TA.) maA tanodaY SafaAtuhu is a prov., (S,) applied to the niggardly, like maA yabiD~u Hajaruhu , (S, in art. bD ,) meaning (assumed tropical:) No good is obtained from him. (TA in that art.) And one says also, qaraEa SafaAtahu , meaning (assumed tropical:) He im- pugned his character; blamed, or censured, him; or spoke against him. (Mgh in art. gmz .) ― -b2- AlS~afaA A certain place in Mekkeh (S, Msb) may be masc. or fem., as meaning either the makaAn or the buqoEap . (Msb.) ― -b3- [ binotu SafFA , accord. to Reiske, as stated by Freytag, signifies The echo. ]

definition: Clearness, limpidness, or purity;
sourceDefinition: Clearness, limpidness, or purity; contr. of kadarN ; (M, K;) like [the inf. ns.] SafaA='N and Sufuw~N [&c. when used as simple substs.: see 1, first sentence]. (K.) (M.) ― -b6- And A palm-tree ( naxolapN ) abounding with fruit; (M, K;) or so ↓ Safiy~apN : (Z, TA:) pl. of the former, (TA,) or of the latter, as above. (Z, TA.)

definition: Clear, limpid, or pure;
sourceDefinition: Clear, limpid, or pure; free from kadar [or turbidness, &c.]; (Msb;) and so ↓ SafiY~N , applied to anything. (M.) Applied to pasturage, the former word may mean Clear of dried-up leaves or similar rubbish: or it may be formed by transposition from SaAy^ifN , meaning “ of the [season called] Sayof , ” and so belonging to art. Syf . (M. [See also SaAfK in another sense as formed by transposition from SaAy^ifN , voce SaAfN , in art. Swf .]) In the phrase All~awoni ↓ SafaApu applied by the poet Kutheiyir-'Azzeh to honey ( janaApu Aln~aHoli ), and expl. as meaning Clear in respect of colour, [ISd says,] I think that SfAp is originally Safiyap , as a possessive epithet. (M.) [ SaAfK is also applied to a sword, and the like, as meaning Bright, or free from rust. ] And in the Kur xxii. 37, [instead of the common reading SawaAf~a , pl. of SaAf~N and SaAf~apN ,] some read SawaAfiYa , [pl. of SaAfiyapN , as well as of SaAfK applied to irrational animals,] as meaning that the animals there mentioned are [to be regarded as ] things purely [or exclusively ] belonging to God. (TA.) ― -b2- See also SafowaAnu . -A2- Also A certain fish, which [ it is said ] chews the cud; pl. SawaAfK . (TA.)

(Kr, M, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. SunoEN and SanoEN , He made, wrought, manufactured, fabricated, or constructed, the thing; syn. Eamilahu : (K:) [or he made it, &c., skilfully, or well; for] AlS~unoEu signifies A_ijaAdapu AlfiEoli ; and every SunoE is a fiEol , but every fiEol is not a SunoE ; and it is not predicated of [irrational] animals [unless tropically, (see A^aSonaEu ,)] nor of inanimate things, like as AlfiEolu is. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] SanaEa signifies also (assumed tropical:) [ He fabricated speech or a saying or sentence or the like:] he forged a word; and poetry, EalaY fulaAnK in the name of such a one. (Mz, 8th nwE .) ― -b3- And SanaEa , inf. n. SanoEN [and SunoEN ] and SaniyEN , [with the objective complement understood,] He worked, or wrought; he practised, or exercised, an art, a craft, or a manufacture. (MA.) ― -b4- And SanaEa A_ilayohi maEoruwfFA , (S, O, K,) aor. as above, (K,) inf. n. SunoEN , with damm, He did to him a benefit, favour, or kind act: and SanaEa bihi SaniyEFA qabiyHFA he did to him an evil, or a foul, deed: syn. faEalahu : (S, O, K:) and one says also [in the former of these two senses], Einodahu SaniyEapF ↓ AiSoTanaEa ; (S, Mgh, K;) syn. Ait~axa*ahaA ; (K;) or A^aHosana A_ilayohi . (Mgh.) The saying maA SanaEota waA^abaAka means maEa A^abiyka [i. e. What didst thou together with thy father? ]. (S.) The saying of the Prophet, A_i*aA lamo tasotaHoYi faA@SonaEo maA $iy^ota [ If thou be not ashamed, do what thou wilt, ] is said to be an instance of an imperative phrase of which the meaning is predicative; i. e. it is as though he said, he who is not ashamed does what he will: (O, L, TA: *) and other explanations of it are mentioned in the O and L: (TA:) [but] this is held by A 'Obeyd to be the right meaning. (L.) In the phrase SunoEa A@ll~`hi , in the Kur [xxvii. 90, which may be rendered By the doing of God ], SnE is in the accus. case as an inf. n.: but one may read it in the nom. case, meaning *`lika to be understood before it. (Zj, O, TA.) One says also, maA A^aHosana SunoEa A@ll~`hi Einodaka and SaniyEa A@ll~`hi [ How good is the doing of God with thee, or at thine abode! ]. (K.) ― -b5- And SanaEotu farasiY , inf. n. SanoEN and SanoEapN , (tropical:) I tended well my horse; or took good care of him; (S, O, K, TA;) supplied him with fodder, and fattened him: and SanaEa jaAriyatahu (tropical:) he reared, or nourished, his girl, or young woman: (TA:) and SuniEati AljaAriyapu (tropical:) the girl, or young woman, was treated [or nourished ] well, so that she became fat; as also ↓ Sun~iEat , inf. n. taSoniyEN : (K, TA:) or you say AiSonaEi Alfarasa , (so accord. to my MS. copy of the K,) or Alfarasa ↓ A^aSonaEa , (so accord. to other copies of the K, and in the O, [in the CK AuSoniEa Alfarasu ,]) without teshdeed; [which seems to indicate that the right reading is SanaEa , agreeably with the reading in my MS. copy of the K which gives the imperative form; though it is stated in the TA that A^aSonaEa Alfarasa is said by IKtt to be a dial. var. of SanaEahu ;] (O, K;) and AljaAriyapa ↓ San~aEa , with teshdeed, meaning he treated [or nourished ] well the girl, or young woman, and fattened her; (O, K; [in my MS. copy of the K San~iEi AljaAriyapa ;]) because the tSnyE of the girl, or young woman, is by means of many things, and by careful tending: (O, K:) so says Lth: (O:) but Az says that by other, or others, than Lth, it is allowed to say SanaEa jaAriyatahu , without teshdeed: and hence the phrase in the Kur [xx. 40.], walituSonaEa EalaY EayoniY , (TA,) meaning (assumed tropical:) [ And this I did] that thou mightest be reared and nourished in my sight; (O, TA;) for which some read waloituSonaEo , as an imperative; and some, walitaSonaEa , meaning and that thou mightest work in my sight, (Ksh, Bd,) lest thou shouldst do so contrary to my command. (Bd.) You say likewise, of a woman, SanaEato nafosahaA : see 5. And you say also ↓ AiSoTanaEotuhu , meaning (tropical:) I reared him; and educated, disciplined, or trained, him well. (S, * O, K, TA.) -A2- Accord. to IDrst, SaniEa , inf. n. SanaEN , signifies He was, or became, skilled, or skilful: but IB says that SaniEa has not been heard. (TA.)

SanoEN and SanoEapN , (tropical:) I tended well my horse; or took good care of him; (S, O, K, TA;) supplied him with fodder, and fattened him: and SanaEa jaAriyatahu (tropical:) he reared, or nourished, his girl, or young woman: (TA:) and SuniEati AljaAriyapu (tropical:) the girl, or young woman, was treated [or nourished ] well, so that she became fat; as also ↓ Sun~iEat , inf. n. taSoniyEN : (K, TA:) or you say AiSonaEi Alfarasa , (so accord. to my MS. copy of the K,) or Alfarasa ↓ A^aSonaEa , (so accord. to other copies of the K, and in the O, [in the CK AuSoniEa Alfarasu ,]) without teshdeed; [which seems to indicate that the right reading is SanaEa , agreeably with the reading in my MS. copy of the K which gives the imperative form; though it is stated in the TA that A^aSonaEa Alfarasa is said by IKtt to be a dial. var. of SanaEahu ;] (O, K;) and AljaAriyapa ↓ San~aEa , with teshdeed, meaning he treated [or nourished ] well the girl, or young woman, and fattened her; (O, K; [in my MS. copy of the K San~iEi AljaAriyapa ;]) because the tSnyE of the girl, or young woman, is by means of many things, and by careful tending: (O, K:) so says Lth: (O:) but Az says that by other, or others, than Lth, it is allowed to say SanaEa jaAriyatahu , without teshdeed: and hence the phrase in the Kur [xx. 40.], walituSonaEa EalaY EayoniY , (TA,) meaning (assumed tropical:) [ And this I did] that thou mightest be reared and nourished in my sight; (O, TA;) for which some read waloituSonaEo , as an imperative; and some, walitaSonaEa , meaning and that thou mightest work in my sight, (Ksh, Bd,) lest thou shouldst do so contrary to my command. definition: primarily signifies The doing to one a thing in order that he may do another thing to the doer of the former thing.
sourceDefinition: primarily signifies The doing to one a thing in order that he may do another thing to the doer of the former thing. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (TA,) (assumed tropical:) The treating with gentleness, or blandishment; soothing, coaxing, wheedling, or cajoling; and endeavouring to conciliate. (O, K, TA.) And (assumed tropical:) He acted hypocritically with him. (TA.) And SAnEhu Eani Al$~aYo'i (assumed tropical:) He strove, or endeavoured, to turn him from the thing by deceit, or guile. (TA.) ― -b3- And hence, (A, TA,) or from the last signification in this paragraph, (TA,) (tropical:) The act of bribing. (S, O, Msb, * K, * TA.) (O, K, TA.)

definition: He (a man, O) aided, or assisted, another.
sourceDefinition: He (a man, O) aided, or assisted, another. (O, K.) And accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, followed in the O and TS and K, one says also, ASnE AlA^axoraqu , meaning The unskilful learned, and did soundly, thoroughly, skilfully, or well: but this is a mistake, occasioned by his deeming dubious, or obscure, a passage in the Nawádir of IAar, where the latter says that ASnE Alr~ajulu means A^aEaAna AlA^axoraqa [i. e.
