[A trad. of 'Omar, quoted below, presents another instance to which this signification is said to apply.] ― -b19- Or ka*aba denotes instigation, or incitement, of the person addressed, to keep to the thing that is mentioned; as in the saying of the Arabs, ka*aba Ealayoka AlEasalu , meaning Eat thou honey: but the explanation of this is, ( The relinquisher of ) honey hath erred [ to thee; i. e., in his representation of its evil qualites &c.; which is equivalent to saying, Eat, or keep to, honey ]: AlEasalu being put for taAriku AlEasali . [See also 1 in art. Esl .] In like manner, the saying of 'Omar, ka*aba Ealayokumu AlHaj~u &c., (see below,) signifies Keep ye to the performance of the pilgrimage, &c.: [or ( the relinquisher of ) the pilgrimage hath erred to thee in his representation of it: therefore it means as above]. (IAmb.) Accord. to IAmb the noun signifying the object of instigation [which may also be called the cause thereof] cannot be rightly put in the acc. case: if so put, the verb is without an agent. (TA.) [But see what is said on this point in the remarks on the trad. of 'Omar below.] ― -b20- Or the verb in a case of this kind signifies A^amokana : thus, ka*abaka AlHaj~u signifies The performance of the pilgrimage is possible, or practicable, to thee: therefore [it means] Perform thou the pilgrimage. (ISh.) ― -b21- Or A^amokana is its original signification; and the meaning intended is Keep to; as in the ex. ka*aba AlEatiyqu . (Aal.) ― -b22- 'Antarah, addressing his wife 'Ableh, says; or, accord. to some, the poet is Khuzaz Ibn-Lowdhán; ka*aba AlEatiyqu wamaA='u $an~K baAridN A_ino kunoti saAy^ilatiY gabuwqFA faA@*ohabiY (TA.) i. e., Keep thou to the eating of dates, and to the cool water of an old, worn-out, skin: if thou ask me for an evening's drink of milk, depart: for I have appropriated the milk to my colt, which is profitable to me, and may preserve me and thee: (L:) AlEtyq is in the nom. case accord. to the dial. of El-Yemen: but in the acc. accord. to that of Mudar. (TA.) ― -b23- Er-Radee [reading AlEtyqa ] cites this verse as a proof that ka*aba , originally a verb, has become a verbal noun, signifying Ailozamo . (TA.) But he is the only one who asserts it to be a verbal noun. (MF.) ― -b24- Also, Mo'akkir El-Bárikee says, wa*uboyaAniy~apK A^uwoSato baniyhaA biA^ano ka*aba AlqaraATifu waAlquruwfu And many a woman of Dhubyán charged her sons by [ saying ], Keep to the red garments ( Aksyp ), and the bags (or receptacles ) of leather tanned with pomegranate-bark. She charged them to take plenty of these two things as spoil from the tribe of Nemir, if they should prevail over them. (Aboo-'Obeyd El-Kásim Ibn-Selám.) ― -b25- k*b is also said to have the same meaning in the words of the trad. ka*aba Aln~as~aAbuwna [ Keep to those skilled in genealogy: ] or Regard is to be had to what is said by those skilled in genealogy: another meaning to which is assigned below. (TA.) ― -b26- It sometimes signifies It is incumbent, or obligatory. So in the following: (a trad. of 'Omar: TA:) ka*aba Ealayokumu AlHaj~u ka*aba Ealayokumu AlEumorapu ka*aba Ealayokumu AljihaAdu vlaAvapu A^asofaArK ka*abona Ealayokumo [ The performance of the pilgrimage is incumbent on you: the performance of ( the rites called ) AlEmrp is incumbent on you: warring ( for the sake of religion ) is incumbent on you: three expeditions are incumbent on you ]: (S, * K:) or k*b , here, is from ka*abatohu nafosuhu , “ his soul made him to desire things, and to conceive hopes, that could scarcely come to pass; ” and the meaning is let [ the expectation of the reward which will follow ] the performance of the pilgrimage render thee active, or brisk, and animate thee, instigate thee, or incite thee, to the act: [and so of the rest of the trad.: but here I should observe, that, for liyako*ibaka and liyuna$~iTaka and yaboEavaka , in the CK, we should read liyako*iboka &c.:] (K:) ― -b27- or, as ISk says, k*b , here, seems to denote instigation, or incitement, meaning Ealayokumo bihi keep ye to it; and is an extr. word with respect to analogy: (S:) ― -b28- accord. to Akh., AlHj~ is governed in the nom. case by k*b ; but as to the meaning, it is in the acc.; because the meaning is a command to perform the pilgrimage; as when you say, A^amokanaka AlS~ayodu [“ the game hath become within thy power, or reach ”], meaning “ shoot it, ” or “ cast at it: ” (S:) he who puts AlHj~ in the acc. case, [agreeably with one relation of the trad., TA,] makes Elyk [or Elykm ] a verbal noun; and in k*b is [implied] the pronoun which refers to AlHj~ [and which is the agent of the verb]; (K;) or the agent is implied in k*b , and explained by what follows it; (Sb;) [so that] the meaning is ka*aba AlHaj~u Ealayokumu AlHaj~a : (Z:) or, [as shown above,] k*b is a verbal n., meaning Alozamo , and AlHj~ is in the acc. case as governed by it: (Er-Radee:) though its being in the acc. case, accord. to some, is altogether unknown: (TA:) ― -b29- [or the meaning is as stated before on the authority of ISh.:] ― -b30- or the trad. means ka*aba Ealayoka AlHaj~u A_ino *ukira A^an~ahu gayoru kaAfK haAdimK limaA qabolahu mina Al*~unuwbi [( the relinguisher of ) the pilgrimage hath erred to thee if it have been spoken of (by him) as not sufficient, (and as not) abolishing the sins, or offences, (committed) before it: agreeably with the explanation by IAmb, given above]. (K.) ― -b31- ka*aba He said what was false unintentionally; committed a mistake, or error. The verb is used in this sense by the people of El-Hijáz, and the rest of the Arabs have followed them in so using it. (Towsheeh.) -A2- ka*aba is also said to signify He spoke truth; so as to bear two contr. meanings: and thus, ka*aba Aln~as~aAbuwna may signify Those skilled in genealogy have spoken truth: but another explanation of this saying is given in this art. (MF, &c.) -A3- ka*abato Eaf~aAqatuka [and the like] Thou brokest wind. (S in art. Efq .)

definition: , inf. n. tako*iybN , (and ki*~aAbN , TA, and tako*ibapN [like tajoribapN &c.], occurring in the TA, voce lahabapN , &c.) He made, or pronounced, him a liar; an utterer of falsehood; or a sayer of...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. tako*iybN , (and ki*~aAbN , TA, and tako*ibapN [like tajoribapN &c.], occurring in the TA, voce lahabapN , &c.) He made, or pronounced, him a liar; an utterer of falsehood; or a sayer of what was untrue: (K:) he attributed, or ascribed, to him lying, untruth, mendacity, or the speaking untruth: (Msb:) and (Msb) [ accused him of lying: ] he gave him the lie; said to him, “ Thou hast lied, ” &c. (S, Msb.) See also 4. ― -b2- k*~b biAlA^amori , inf. n. tako*iybN and ki*~aAbN (K: the latter inf. n. of the dial. of El-Yemen: Ks, Fr) and ki*aAbN , (TA,) He rejected, disallowed, denied, disacknowledged, disbelieved in, or discredited, the thing; syn. A^anokarahu ; (K;) as also k*~bhu , and ↓ ka*abahu . (Jel, liii. 11.) Ex. waka*~abuwA biA=yaAtinaA ki*~aAbFA [ And they rejected our signs, with rejection: Kur, lxxviii. 28]. (S.) And ka*~aba Alfuw^aAdu maA raA^aY , and ↓ ka*aba : see art. fA^d , and see 1. ― -b3- k*~b Eanohu (assumed tropical:) He repelled from him, [or defended him ]; syn. rad~a Eanohu ; namely, a man. (K.) [See exs. voce Ew~Y , in art. Ew .] -A2- Hamala famaA ka*~b , inf. n. tako*iybN , (tropical:) He charged, and was not cowardly, (S, K,) and did not retreat. (TA.) Hamala vum~a k*~b He charge, and then was cowardly, or did not charge with earnestness, or sincerity: (S:) ― -b2- or falsified the opinion formed of him: or made a false charge. (A.) k*~b Eana qironihi He charged, and then retreated from his adversary. (Sh.) k*~b AlqitaAla He was cowardly in fight. Alt~ako*iybu in fighting is the contr. of AlS~idoqu . (TA.) ― -b3- k*~b Als~ayora [ He slackened his pace, or became slow, after giving promise of being quick; ] he did not proceed in his journey with energy. (TA.) ― -b4- maA ka*~aba A^ano faEala ka*aA (so in the TA, and in a MS. copy of the K: in the CK, and in two copies of the S, maA ka*aba :) (tropical:) He did not delay to do so: (S, K:) he was not cowardly and weak, and did not delay to do so. (TA.) -A3- k*~b Eano A^amorK qado A^araAdahu (tropical:) He abstained, or desisted, or drew back by reason of fear, from a thing that he had desired to do. (K.) ― -b2- k*~b (and ↓ ka*aba , TA,) (assumed tropical:) He (a wild beast) took a run, and then stopped to see what was behind him, (K,) whether he were pursued or not. (TA.)

definition: He found him a liar;
sourceDefinition: He found him a liar; an utterer of falsehood; or a sayer of what was untrue: (S, K:) or he said to him, “ Thou hast lied ”: &c.: (TA:) or this verb bears the former of these two significations, and ↓ k*~bh signifies the latter: (S:) or Ak*bh signifies he shewed him that he had told a lie, &c.: (Zj:) or Ak*bh signifies he announced that he had told, or related, a lie, &c.: and ↓ k*~bh , he announced his being a liar, &c.: (Ks, S:) or Ak*bh and ↓ k*~bh are syn.: but the former sometimes signifies he incited, urged, or induced, him to lie, &c. (Th, S, * TA.) -A2- Ak*b , inf. n. A_iko*aAbN , (tropical:) He, being called to, or shouted to, remained silent, feigning to be asleep. (AA, K.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ A^uko*uwbapN [pl. A^akaA*iybu ] (S, K) and ↓ ku*obaY and ↓ mako*uwbN (K: this last a pass. part. n. used in the sense of an inf. n., as is said to be done in only four other instances: MF) and ↓ mako*uwbapN (S, K: a fem. pass. part. n. which is less used in this manner than a masc.: TA [or perhaps an inf. n., as its contr. maSoduwqapN is said to be:]) and ↓ mako*abapN (K: a meemee inf. n. agreeable with analogy: TA) and ↓ muko*ubapN (CK: omitted in a MS. copy, and in the TA) and ↓ kaA*ibapN (S, K) and ↓ ku*obaAnN and ↓ ku*~aAbN (K) and ↓ tako*aAbN (L, art. msH ,) are synonymous: (S, K) [all of these are regarded by some as inf. ns., signifying The act of lying; uttering a falsehood; or saying what is untrue: by others, all but the first seem to be regarded as simple substantives, signifying a lie; a falsehood; an untruth; a fiction; a fable: and the first, being an inf. n., is often used as a subst.] ― -b2- A_in~a baniY ↓ numayorK layosa lahumo mako*uwbapN [ Verily no lying, or lie, is attributable to the sons of Numeyr ] is related as a phrase of the Arabs. (S.) ― -b5- ↓ laA muko*abapa , and ↓ lA ku*obaY , and ↓ lA ku*obaAna , I do not accuse thee of lying; or make thee a liar: (TA:) [and in like manner] laA ku*oba laka , and lA ku*obaY laka , signify lA tako*iyba There is no accusing thee of lying; or making thee a liar. (Lb.) ― -b6- Al$~iEori ↓ takaA*iybu [ The lies of poetry ]. (TA.) ― -b7- jaAw^uwA EalaY qamiySihi bidamK ka*ibK , [Kur xii. 18, They brought, upon his shirt, false blood ]: k*b here means ↓ mako*uwbK : (Fr and Abu-l- 'Abbás:) or is for *iY ka*ibK , meaning mako*uwbK fiyhi : (Zj:) or the blood is termed k*b because he (Jacob) was told a lie thereby. definition: and Alka*uwbapu (tropical:) Names of the soul.
sourceDefinition: and Alka*uwbapu (tropical:) Names of the soul. (AZ, K.) See 1. ― -b2- Sadaqatohu Alkaduwbu , [ The soul ( i. e. his soul ) told him truth: ] the soul diverted him, or hindered him, or held him back, from an undertaking, causing him to imagine himself unable to prosecute it. (TA.)

(A, L.)

(of pauc., S) A^akomuw^N ; (S, K;) and [pl. of mult.] kamoA^apN : (K:) this last is not a pl. of km' , but a quasi-pl. n.: (Sb, K:) [or kamoA^apN is rather a coll. gen. n. of which the n. un. is without the p , contr. to analogy: (see jabo'N :)] in speaking of many, you say kamoA^apN , contr. to analogy: (S:) or kamoA^apN is the sing., and kamo'N pl.: or [accord. to some,] kamoA^apN is both sing. and pl.: (K:) AHn mentions kamoA^apN as sing., and kamoA^ataAni as dual, and kamoA=tN as pl.: but the right opinion is that of Sb. (TA.) [ kamoA^apN also signifies Any kind of fungus, such as the mushroom, and toadstool. See fuTorN .]

sourceDefinition: and ↓ laduwdN , (S, L, Msb, K,) the latter having an intensive sense, and ↓ lad~N , which is an inf. n. used as an epithet [and therefore also intensive], (Msb,) A man who overcomes in contention, or altercation; in dispute; in litigation: (S, * L, K: *) or, who opposes violently, or vehemently, and very violently, or vehemently, in contention, or altercation; in dispute; in litigation: (Msb:) and ↓ A^alad~u (S, L, Msb, K) and ↓ A^alanodadN and ↓ yalanodadN (S, L, K) a man violent, or vehement, in contention, or altercation; in dispute; in litigation: (S, L, Msb:) or difficult therein, and vehement in war: (IKtt:) or a contentious, disputatious, or litigious, (L,) and tenacious adversary, who will not incline to the truth: (L, K:) the fem. of ↓ A^lad~u is lad~aA='u : (L, Msb:) and the pl, lud~N (S, L, Msb, K) and lidaAdN : (L, K:) the A^ in ↓ A^alanodadN and the Y in ↓ yalanodadN are letters of quasi-coördination, [i. e., added to render those two words quasi-coordinate to safarojalN ,] as is shown by the two dáls being not incorporated by idghám; for it is allowable to add a letter at the beginning of a word for the purpose of quasi-coördination when the word has another augmentative letter: (IJ, L:) the dim. of ↓ A^alnodadN is ↓ A^ulayod~u , because it is originally A^alad~u , the n being added to render it quasi-coördinate to safarojalN . (S, L.) qawomFA lud~FA in the Kur, [xix. 97,] is said to signify A people who are adversaries perverted from the truth: or, who are deaf to the truth. (L.) You say also, huwa $adiydN ladiydN [assimilating the second epithet in form to the first, He is strong, and one who overcomes in contention, &c. ] (A.)

definition: , aor. , inf. n. masoHN ; and ↓ ms~Hhu , inf. n tamosiyHN ; He wiped a thing that was wet or dirty, with his hand, or passed his hand over it to remove the wet or dirt that was upon it: (L:) masoHN...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. masoHN ; and ↓ ms~Hhu , inf. n tamosiyHN ; He wiped a thing that was wet or dirty, with his hand, or passed his hand over it to remove the wet or dirt that was upon it: (L:) masoHN and tamosiyHN and ↓ tamas~uHN signifying the passing the hand over a thing that is flowing [ with water or the like ], or dirtied, soiled, or polluted, to remove the fluid or dirt, or soil or pollution; (L, K;) as when one wipes his head with his hand to remove water; and his forehead, to remove sweat. (L.) [It often signifies He stroked a thing with his hand; as, for instance, the Black Stone of the Kaabeh; see below.] ― -b2- masaHa raA^osahu mina AlmaA='i ; and jabiynahu Alr~a$aHi ; He wiped his head with his hand to remove the water that was upon it; and his forehead to remove the sweat. (L.) ― -b3- masaHa biraA^osihi (S) He wiped with his hand, or passed his hand closely over, his head, or a part thereof, without making any water to flow upon it: so in the Kur, v. 8; where it is said, faA@gosiluwA wujuwhakumo waA^ayodiyakumo A_ilaY A@lomaraAfiqi waA@mosaHuwA biruw^uwsikumo waA^arojulakumo A_ilaY A@lokaEobayoni : here A^arojulakumo is in the acc. case as an adjunct to Aydykm ; [i.e., as a third objective complement to the verb AgslwA ; not as an adjunct to rw^wskm ;] but some read A^arojulikumo , putting it in the gen. case because of its proximity to rw^wskm ; (Jel;) [in like manner as xaribK is put in the gen. case in the phrase h`*aA juHoru Dab~K xaribK , an ex. given by many of the grammarians, showing that this is allowable in prose,] notwithstanding that it is said, by Aboo-Is-hák the grammarian, that the putting a noun in the gen. case because of its proximity to a preceding noun in that case is not allowable except in poetry, when necessity requires it: (L:) the head, which is wiped, is mentioned between the arms and the feet, which are washed, to show the order which is to be observed in the purification. (Jel.) But masaHa signifies both he wiped with the hand, and also he washed: so says IAth: (L:) and AZ and IKt say the like: (Msb:) you say masaHotu yadaY~a bAlmaA='i , meaning I washed my hands with water. (AZ, Msb.) ― -b4- masaHa $ayoy^FA biAlmaA='i He wiped a thing with his hand wetted with water; passed his hand, wetted with water, over a thing. (Msb.) ― -b5- masaHa Albayot He compassed the House [ of God, i.e. the Kaabeh: because he who does so passes his hand over the corner in which is the Black Stone]. (L.) ― -b6- masaHa A@ll~`hu Eanoka maA bika May God remove that which is in thee! (L;) or, wash and cleanse thee from thy sins! (TA, art. mSH .) A prayer for a sick person. (L, from a trad.) ― -b7- masaHahu He anointed him or it with oil. (A.) ― -b8- musiHa biAlkarami , inf. n. masoHN , (tropical:) He was characterized by somewhat, or by some sign or mark, of nobility. (L.) [See masoHapN .] ― -b9- masaHa , inf. n. masoHN , He combed and dressed hair; syn. ma$aTa . (K.) ― -b10- masoHu All~uHiYa [ The stroking of the beards ] was a sign of reconciliation. (S, O, in art. Eq : see Eaqu biAls~ahomi .) ― -b11- masaHahu , or masaHahu biAlmaEoruwfi , i. e. bAlmErwf mina Alqawoli , (L,) inf. n. masoHN ; (L, K;) and ↓ ms~Hhu , (L,) inf. n. tamosiyHN ; (L, K;) He spoke to him good words, deceiving, or beguiling, him therein, (L, K,) and giving him nothing. (L.) ― -b12- fulaAnN yamosaHu raA^osa zayodK (tropical:) Such a one beguiles, or deceives, Zeyd. (A.) [See also 3.] ― -b13- masaHa , inf. n. masoHN and tamosaAHN He lied; uttered what was false. (K.) ― -b14- masaHa fiY AlA^aroDi , inf. n. musuwHN , He set forth journeying through the land, or earth: (A'Obeyd, K: *) as also maSaHa . (TA.) ― -b15- masaHahumo (tropical:) He passed lightly by them, or brushed by them, without remaining by them. (L.) ― -b16- masiHa , [aor. ,] inf. n. masaHN , The inner sides of his (a man's, S) thighs rubbed together, (S, L, K,) so as to become sore and chapped: (L:) or he had the inner side of his knee inflamed by the roughness of his garment. (L, K.) ― -b17- masaHa AlA_ibila , inf. n. masoHN (tropical:) He made the camels to journey all the day long: and he made the backs of the camels to be wounded by the saddles, and emaciated them; as also ↓ mas~aHahaA , inf. n. tamosiyHN : (K:) and in the latter sense you say masaHa Aln~aAqapa , and ↓ ms~HhA . (TA.) ― -b18- masaHati AlA_ibilu yawomahaA (tropical:) The camels journeyed all the day. (S.) masaHati AlA_ibilu AlA^aroDa yawomahaA daA^obFA (tropical:) The camels journeyed all the day laboriously. (TA.) -A2- masaHa , (S,) inf. n. masoHN (K) and misaAHapN , (S, K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) (tropical:) He measured land. (S, K.) -A3- masaHa , inf. n. masoHN , (tropical:) He cut, or severed: and he struck, or smote: (K:) he severed the neck, and the arm. (TA.) masaHa Eunuqahu and biEunuqihin , aor. , inf. n. masoHN , He smote his neck: or, as some say, severed it, or cut it through. Agreeably with both these significations masoHFA is rendered in the Kur, xxxviii. 32: some say that what is here meant is the wiping with the hand wetted with water: accord. to IAth, Solomon is here said to have smitten the necks and hock-tendons of the horses. (L.) [See art. Tfq .] masaHahu biAls~ayofi He smote him with the sword: (L:) and he cut him with the sword: (S, L:) or masaHahu signifies he struck him gently with a staff, or stick, and with a sword. (TA in art. dhn .) ― -b2- See 8. ― -b3- Also masaHahumo He slew them. (L.) -A4- masaHahu , (inf. n. masoHN , K,) He (God) created him blessed, (AHeyth, K,) and goodly: (AHeyth:) ― -b2- and, contr., created him accursed, (AHeyth, K,) and foul, or ugly. (AHeyth.) -A5- masaHa , (S,) inf. n. masoHN , (K,) (tropical:) Inivit feminam. (S, K.)

definition: Anointed: wiped over with some such thing as oil.
sourceDefinition: Anointed: wiped over with some such thing as oil. (K.) ― -b2- A king. (El-'Eynee.) ― -b3- AlmasiyHu [ The Messiah, the Christ, the Anointed, ] Jesus, on whom be peace ! (S, Msb, K,) [correctly] an arabicized word, [from the Hebrew,] originally ma$iyHaA , with $ : (T, Msb:) but the learned differ as to this word, whether it be Arabic or arabicized: F relates, in the K, his having mentioned, in his Expos. of the Meshárik el-Anwár, fifty opinions respecting the derivation of it; and in another work he has made the number fifty-six. (TA.) ― -b4- Also, (K,) or AlmasiyHu Alka*~aAbu , (S,) or ↓ Almis~iyHu , (K,) [ The Messiah, or Christ, surnamed the Great Liar; the False Christ; Antichrist; also called] EdDejjál, Ald~aj~aAlu : (S, K:) it is not allowable, however, to apply to him the appellation AlmasiyHu without restriction; wherefore one says AlmasiyHu Ald~aj~aAlu [or Alka*~aAbu ]; (TA;) [unless in a case like the following, in which] a poet says A_i*aA AlmasiyHu yaqotulu AlmasiyHa [ When the true Messiah shall slay the false Messiah ] (Msb.) [Many opinions respecting the derivation of the appellation thus applied are also mentioned by various authors.] ― -b5- masiyHN Sweat: (T, S, K:) so called because it is wiped off ( yumosaHu ) when it pours forth. (T.) ― -b6- masiyHN (tropical:) A dirhem [or silver coin] of which the impression is obliterated; syn. A^aTolasu ; (S, Msb, K;) having no impression. (Msb.) ― -b7- masiyHN (S, K) and ↓ masiyHapN (TA) A piece of silver. (As, S, K.) ― -b8- masiyHN . (tropical:) i. q. mamosuwHu Alwajohi , (K,) i.e., A man having one side of his face plain, without eye or eyebrow: said to apply in this sense to EdDejjál, among others. (IF, L.) ― -b9- One-eyed. (Az.) [See also A^amosaHu .] ― -b10- masiyHN A rough napkin, or kerchief, with which one wipes himself: (L, K:) so called because the face is wiped with it, or because it retains the dirt. (TA.) [A dusting-cloth, or dish-clout, or the like, is now called ↓ mimosaHapN .] ― -b11- masiyHN Beautiful in the face. (TA.) ― -b12- masiyHN One who journeys or goes about much for the sake of devotion, or as a devotee; as also ↓ mis~iyHN (K,) and ↓ A^amosaHu , (TA,) the fem. of which is masoHaA='u . (K, TA.) See mas~aAHN . -A2- masiyHN (tropical:) Multum coiens; as also ↓ maAsiHN . (K.) ― -b2- masiyHN Erring greatly. (TA.) ― -b3- masiyHN A great liar; one who lies much; as also ↓ maAsiHN and ↓ mimosaHN (K) and ↓ timosaHN (Lh, K) and ↓ A^amosaHu , (TA,) the fem. of which last is masoHaA='u . (K, TA.) See maAsiHN . -A3- masiyHN Very veracious; syn. Sid~iyqN : (K, L, TA: in the CK SadiyqN :) a meaning unknown to many of the lexicologists, and probably obsolete in their time. (L.) -A4- masiyHN Created blessed, and goodly; (L;) created ( mamosuwHN ) with blessing, or prosperity: (K:) ― -b2- and, contr., created accursed, and foul, or ugly; (L;) created with unfortunateness. (K.)

definition: A flat place, with small pebbles, and without plants, or herbage.
sourceDefinition: A flat place, with small pebbles, and without plants, or herbage. (S.) ― -b2- masoHaA='u A plain tract of land, with small pebbles, (S, K,) and without plants, or herbage: (S:) [ex.] mararotu bixariyqK mina AlA^aroDi biyona masoHaAwayoni [ I passed by a depressed tract of land containing herbage between two plain tracts containing small pebbles and without herbage ]: (Fr, S:) or a piece of flat ground, bare, abounding with pebbles, containing no trees nor herbage, rugged, somewhat hard, like a flat place in which camels &c. are confined, or in which dates are dried, not what is termed quf~ , nor what is termed saholap : (ISh:) pl. masaAHK and masaAHY [i. e. masaAHaY or masaAHiY~u ]; pl. forms proper to substs.; as it is an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates. (L.) ― -b3- Also masoHA='u Red land. (K.) ― -b4- masoHaA='u A woman having little flesh in her posteriors and thighs; or foul, ugly, or unseemly; syn. rasoHaA='u . (S.) [In the K., AlA^aroDu Alr~asoHaA='u , given as an explanation of AlmasoHaA='u , is an evident mistake for AlmaroA^apu Alr~asoHaA='u , as observed by Freytag.] ― -b5- A^amosaHu , or A^amosaHu Alqadami , A man having a flat sole to his foot, without any hollow: (L:) fem. masoHaA='u : (L, K:) and ↓ masiyHN , or Alqadamayoni ↓ masiyHu , signifies the same: and also having smooth and soft feet, without fissures or chaps, so that they repel water when it falls upon them. (L.) ― -b6- Also masoHaA='u , (K,) or msHA='u Alv~adoYi , (L,) A woman whose breast has no bulk. (L, K.) ― -b7- Also masoHaA='u A one-eyed woman: [see also masiyHN :] and such as is termed bixoqaA='u , whose eye is not mulaw~azap : so in [most of] the copies of the K., but in some, bil~aworap : (TA:) [the meaning seems to be whose eye has no crystalline humour ]. ― -b8- A^amosaHu A man having little flesh in his posteriors and thighs; or having small buttocks sticking together; syn. ArsH : fem. masoHaA='u : pl. musoHN . (L.) ― -b9- A^amosaHa A man (S) having the inner sides of his thighs rubbing together (S, L, K) so as to become sore and chapped: (L:) or having the inner side of his knee inflamed by the roughness of his garment: (L, K:) fem. masoHaA='u , and pl. musoHN . (L.) ― -b10- gaArapN masoHaA='u (tropical:) A hostile attack, or incursion, by a troop of horse, in which the attacking party passes lightly by the party attacked, or brushes by them, without remaining by them. (L, from a trad.) ― -b11- See masiyHN .

definition: A loan, or lending, of a she-camel or sheep or goat, that the person to whom the loan is granted may milk her for a certain period and then restore her to the lender: (A'Obeyd:) [and in like manner,] ↓ maniyHapN a gift ( minoHap ) of milk;
sourceDefinition: A loan, or lending, of a she-camel or sheep or goat, that the person to whom the loan is granted may milk her for a certain period and then restore her to the lender: (A'Obeyd:) [and in like manner,] ↓ maniyHapN a gift ( minoHap ) of milk; as a she-camel or sheep or goat that is given to another that he may milk her and afterwards restore her to the lender: (S:) or minoHapN signifies a ewe or a she-goat or a she-camel, which her owner lends to a man that he may drink her milk and restore her when her milk ceases to flow: (Msb:) or both words signify a she-camel or sheep or goat whose milk is given to another: (A:) or a she-camel of which the soft hair ( wabar ) and milk and offspring are conceded by the owner to another: (K:) or ↓ maniyHapN signifies a she-camel or sheep or goat that is lent for the sake of her milk [ &c. ]; and minoHapN , the profit which the lender thereof bestows upon the borrower. (Lh, L.) The Arabs have four words which they use in the place of EaAriy~apN , viz. ↓ maniyHapN , Eariy~apN , A_ifoqaArN , and A_ixobaAlN . (A'Obeyd, S.) ― -b2- minoHapN mino layanK Milch sheep or goats; (L;) [app. meaning, that are lent to a person ]. ― -b3- Also minoHapN A loan of land, and of money. (L.) ― -b4- Also, A gift, or thing given; (S, L, K;) as also ↓ maniyHapN : (TA:) a free gift: (A'Obeyd, L:) pl. minaHN ; (A;) and pl. of maniyHapN , manaAy^iHu . (TA.)

definition: An arrow ( of those used in the game called Almayosir , S) which has no lot, or portion, (S, K,) unless the person to whom it pertains be given something: (S:) it is the third of the arrows to which...
sourceDefinition: An arrow ( of those used in the game called Almayosir , S) which has no lot, or portion, (S, K,) unless the person to whom it pertains be given something: (S:) it is the third of the arrows to which the term gufolN is applied, which have no notches, and to which is assigned no portion and no fine; these being only added to give additional weight to the collection of arrows from fear of occasioning suspicion [of foul play]: it is one of four arrows to each of which is assigned no portion and no fine; the first is called AlmuSad~aru ; the next, AlmuDaE~afa ; the next, AlmnyH ; and the last, Als~afiyHu : (Lh:) accord. to some, (TA,) an arrow that is borrowed because it is regarded as fortunate: (K, TA:) or an arrow which has a portion assigned to it. (K.) ― -b2- kunotu maniyHa A^aSoHaAbiY yawoma badorK (assumed tropical:) I was, among my companions, like the arrow called AlmnyH , on the day of the battle of Bedr; i. e., by reason of my youth, I was like the arrow that neither gains nor loses. (L, from a trad.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. nabo*N , (S, L, Msb, K,) He cast, threw, or flung, it away, as a thing esteemed of no account or importance: this is the original signification; and in this sense it is mostly used in the Kur-án: (Er-Rághib:) he cast, threw, or flung, it (S, A, L, Msb. K) from his hand, (S, L,) before him or behind him: (L, K:) and he cast, threw, or flung, it far away, or to a distance: (L:) and (so in the L; but in the K, or) he cast, threw, or flung it in any manner: (L, K:) ↓ nb~* has teshdeed given to it to denote frequency, or repetition, of the action, or its application to many objects. (S, A, L.) ― -b2- naba*a xaAtamahu He threw his signet from his hand. (L, from a trad.) ― -b3- fanaba*uwhu waraA='a Zuhuwrihimo (Kur, iii. 184) (tropical:) [lit., And they cast it behind their backs; ] means and they did not observe it; (namely, their covenant;) they disregarded it. (Beyd.) ― -b4- nabo*N is both by act and by word; having for its objects both substances and accidents: (L:) you say naba*a AlEahoda (tropical:) He dissolved the league, or covenant, and cast it from him to him with whom he had made it: (A, L, Msb: *) and naba*a kul~u fariyqK minohumaA A_ilaY SaAHbh AlEahoda Al~a*iY tahaAdanaA Ealayohi (tropical:) [ Each party of them cast from him, to the other, the league, or covenant, by which they had made a truce; i. e., each party of them rejected it, or renounced it, to the other ]: (T:) and naba*a A_ilaY AlEaduw~i , and ↓ nAb*hu , (tropical:) He cast from him the league, or covenant, to the enemy, and dissolved it: and ↓ tanaAba*uwA (tropical:) They mutually cast from themselves the league, or covenant, and dissolved it. (A.) See also 3. ― -b5- naba*a A^amoriY waraA='i Zahorihi (tropical:) [lit., He cast my affair behind his back; meaning,] he did not perform my affair; (A;) he neglected it. (Msb.) ― -b6- naba*ato fulaAnapu qawolFA maliyHFA (tropical:) Such a woman threw out a goodly, beautiful, or pretty, saying. (A.) ― -b7- naba*otu A_iloyhi Als~alaAma , and Alt~aHiy~apa , (tropical:) I threw to him the salutation. (A.) ― -b8- nubi*otu bika*aA (tropical:) [ I had such a thing as it were thrown to me; I had it thrown in my way; ] I had it offered, or presented, to me, the meeting with it being appointed, or prepared; as also rumiytu bihi . (A.) ― -b9- lil~`hi A^um~N naba*ato bika (tropical:) To God ( be attributed the excellence of ) the mother that brought thee forth! ] (A.) ― -b10- naba*a He threw forth earth or dust [in digging a hole &c.]; as also nabava . (A.) See also nabiy*apN . ― -b11- naba*a He threw dates or raisins into a bag or skin, and poured water upon them, and left the liquor until it fermented and became intoxicating: (T:) [or, simply, he steeped dates or raisins in water; for the beverage thus made, called nabay* , was not always left until it became intoxicating, as is shown by several trads.] ― -b12- naba*a nabiy*FA , (S, L, K, &c.,) the most usual form of the verb, (Kz,) aor. , only; (MF;) and ↓ nb~*hu , (A, L, K,) and ↓ Anb*hu , (L, K,) a form used by the vulgar, (S, IDrst,) and rejected by Th and others, but mentioned, on the authority of Er-Ruásee, by Fr, who says that he had not heard it from the Arabs, but that the authority of its transmitter is worthy of reliance, (TA,) and ↓ Antb*hu ; (L, K;) (tropical:) He made beverage of the kind called nabiy* . (S, A, L, K.) ― -b13- Also, naba*a tamorFA , (Lh, IAth, L,) and EinabFA , (IAth, L,) and ↓ Anb*hu , but this is seldom used, (Kutr, Lh, ISk, and others, and L,) and ↓ Antb*hu , (L,) (tropical:) He made, of the dates, and of the grapes, beverage of the kind called nabiy* ; (Lh, L;) he left the dates, and the grapes, in water, that it might become beverage of the kind so called. definition: , inf. n. munaAba*apN , He bargained with him by saying, Throw thou to me the garment, or piece of cloth, (A'Obeyd, L, K,) or other article of merchandise, (A'Obeyd, L,) or I will throw it to thee,...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. munaAba*apN , He bargained with him by saying, Throw thou to me the garment, or piece of cloth, (A'Obeyd, L, K,) or other article of merchandise, (A'Obeyd, L,) or I will throw it to thee, and the sale shall become binding, or settled, or concluded, for such a sum: (A' Obeyd, L, K:) or, by throwing to another a garment, or piece of cloth, the other doing the like: (Lh, L, K:) or, by saying, When thou throwest thy commodity, or when I throw my commodity, the sale is binding, or settled, or concluded, for such a sum: (Msb:) or, by saying, When I throw it to thee, or when thou throwest it to me, the sale is binding, or settled, or concluded: (Mgh, art. lms :) or, by saying, When I throw the pebble (L, K) to thee, (L,) the sale is binding, or settled, or concluded: (L, K:) or by another's throwing a pebble to him: (L:) bayoEu AlmunaAba*api and bayoEu AlHaSaApi and bayoEu A_iloqaA='i AlHajari signify the same; (Mgh;) as also bayoEu AlA_iloqaA='i : (A:) such bargaining is forbidden. (L.) ― -b2- nAb*wA , inf. n. munaAba*apN ; and ↓ Antb*wA ; (tropical:) They retired, each of the two parties, apart, in war. (L, K.) ― -b3- naAba*ahumu AlHaroba , and A_ilayohimu AlHaroba ↓ naba*a , He retired from them to a place aside, or apart, in war, for a just purpose, ( liloHaq~i , in the 'Eyn for war, liloHarobi , TT,) they doing the like: (Lth, T, L:) or these two phrases, followed by EalaY sawaA='K , are used when there is between two parties at variance a covenant, or league, or a truce, after fighting, and they desire to dissolve the league, or covenant, and each party casts it from him ( yanobi*uhu ) to the other: thus, faA@nobi*o A_ilayohimo EalaY sawaA='K , in the Kur, [viii. 60, lit., cast thou from thee, to them, their league, or covenant, in an equitable, or just, manner, ] means, announce thou to them that thou hast dissolved the league between thee and them, so that they may have equal knowledge with thee of the dissolving thereof and of the returning to war: (T, L:) ElY swA' here signifies ElY AlHaq~i waAlEadoli : (Lh:) naAba*ahu AlHaroba also signifies he made war with him openly; (S, L, Msb;) and is syn. with naba*a A_ilayohi AlHaroba : (L:) and naAba*uwhumo EalaY sawaA='K they made war with them openly, in an equitable manner, declaring their hostile intention, so that it was equally known to their enemies and themselves. (L.) See also 1. ― -b4- naAba*otuhumo (tropical:) I acted contrarily to, or differently from, or adversely to, them; or was, or became, contrary to, or different from, or adverse to, them; syn. xaAlafotuhumo . (Msb.)

definition: Cast, thrown, or flung, [ &c.
sourceDefinition: Cast, thrown, or flung, [ &c.; see 1;] (K;) i. q. manobuw*N . (L.) But see below. ― -b2- ↓ nabiy*apN The earth or dust that is thrown forth from a hole or the like that is dug; as also nabiyvapN : pl. nabaAy^i*N . (A, * L.) Yaakoob asserts, that the * is a substitute for v . (L.) ― -b3- nabiy*N (tropical:) A kind of beverage, made of dates, and of raisins; i. e., must; and of honey; i. e., mead; and of wheat, and of barley, &c.; i. e. wort: (L:) or made of dates, or of raisins, which one throws ( yanobi*u , i. e. yaToraH , whence its appellation,) into a vessel or skin of water, and leaves until it ferments ( yafuwr , T, L, or yagoliY , Mgh) and becomes intoxicating, or not so long as to become intoxicating: before it has become so, it is a lawful beverage: (T, L:) whether intoxicating or not, it is thus called: (L:) or it is thus called because it is left ( yunoba*u , i. e., yutoraku ,) until it becomes strong; (Msb;) being expressed juice, or the like, that is left ( nubi*a ) [ for a time to acquire strength ]: (L, K:) it is said that this word is originally of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , but that it has become obsolete in this latter sense, and, applied to the beverage, is used as though it were a primitive substantive, as is shown by the form of its pl., (M, F,) which is A^anobi*apN ; (S, L, MF;) for a word of the measure fEyl in the sense of the measure mfEwl has not this form of pl.: (MF:) wine expressed from grapes is also called nabiy*N , like as nby* is also called xamorN : [ nabiy*N is a coll. gen. n., and its n. un. is with p :] nabiy*apN signifies some nabiy* ; lit., a portion thereof. (Msb, art. xmr .) See also mizorN . (L.)

definition: or ↓ nux~apN or ↓ nix~apN , as occurring in the following words of a trad.
sourceDefinition: or ↓ nux~apN or ↓ nix~apN , as occurring in the following words of a trad., layosa fiY Alnx~pi SadaqapN , [ No alms are required by the law in the case of ....,] is variously explained. (TA.) It is said that nax~apN signifies Slaves, (AO, Az, S, K,) men and women: (AO, Az:) also, a [single] male slave: (ISh:) also, working bulls or cows; (S, K;) and so nux~apN : (K:) Th says that this is the correct meaning, because it is from nax~N , signifying the “ act of driving vehemently; ” and Ks says that this is its meaning, but that it is only nux~apN , with damm: (S:) also, asses, HumurN , [in the CK, xamorN ,] (IAar, L, K,) collectively; (L;) and so nux~apN (L, K) and nix~apN : (K:) also, [ animals ] reared in houses or tents: (K:) also, whatever are employed in labour, of camels, and bulls or cows, and asses, and slaves; as also nux~apN : (Aboo-Sa'eed:) also, pastors; and so nux~apN : also, drivers, leaders, or attendants, of camels: (K:) also, the taking of a deenár for himself by the collector of the alms required by the law, called Sadaqap , (S, K,) after he has finished receiving those alms: (S:) also, the deenár itself so taken is thus called. (K.) In all these senses the word nx~p is explained in the above trad. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , or EalaY AlA^aroDi , (TA,) inf. n. nayorabapN , (TA,) The wind lays the dust upon it, or upon the ground, in cross, wavy lines: syn. tanosijuhu . (K.) Hence nayoraba AlkalaAm . (TA.) ― -b2- It has been asserted that n and r do not come together in any [pure] Arabic word; and F has said the same in art. nr$ ; [or rather he has there said that r does not occur in an Arabic word with n before it; (meaning a radical n ;)] yet he has here mentioned this word as though it were pure Arabic. So says MF. To this it may be replied, that Y is inserted to separate the n and r , as remarked in the L. (TA.) ― -b3- nayoraba He forged [speech, or language]: syn. nasaja . (K.) You say huwa yunayoribu Alqawola . (TA.) ― -b4- nayoraba He mixed, or confounded, speech, [ introducing what was false with that which was true ]. (K.) ― -b5- nayoraba He uttered a malicious and mischievous misrepresentation, a calumny, or slander. (K.)

definition: , of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , (S,) A month which the Arabs, in the time of paganism, postponed: (K:) the doing of which is forbidden in the Kur, ix.
sourceDefinition: , of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , (S,) A month which the Arabs, in the time of paganism, postponed: (K:) the doing of which is forbidden in the Kur, ix. 37. (S.) ― -b2- Also, as an inf. n. of nasaA^a , (which it is also said to be in the L,) The postponing of a month: i. e., the postponing of the sacredness of a month; transferring it to another month. When the Arabs returned from Mina, [after the accomplishment of the pilgrimage,] it was customary for a man of the tribe of Kináneh to arise and say, A^anaA Al~a*iY laA yurad~u liY qaDaA='N [“ I am he whose decree is not to be rejected ”]; (S;) or A_in~iY laA A^uHaAbu walaA A^uEaAbu walaA yurad~u qawoliY , or wlA yrd~ maA qaDayotu bihi ; [“ Verily I am not to be accused of a sin, nor am I to be charged with a fault, nor is my saying, (or decree,) to be rejected; ”] (TA;) whereupon they would say, A^anosiy^onaA $ahorFA [“ Postpone for us a month ”]; i. e., “ Postpone for us the sacredness of El-Mo- harram, and transfer it to Safar: ” for they disliked that three months during which they might not make predatory expeditions should come upon them consecutively, as their subsistence was obtained by such expeditions: so he made ElMoharram free from restriction to them. (S.) [But this, as appears from what is said in the Kur, ix. 37, was not done every year.] The tribes of Teiyi and Khath'am did not observe the sacred months; therefore the naAsiy^ (or postponer) proclaimed it lawful to slay them therein, when they were aggressors. (TA.) ― -b3- [The term nasiYo' appears also to have been applied to The postponement of the time of the pilgrimage; which was another custom of the Pagan Arabs, mentioned under this word in the TA.] The Arabs, liking that the day of their return from pilgrimage should always be at one season of the year, postponed it every year eleven days; at the same time keeping sacred the two months in which the pilgrimage took place, and the month next after those two, and also the month of Rejeb, at whatever season this fell. (TA.) [For the same purpose, at one time, they used to intercalate a month in the third and sixth and eight of every eight years. See Kur, ix. 36, where the prohibition of this custom is implied; and Sale's Prel. Disc., § vii.]. ― -b4- See naso'N . ― -b5- nasiYo'N (K, TA) and ↓ nasiyoy^apN and ↓ nusoA^apN , (S, K,) like kuloA^apN , (S,) A postponement, or delay, as to the time of the payment of a debt, or of the price of a thing sold, &c. (S, K, TA.) The first is a subst.; (K;) and also an inf. n.; (L;) [and each of the others seems to be sometimes used as such]. ― -b6- ↓ baAEahu binasiyoy^apK , and ↓ binusoA^apK , (as also bikuloA^apK , S,) He sold it on credit; for payment to be made at a future period. (S, K, TA.)

definition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, M, and so in a copy of the B by the author of the K,) or , (A, K,) [the latter being agreeable with analogy,] inf. n. nuEaAsN , (S, A, K, * TA,) or this is a simple subst., (Msb,) [ He drowsed; he was, or became, drowsy, or heavy with sleepiness: or he slumbered, or dozed: ] the inf. n. is syn. with wasanN : (S, A, K:) or ↓ nuEaAsN signifies languor in the senses, (K, TA,) arising from the heaviness [ which is the prevenient sign ] of sleep: (TA:) or the beginning of sleep: (M, art. wsn :) or its proper signification is, accord. to Az, (Msb, TA,) wasanN (Msb) or sinapN (TA) without sleep: (Msb, TA,) or sinapN is in the head, and nuEaAsN is in the eye: or snp is the vapour ( ryH ) of sleep which begins in the face, then is transmitted to the heart, and you say, of a man, yanoEasu , and then, yanaAmu . definition: A diacritical point of a letter or word: a syllabical point thereof: see 1:] (K:) [ a point, dot, speck, speckle, or small spot: a mathematical point;
sourceDefinition: A diacritical point of a letter or word: a syllabical point thereof: see 1:] (K:) [ a point, dot, speck, speckle, or small spot: a mathematical point; i. e.] the extremity of a line: (TA:) pl. nuqaTN (S, Msb, K,) and niqaATN . (AZ, S, K.) Hence, one says, maA A@xotalafaA fY nuqoTapK They two did not differ respecting so small a thing as a point of a letter or word. (TA.) And [hence] the vulgar say, when they admire one, huwa nuqoTapN fiY muSoHafK (assumed tropical:) [ He is like a point, or stop, in a copy of the Kur-án; because the stops in the Kur-án are generally ornamented, and often very beautifully, with gold and colours]. (TA.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) [ Any very small thing, that may be likened to a point, dot, or speck. Hence,] 'Alee is related to have said, AlEilomu nuqoTapN A_in~amaA kat~arahaA AljaAhiluwna (assumed tropical:) [ Science, or knowledge, is a very small thing: only the ignorant have made it to be much ]. (TA.) And you say, A^aEoTaAhu nuqoTapF mino EasalK (tropical:) [ He gave him a drop, or very small quantity, of honey ]. (TA.) ― -b3- (tropical:) [ A portion of a thing, or some of a number of things, in a separate, or scattered, state, here and there ] You say, maA baqiYa mino A^amowaAlihimo A_il~aA nuqoTapa (tropical:) There remained not of their possessions [aught] save some palm-trees and a portion of seed-produce here and there. (IAar, TA) And fiY AlA^aroDi niqaATN mina AlkalaA_i , and nuqaTN minohu . (tropical:) In the land are scattered spots, or portions, of herbage. (K, * TA.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) A thing: an affair; a matter: a case; an event; an action. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: The facing, or outer covering, ( ZihaArap ,) of a bed (T, Mgh, K) upon which one sleeps, (Mgh,) or of a thing that is spread upon the ground to sit or lie upon, (T, K,) whatever it be: (K:) or a sort of carpet or other thing that is spread upon the ground: (S, K:) and a woollen cloth (Mgh, Msb, K) which is thrown over the [ kind of vehicle called ] hawodaj , (Mgh, K,) having a fine nap, or pile, (TA,) of some colour; what is white being seldom or never so called: (Msb:) or a sort of dyed cloth, like zawojN , these names being seldom or never applied but to what is coloured red or green or yellow; what is white not being called namaTN : (Az, L:) and a cloth that is spread beneath a horse's saddle: (Meyd, as cited by Golius:) some say, that it is a receptacle like the safaT : (Har, p. 273 [but this I think doubtful:] pl. A^anomaATN [properly a pl. of pauc. but used also as one of mult.] (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and nimaATN . (IB, K.) -A2- A body of men (S, Mgh, Msb, K) whose case is one; i. e. a class of men. (S, K.) It is said in a trad., (S, Mgh,) of 'Alee, (Mgh,) xayoru h`*ihi AlA^um~api Aln~amaTu AlA^awosaTu The best of this people is the middle body thereof (S, Mgh) whose case is one; i. e. the middle class thereof: (S, in which is added, yuloHaqu bihimu Alt~aAliY wayurojaEu A_ilayohimu AlgaAliY [ he who falls short shall be made to reach them, and he who exceeds the due bounds shall be brought back to them: ]) A 'Obeyd says, (Mgh, TA,) the meaning of this saying of 'Alee is, (TA,) that he disliked the exceeding of the due bounds and the falling short (Mgh, TA) in religion. (TA.) -A3- A way: (Msb, TA:) a way, course, mode, or manner, of acting, conduct, or the like; (Mgh, K;) as also ↓ AnmT : (TA [so there written, without any syll. points:]) a tenet, or body of tenets, belief, creed, opinion, or persuasion, which one takes to, or holds: (Mgh, TA:) a kind, or way, of speech. (TA.) You say, A_ilozamo h`*aA Aln~maTa keep thou to this way. (TA.) And takal~amuwA EalaY namaTK waAHidK They spoke according to one way, course, mode, or manner, &c. (Mgh.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A sort, or species, (Mgh, Msb, K,) of a thing, (K,) of goods or commodities, of learning or. science, &c. (TA.) You say, EinodiY mataAEN mino h`*aA Aln~amaTi (tropical:) I have goods of this sort, or species. (Mgh.) And h`*aA mino namaTi h`*aA (tropical:) This is of the sort, or species, of this. (Msb.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaTaA^u ; (S, K;) the w , falls out from the aor. of this verb, and from that of wasiEa , because they are transitive; for other verbs of the class faEila , having the aor. of the measure yafoEalu , and the first radical letter infirm, are intransitive; and as these two differ from their class in being transitive, they are also made to differ in the aor.; (S;) or yaTaA^u was originally yaTiy^u , and therefore the w , falls out from it; (TA;) inf. n. waTo'N , (TA) [and Tiy^apN , q.v. infra]; and ↓ wT~A^ , (K, but this has an intensive signification, MF;) and ↓ twT~A^ (S, K) He trod; trod upon; ( birijolihi with his foot; S) trod under foot; trampled upon: (S, K, TA:) or waTiy^ahu signifies he pressed, or bore, upon him, or it, with his hand or his foot. (TA, in art. vTA^ .) [See also waToA^apN .] ― -b2- Th , at the commencement of the 20th ch. of the Kur, is read by some Taho , and said to be for TaA^o , (the h being substituted for ' ,) and to signify Tread upon the ground with the soles of both thy fect; because Mohammad raised one of his feet in prayer. (TA.) ― -b3- humo yaTaw^uhumu AlT~ariyqu (tropical:) They (i. e. the sons of such a one) sojourn, or encamp, near the road, so that its passengers tread upon them [ i. e., became their guests ]: (Sb, K:) a tropical phrase, in which AlTryq is put for A^aholu AlT~ariyqi ; this being done to give greater force to the phrase, as it is one expressive of praise; for the road is a thing that is constant; whereas its passengers are sometimes upon it, and sometimes absent. (L.) [It means They are a people who take up their abode near the road in order that many passengers may enjoy their hospitality. ] ― -b4- [See also TariyqN .] ― -b5- Of the same kind is the phrase A^axa*onaA EalaY AlT~ariyqi AlwaATiy^i libaniY fulaAnK (tropical:) [ We look to the road whose passengers tread on ( i. e., make themselves the guests of, ) the sons of such a one ]. (IJ.) ― -b6- So too, mararonaA biqawomK mawoTuwy^iyna biAlT~ariyqi (tropical:) [ We passed by a people trod on ( i. e., resorted to for their hospitality, ) by the passengers of the road ]. (IJ.) ― -b7- Also, yaA Tariyqu TaA^o binaA baniY fulaAnK (tropical:) O road, bring us near to [or, lit., make us to tread on, i. e., make us the guests of, ] the sons of such a one ! (IJ.) ― -b8- waTiy^a , (S, K,) aor, as above, (S,) Inivit feminam. (S, K.) ― -b9- waTaA^a , inf. n. Tiy^apN , (assumed tropical:) He trod under foot, and despised. Ex. naEuw*u biAll~`hi mino Tiy^api Al*~aliyli We put our trust in God for protection from the vile person's treading us under foot, and despising us. (Lh.) ― -b10- waTaA^a and ↓ wT~A^ (in MF's copy of the K wATA^ ) He prepared, and made plain, smooth, or soft. (K.) ― -b11- waTayotu ; for waTaA^otu , is disallowed. (TA.) ― -b12- waTuw^a , aor. yawoTuw^u , inf. n. wTA^ , [so in the TA: probably a mistake for waTaA='apN : see Tiy^apN below:] He (a horse &c.) was, or became, easy to ride upon. (TA.) ― -b13- waTuw^a , aor. yawoTuw^u , inf. n. waTaA='apN (S, K) and wuTuwo'apN (TA) and TaA^apN (TA, as from the K) [and, app., Tiy^apN , q.v. infra], It (a place, S) was plain, level, smooth, soft, or easy to be travelled, or to walk, or ride or lie upon. (S, K, TA.) -A2- kunotu A^aTaA^u *ikorahu (assumed tropical:) I used to conceal the mention of him, or it. (TA, from a trad.)

definition: He made another to tread, or trample, upon him.
sourceDefinition: He made another to tread, or trample, upon him. (TA.) ― -b2- AwTA^h farasahu He made his horse to tread, or trample, upon him. (K, TA.) ― -b3- AwTA^hu AlA^rDa He made him to tread upon the ground. (Msb.) ― -b4- A^awoTaw^uwhumo (assumed tropical:) They overcame them, or prevailed over them, in a contention, or dispute. (TA.) ― -b5- In a trad. it is said, that the pastors of the camels, and the shepherds, boasted, one party over the other, and the former overcame the latter ( AwTw^whm ). (TA.) The verb is used in this sense because it originally signifies, with the annexed pronoun, they made (others) to tread, or trample, upon them: (K, TA:) for him with whom you wrestle or fight, and whom you throw down, you trample upon, and make to be trampled upon by others. (TA.) ― -b6- AwTA^hu AlEa$owapa , (K,) and Ea$owapF , (S, K,) He made him to pursue a course without being rightly directed. (K *, TA.) See art. E$w . ― -b7- AwTA^ fiY Al$~iEori , (S, K,) inf. n. A_iyT~A='N ; (TA;) and AwTA^ Al$~iEora , and fiyhi ↓ wATA^ , and ↓ wT~A^hu , and A^aT~aA^ahu , and A=TaA^ahu , (K,) in which last the w is changed into A ; (TA;) He repeated a rhyme in a poem, (S, K,) using the same word in the same sense: (Akh, K:) when the word is the same, but the meaning different, the repetition is not called AyTA' [but jinaAsN taAm~N ]. (TA.) This repetition ( AyTA' ) is deemed by Arabs a fault: or it is only deemed a fault if it occur two, or three, or more, times. (TA.)

definition: A certain kind of food, (S,) i.
sourceDefinition: A certain kind of food, (S,) i. q. HayosapN : (IAar:) or dates of which the stones are taken out, and which are kneaded with milk: or what is called A^aqiT , with sugar: (K:) or a food of the Arabs, prepared with dates, which are put into a stone cooking-pot; then water is poured upon them, and clarified butter if there be any; ( but no AqT is mixed up with them; ) and then it is drunk, like Hysp : (T:) or it is like jayos ; dates and AqT kneaded together with clarified butter: (ISh:) or a certain kind of food, also called waTiYo'N ; a thin EaSiydap : when it is thickened, it is called nafiytap ; when a little more thick, nafiyvap ; when a little thicker, lafiytap ; and when so thick that it may be chewed, ESydp . (El-Muffaddal.) ― -b2- Also, (as some say, TA,) A thing like [ the kind of sack called ] a giraArap : (S:) or a grArp containing dried meat ( qadiyd ) and kaEok (K) and other things: (TA:) ― -b3- A^axorijo A_ilayonaA valaAva A^ukalK mino wTyy^pK Take forth and give us three cakes of bread from a grArp . (S, TA, from a trad.) ― -b4- [See also waATiy^ap and muwaT~aA^N .]

definition: He [ undertook a thing, or an affair, as imposed upon him: or] took, or imposed, upon himself, or undertook, a thing, or an affair, [ as a task, or] in spite of difficulty, trouble, or inconvenience;
sourceDefinition: He [ undertook a thing, or an affair, as imposed upon him: or] took, or imposed, upon himself, or undertook, a thing, or an affair, [ as a task, or] in spite of difficulty, trouble, or inconvenience; (Msb;) syn. tajat~amahu : (S, K:) he constrained, or tasked, or exerted, himself, or took pains, or made an effort, to do a thing; meaning, a thing that was difficult, troublesome, or inconvenient, to him: or he affected, as a self-imposed task, the doing of a thing. (The Lexicons, passim: see tgz~l : and see kal~afahu A^amorFA .) ― -b2- tkl~f SifapF He affected, or endeavoured to acquire, a quality. So in the explanations of verbs of the measure tafaE~ala ; as naHal~ama . (Sharh El-'Izzee, by Saad-ed-Keen.) ― -b3- Also, He affected, or pretended to have, a quality, not having it. So in the explanations of verbs of the measure tafaAEala , as tajaAhala : (idem:) [and sometimes in verbs of the measure tafaE~ala also, as takas~ara &c.]. And takal~afa alone, He exercised self-constraint, or put himself to trouble or inconvenience. ― -b4- takal~afa He affected what was not natural to him. ― -b5- takal~afa He used forced efforts to do a thing, and to appear to have a quality. He affected, or endeavoured to do or acquire, &c.; he constrained himself to do, &c.; he applied himself, as to a task, to do a thing. tkl~f Al$~ajaAEapa He made himself, or constrained himself to be, courageous; affected, or endeavoured to acquire, or characterize himself by, courage. ― -b6- tkl~f Al$~ajaAEapa also, He acted, or behaved, with forced courage; endeavoured to be courageous. ― -b7- tkl~f fiY Earabiy~atihi He used a forced, or affected, manner in his Arabic speech. ― -b8- takal~ufN A straining of a point in lexicology. ― -b9- taEaq~ala signifies He affected or endeavoured to acquire, intelligence; explained by tkl~f AlEaqola : and taEaAqala , he pretended to be intelligent, not being really so. (S, art. Eql .) takal~ufN in a verb of the measure tafaE~ala is as above explained, signifying a desire for the existence of an attribute in one's self: in a verb of the measure tafaAEala it is different, and means the pretending to be or to do something which in reality one is not or does not; as in the instance of tajaAhala , he pretended to be ignorant, not being so in reality. (Sharh El-'Izzee, by Saad-ed-Deen.) takal~afa ka*aA He did so purposely. ― -b10- takal~afa He tasked himself. ― -b11- takal~afa AlqaYo'a He vomited intentionally. (TA, art. qY' .)
